Employees shall notify their immediate supervisor as soon as possible of any potentially violent situation or any threat, assault or violent act (as defined) toward an employee by any individual.
NOTE: This requirement is not intended to apply to arrest situations in which an officer is threatened or assaulted by an arrestee.
In most instances, the supervisor who is made aware of any such problem shall prepare an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT.
It shall be the supervisor's responsibility to determine whether the affected section commander should be immediately notified, based on the apparent seriousness of the situation.
The department will take the steps it deems necessary to immediately address and remedy the problem.
All department employees shall comply with this order.
Policy

It is the policy of the Toledo Police Department to guard against improper conduct in order to maintain a quality working environment for all employees of this department. Employees are entitled to a workplace free from intimidation, humiliation, insult, physical abuse, verbal abuse or actions of a sexual, ethnic, racial or religious nature.
Definition

Personal harassment includes unwelcome sexual advances or requests for sexual favors or sexual, racial, ethnic or religion related jokes, comments, insults, cartoons or innuendoes or other verbal or physical conduct that could be construed as offensive or sexual in nature when:
Submission to such conduct is made explicitly or implicitly a term or condition of employment.
Submission to or rejection of such conduct by an individual is used as the basis for any employment decision affecting that individual.
Such conduct has the purpose or effect of interfering with an individual’s work performance or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive workplace.
Procedures
PERSONAL HARASSMENT

No employee of the Toledo Police Department shall personally harass another member. No employee of the department shall initiate, engage in alone or with others, or encourage another to violate any portion of this section.
SUPERVISORS ACCOUNTABLE

It shall be the responsibility of the Toledo Police Department to take appropriate action to prevent offensive physical and verbal conduct from occurring and to deal with all such reported incidents in a fair, impartial and speedy manner.
All complaints or incidents shall be investigated on a case-by-case basis.
When it is determined that a violation has occurred, action shall be taken to remedy the situation and to prevent any reoccurrence.

All supervisors shall be accountable to prevent personal harassment incidents from occurring within their work jurisdiction and to report any such incidents coming to their attention regardless of where they occur within the department.
REPORTING PERSONAL HARASSMENT

Incidents of personal harassment shall be reported to the commander of the Internal Affairs Section or any other supervisor of the employee’s choosing. The reports shall be forwarded directly to the commander of the Internal Affairs Section for investigation.

Nothing in this policy prevents an employee from directly contacting the Office of Diversity and Inclusion of the City of Toledo to file a complaint in addition to, or in lieu of, contacting the Internal Affairs Section.
Policy
The Toledo Police Department recognizes illegal drug usage as a threat to the public safety and welfare of the employees of the department.

Thus, the Toledo Police Department will take the necessary steps, including drug testing, to eliminate illegal drug usage by its employees. The goal of this policy is prevention and rehabilitation rather than termination. The illegal use of drugs and alcohol by employees of this department can have a major impact on job performance.
Procedures
IMPACT OF DRUG USE
DRUG-RELATED CRIMES

The department is especially sensitive to the fact that even the one-time usage of a controlled substance feeds into a vast network of criminal activity. Frequent use of drugs may lead to selling drugs, theft of drugs, theft of evidence, commission of other serious crimes, association with criminal corruption and involvement with organized crime.
UNRELIABLE WITNESSES
Employees who have used or abused drugs can easily be discredited as a witness in a court case.
MORALE AND LOSS OF PUBLIC TRUST

A scandal involving illegal drug usage in the police department would have a major impact on the vast majority of employees who have earned the public’s trust. The department would face speculation about the integrity and the willingness of the department to police its own.
SAFETY AND LIABILITY ISSUES
Department members have a number of responsibilities that set them apart from employees in other organizations:
They are entrusted with firearms.
They operate vehicles, sometimes under emergency conditions.
They have the authority to deprive others of their liberty.
They provide back-up to other officers in dangerous and sometimes lifethreatening situations.
They may be recalled to duty 24 hours a day.
DRUG TESTING; NOTIFICATION
ASSIGNMENT/SPECIALIZED UNIT - NOTIFICATION/TESTING

Personnel assigned to special units as specified in the respective bargaining agreements, and those in the Special Operations Bureau may be ordered at the Chief’s discretion to submit a urine sample for testing for illegal drug usage once each calendar year.
A calendar year shall be from January 1 to December 31.
The Chief of Police or his designee shall determine the date and time of the testing.
All notifications of assignment-related drug testing shall be made in writing on an ILLEGAL DRUG USAGE SCREENING FORM (TPD FORM 5.10).
During normal business hours, a sworn supervisor of at least one rank higher and/or the Personnel Section Commander or his designee shall accompany the officer to the city physician's office.
The officer shall then be ordered to submit a urine sample according to the specific procedures established by the city physician’s office.
PROMOTION-RELATED NOTIFICATION/TESTING
Sworn personnel may be tested as a requirement of promotion.
Officers tested as a requirement of promotion shall be notified of the place and time of the test.
All notifications of promotion-related drug testing shall be in writing on an ILLEGAL DRUG USAGE SCREENING FORM.
REASONABLE SUSPICION NOTIFICATION/TESTING
Any employee may be tested for illegal drug usage based on reasonable suspicion, whether on-duty or off-duty.
Reasonable suspicion is a lesser standard than probable cause.
There is reasonable suspicion when there is some articulable basis for suspecting the employee is using illegal drugs or using intoxicants.
This section removed.
All notifications to submit to drug testing due to reasonable suspicion shall be made in writing on an ILLEGAL DRUG USAGE SCREENING FORM AND FITNESS FOR DUTY USE OF INTOXICANTS FORM (TPD FORM 5.12).

It is the policy of the department to collect urine samples in a medical setting. Generally, the sample should be collected during normal business hours at the office of the designated city physician. However, samples may be collected in other medical settings during other than normal business hours.
RANDOM NOTIFICATION/TESTING

Employees whose labor agreement allows for random testing for illegal drug usage may be ordered to submit a urine sample to test for illegal drug usage. Whenever they are selected for such testing, employees will be required to submit a urine sample through the random method utilized by the Department’s drug screening provider.
The Chief of Police or his designee shall determine the date, time and location of the testing.
All notifications, of random drug testing, shall be made in writing on an ILLEGAL DRUG USAGE SCREENING FORM.
INCIDENT-RELATED NOTIFICATION/TESTING

Employees whose labor agreement allows for testing based on their involvement in an incident-related action (e.g., vehicle operator in an on-duty traffic accident, officerinvolved shooting, etc.) may be ordered to submit a urine sample to test for illegal drug usage, if they are involved in a covered incident.
Covered incidents are outlined in the current labor agreement.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Immediate testing based upon reasonable suspicion or probable cause is not limited to the listed incidents or to duty status. Testing procedures found in Directive 103.9/3.2 – SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES shall be utilized.

When an employee whose labor agreement calls for such testing is involved in an incident-related action, the employee’s Deputy Chief shall be immediately made aware of the facts surrounding the incident.
The Deputy Chief shall determine whether or not the employee shall be required to submit a urine sample to test for illegal drug usage.

When it is determined that an employee is to be tested as a result of an incident-related action, he shall be given a written order setting forth the time and date of the test, on an ILLEGAL DRUG USAGE SCREENING FORM AND FITNESS FOR DUTY USE OF DRUGS OR INTOXICANTS FORM.
A sworn supervisor of at least one rank higher, and the Personnel Section Commander or his designee, shall accompany the employee to the city physician’s office.
The employee shall then be ordered to submit a urine sample according to the specific procedures established by the city physician’s office.
FITNESS FOR DUTY; DRUG OR ALCOHOL TESTING

Supervisors are periodically faced with fitness-for-duty situations where immediate action is required. The following is an attempt to clarify and simplify some of the issues involved in the most common types of fitness-for-duty situations.
INTOXICATED EMPLOYEE OR SUSPECTED DRUG USE
If the employee is driving and probable cause exists to believe the employee is under the influence of alcohol and/or a drug of abuse, a criminal charge of OVI may exist.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Any employee suspected of OVI, whether on or off duty, shall be treated the same as any other citizen suspected of OVI.

If the employee is not driving, the basis for the testing of an on-duty or offduty employee is reasonable suspicion; a lesser standard than probable cause. There is reasonable suspicion when there is some articulable basis for suspecting the employee is using illegal drugs or under the influence of alcohol.
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

When an employee is suspected of driving under the influence; or there is reasonable suspicion that an employee is using illegal drugs; or there is reasonable suspicion that an on-duty employee has consumed alcohol or is under the influence of alcohol; or an off-duty officer has consumed any amount of alcohol and acts in the capacity of a police officer, or identifies himself as a police officer:

A sworn supervisor of at least the next higher rank must immediately be notified and respond to the scene. If a civilian employee is involved, the employee’s supervisor shall contact the shift commander, who will immediately respond to the scene.

The employee shall be immediately relieved of duty. The sworn supervisor shall immediately relieve the employee of his service weapon, Taser, police radio, ID card (civilians included) and badge/hat piece.

An employee suspected of being under the influence of drugs or alcohol shall be administered field sobriety tests for criminal proceedings. Field sobriety tests are not required when testing an employee for administrative charges.
Prior to testing for administrative charges, inform the employee of his right to union representation.
Per the T.P.C.O.A. and T.P.P.A. labor agreements, employees must be informed of the Toledo Police Department’s drug testing policy before testing is administered for administrative charges.

Notify the employee’s section commander. The section commander shall then ensure that the employee’s deputy chief, as well as the commanders of the Internal Affairs and Personnel Sections are notified immediately (if nonbusiness hours, contact may be made through Communications).

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: During business hours, the Personnel Section Commander shall review facts with the Chief of Police to determine if reasonable suspicion exists and notify the Safety Director.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: After business hours, the Personnel Section Commander and the respective deputy chief will determine if reasonable suspicion exists; then, the Personnel Section Commander will notify the Safety Director the next day.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: The respective deputy chief shall notify the Chief of Police.
Follow any and all instructions received by the Personnel Section Commander.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: This may include instructions for transporting the employee to a specific medical facility (if not an OVI), where the testing will take place.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: The Personnel Section Commander will meet the sworn supervisor and the employee at the medical facility.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: The Personnel Section Commander will make all arrangements with the medical facility.
The officer must be offered a breathalyzer test as it relates to the criminal or traffic charges of OVI or, if the employee was not driving, the administrative charge of use of intoxicants.

If the employee is being charged with the criminal charge of OVI or administrative charge of being intoxicated while on-duty, and refuses the breathalyzer test, the Personnel Section Commander, or his designee, shall order the employee, in writing, to submit to the breathalyzer test for administrative purposes using FITNESS FOR DUTY USE OF INTOXICANTS.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Refusal could result in the administrative charge of GROSS INSUBORDINATION, WILLFUL VIOLATION and/or CONDUCT UNBECOMING AN OFFICER.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: The officer shall be advised that refusal of the order could be the basis for disciplinary action up to and including dismissal from the department.
If the breathalyzer test is unable to be administered, another test may be given. Reasons for other tests may be, but are not limited to:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Breathalyzer machine is not operating.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Employee is unable, due to medical conditions, to take a breathalyzer test.
A sworn supervisor shall remain with the employee at all times, including transport.
The employee shall not be allowed to operate any vehicle.

The sworn supervisor shall cite the employee for any appropriate criminal/traffic OVI violations. Copies of the citation(s) shall be included with the UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0) and/or DEPARTMENT INVESTIGATION FORM REPORT (TPD FORM 5.6).

As with any private citizen charged with OVI, booking is optional as long as there is a responsible party to whom the arrested person may be released. At no time shall an on-duty officer serve as the responsible party to whom the arrested employee is released.

If the employee was not driving nor booked at the Lucas County Corrections Center, the sworn supervisor shall make arrangements to have the employee driven home by someone other than an on-duty employee. At no time shall an employee relieved of duty for drugs or intoxication be allowed to operate any motor vehicle.
URINE SAMPLES; CUSTODY
URINE TESTING

The sworn supervisor who relieves the employee of duty shall transport and remain with the employee at all times, until the employee has submitted a sufficient sample and the process has been completed. However, in order not to cause embarrassment to the employee, the sworn supervisor shall generally not be required to witness the submission of the urine sample, unless required by the policies of the medical facility.
The submission of samples taken during assignment/promotion-related testing shall not be witnessed.
This section deleted.

An employee, who in the judgement of the collecting official, attempts to substitute another person’s urine, alter by placing or mixing any foreign substance into the sample bottle with his urine, or in any other way, tampers with the collection process, will be required to remain at the medical facility and submit a proper sample.
Once the sample has been collected, the sworn supervisor shall be directed by the Personnel Section Commander where to take the employee.

All required and appropriate reports (i.e., UI, DIF, Supplemental) shall be completed immediately with one copy forwarded to the employee’s deputy chief, one copy to the Personnel Section Commander, and one copy forwarded to the Chief of Police. All envelopes containing reports shall be sealed and marked PERSONAL & CONFIDENTIAL.
SAMPLE AND CHAIN OF CUSTODY
A urine sample collected at the city physician’s office shall remain in his custody. The procedures established by his office for the preservation of the integrity of the sample shall be followed.
The urine sample collected for testing shall normally be obtained as the result of one void.

A minimum of 30 cc of urine must be obtained at one time in order for a split sample to be obtained. For those samples testing positive, the split sample will be subject to a second analysis at a second approved laboratory.
If less than 30 cc of urine is obtained, there will be no split sample. However, the original sample, if tested positive, will continue to be kept and available for testing at a separate laboratory.
SAMPLES NOT COLLECTED BY CITY PHYSICIAN

Incidents may occur where samples may be collected at medical locations other than the city physician’s office. When the Personnel Section Commander is notified, he shall respond to the employee’s location. The Personnel Section Commander shall supervise the collection of the sample. In addition to the other provisions of this order, he shall ensure the following steps are adhered to:
The name and department I.D. number of the employee submitting the sample are securely affixed to the bottle used to collect the sample.
The sample is collected directly from the employee submitting the sample or the medical personnel receiving the sample.
The sample is properly sealed and is marked on the top of the container with the initials of the employee submitting the sample, along with the initials of the medical personnel receiving the sample.
The Personnel Section Commander shall take custody of the sample and deliver it to the city physician’s office.
The city physician will make the request for analysis of the sample and ensure that his standard procedures are followed.
ANALYSIS OF SAMPLE
The urine sample from the employee will be analyzed at a laboratory selected by the city.

The laboratory will use established scientific principles in the analysis of the sample. However, to insure the highest degree of reliability, in every case where the initial screening test is positive, there shall be a confirmation test.
Only samples testing positive through the confirmatory test will be reported as positive.
Normally the EMIT test will be used as the initial screening test and Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometry (CG/MS) will be the confirmatory test.
REMOVED
The positive levels of other drugs being tested for will be determined by the established standards of the testing laboratory.
The confirmation test shall be qualitative in nature rather than quantitative.
PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES -- DRUG FREE WORK PLACE:

The use of, or presence of a prohibited substance in an employee’s system while on or off duty, is not permitted. Prohibited substances include: illegal drugs, prescription drugs not taken as prescribed and marijuana, including medical marijuana. Alcohol is defined as a prohibited substance when an officer is acting in an official capacity.

Marijuana remains an illegal controlled substance at the Federal level under the Controlled Substance Act. As such, department personnel, whether qualified or not by the Ohio Medical Marijuana Control Program, shall not be considered "fit for duty" if they are using or ingesting marijuana, including marijuana for medical purposes.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Any employee or volunteer of the department who has applied for, intends to apply for, received, or been denied a card as a “qualifying patient" under the Ohio Medical Marijuana Control Program, shall immediately notify the Chief of Police of any such action in writing.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Any employee or volunteer of the department who has applied for, intends to apply for, received, or been denied a card as a "caregiver" under the Ohio Medical Marijuana Control Program, shall immediately notify the Chief of Police of any such action in writing.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Any employee or volunteer of the department who has any person living within their residence who is considered, under the Ohio Medical Marijuana Control Program, to be a "qualified patient" or "caregiver" shall immediately notify the Chief of Police in writing indicating the person’s name and what relationship the department member has with the person(s).

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: No member of the department shall be permitted to own, operate, manage, be employed by, be financially involved in, or be otherwise involved in the operation, in any way, of any marijuana cooperative, dispensary, business or location that is used to manufacture, grow, process, use, sell, distribute or dispense marijuana for medical purposes, or any location that is involved in the sale or distribution of any paraphernalia that can be used for any of the above.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: No member of the department shall be permitted to be a "caregiver" as defined by the Ohio Medical Marijuana Control Program for any person, unless so authorized in writing by the Chief of Police. Permission may be granted by the Chief of Police to allow a member to be a "caregiver" in extreme circumstances and only for persons of the department member’s immediate family who are residing with the department member.

Personnel are required to comply with the federal Comprehensive Drug Abuse Prevention and Control Act (also known as the federal Controlled Substances Act) which considers marijuana to be a Schedule I controlled substance. Department personnel are prohibited from manufacturing, distributing, dispensing, or possessing a controlled substance, including marijuana. The manufacture or sale of controlled substances in performance of a work assignment must receive prior authorization from the Chief of Police.
Officers are further prohibited from using marijuana by the federal Gun Control Act, which prohibits an individual who uses marijuana from possessing a firearm or ammunition.
DISCIPLINE
Those employees testing positive for a prohibited substance may be subject to the disciplinary process.

Purpose/Policy

To provide guidance to ensure that police services are delivered equitably, respectfully and free of bias in a manner that promotes broad community engagement, trust and confidence in the Toledo Police Department.

Biased-based profiling is an unacceptable behavior and shall not be tolerated. The Toledo Police Department shall utilize various management tools to ensure that race, ethnicity, national origin, age, gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, economic status, cultural group, limited English proficiency or any other identifiable group profiling does not occur.
Definitions

Racial/ethnic/gender/sexual orientation profiling is defined as the stopping, questioning, detention, arrest, or other disparate treatment of any person based solely on characteristics of race, ethnicity, national origin, age, gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, economic status, cultural group, limited English proficiency or any other identifiable group.
Sufficient reason based upon known facts to believe a crime has been committed or that certain property is connected with a crime.
Legal standard of proof that is less than probable cause, the legal standard for arrests and warrants, but more than a “suspicion or ‘hunch’”; it must be based on “specific and articulable facts”.
Procedures
FAIR AND EQUAL TREATMENT

Officers must ensure all citizens receive equal and fair treatment regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, age, gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, economic status, cultural group, limited English proficiency or any other identifiable group.
BASIS OF STOP OR SEIZURE

Officers shall make traffic stops, field contacts, or any other formal action on the basis of reasonable suspicion or probable cause, shall make arrests only on the basis of probable cause, and shall not stop, detain, search, arrest or seize property based on race, ethnicity, national origin, age, gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, economic status, cultural group, limited English proficiency or any other identifiable group.
CORRECTIVE MEASURES
In addition to remedial training, officers who have profiling or discrimination complaints sustained against them may be subject to the disciplinary process.
Employees are required to report any observed or known violations of this order by any department employee to their immediate supervisor.
ANNUAL ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW
The Office of the Chief of Police, or their designee, shall conduct a documented annual administrative review of the department’s practices concerning biased-based profiling.
The review shall include, but is not limited to, department policy and procedure, statistical data, and citizen concerns and any corrective measures taken to address these concerns.
INITIAL AND ANNUAL AGENCY WIDE TRAINING

The Toledo Police Department shall conduct biased-based profiling related training that includes, but is not limited to the following: field contacts, traffic stops, search issues, asset seizures and forfeitures, interview techniques, cultural diversity, discrimination, and community support to all new hires. It shall also provide annual refresher training to all sworn personnel.
Policy

The Toledo Police department has a responsibility to its employees and the community to identify and assist employees who require additional training or are showing symptoms of job-related stress or performance problems. The Early Intervention System (EIS) offers a non-disciplinary avenue to detect and address problems and/or deficiencies with personnel as early as possible. The behaviors identified under the system parameters will result in a comprehensive review of the individual employee's performance.

The EIS is a proactive program that assists participants in achieving the highest professional and ethical standards to ensure that employees of the Toledo Police Department have the necessary knowledge, skills and abilities to provide the best possible service to the community. The goals of the system are to facilitate positive reinforcement, training, and counseling to promote career longevity for the employee.
The Early Intervention System is divided into three distinct areas:
Identification
Analysis and Review
Participation and Review
Procedures
CRITERIA THAT CAN TRIGGER AN EARLY INTERVENTION ASSESSMENT

Any of the below listed criteria, or a combination of the criteria, may cause an early intervention assessment to be completed by the EIS Review Committee. The EIS Review Committee will take an in-depth look at the criteria; decisions will not be based solely on the benchmarks, but rather as a collective whole.
Three or more complaints within a 12 month period in which the employee was not exonerated.
Three or more ACTION–RESPONSE (TPD FORM 29.3) incidents within a 12 month period which require additional supervisory review as a result of injuries suffered by prisoners.
Two or more violations of the Vehicle Pursuit Policy within a 12 month period.
Two or more preventable accidents within a 12 month period.

Three or more firearm qualification attempts on three separate exercises, or a failure to qualify with an officer’s duty weapon during annual qualifications. Any officer who has consistently demonstrated difficulties during firearm qualifications may also be recommended for the EIS by the range supervisor.
The referral is deemed appropriate by the chief of police.
BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS
The following performance data, although not all-inclusive, may indicate an employee is a candidate for EIS.
Below average performance evaluation.
A significant reduction in work performance.
Unusual or unexplained changes in behavior.
Excessive absenteeism and/or Late-for-Duty Reports.
Any discernible pattern of repeated complaints, regardless of finding, against an employee.
IDENTIFICATION PROCESS
The EIS Employee Identification Process is dependent upon recognition of candidates through the following methods:
DATA SCANNING BY THE ACCREDITATION / INSPECTIONS UNIT
Under this process, employee statistical data is reviewed on an ongoing basis for referral indicators.
DATA SCANNING BY THE INTERNAL AFFAIRS SECTION
Under this process, employee statistical data is reviewed on an ongoing basis for referral indicators.
SUPERVISORY ASSESSMENT
Any supervisor who identifies negative behavior patterns in an employee should request, through the employee’s division commander, that an EIS EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT be completed on the employee.
TRAINING SECTION ASSESSMENT
The Range supervisor, or his designee, identifies that an officer is in need of further firearms training.
EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT

When an employee has been identified through the EIS Employee Identification Process, or through a supervisory assessment, the EIS Review Committee shall thoroughly review all information pertaining to that employee, to determine whether an EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT (TPD FORM 12.40) is to be completed.

The EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT shall include any information that was used to determine the officer’s eligibility for the EIS program, including all reports. In addition, it shall also include the employee's present assignment, length of service, and any prior training that may be appropriate.

The completed EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT shall be sent to the employee’s division commander for review and recommendations. Once completed, the EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT shall be returned to the commander of the Administrative Services Bureau to determine a course of action.
THE EIS REVIEW COMMITTEE

The EIS Review Committee shall serve as an unbiased, objective group of department employees who provide a systematic and comprehensive review of defined indicator criteria when such a review is necessary. The EIS Review Committee shall consist of:
The commander of the Administrative Services Bureau or his designee (Chairperson)
The commander of the Personnel Section, or his designee
The commander of Internal Affairs Section, or his designee
The accreditation manager

The EIS Review Committee shall meet quarterly, and at the discretion of the chief of police, to analyze the preceding twelve months of threshold criteria data. The EIS Review Committee shall compile a list of all officers who have reached the identification process thresholds. The EIS Committee will thoroughly review all necessary reports to determine if a pattern of behavior has been identified or a cause of concern has been substantiated. If determined, then the EIS Review Committee shall complete an EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT (TPD FORM 12.40) and forward it to the appropriate division/bureau/section commanders, with a list of officers who have reached the determined thresholds. The appropriate district commander shall provide any additional information regarding the employee to assist the EIS Review Committee, if applicable.

After reviewing the completed EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT with the division commander’s recommendations, if the committee and the division commander concur they shall work together to develop a PLAN OF ACTION. If the committee and the division commander do not concur, they shall meet with the chief of police to determine the preferred course of action.
If no action is necessary, then the EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT will be filed, and no further action will occur.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: The EIS Review Committee Chairperson shall ensure that the referring supervisor is notified of the decided course of action to be taken.

If action is deemed necessary, the EIS Review Committee will notify the employee’s division/bureau/district commander and collectively, they will develop a PLAN OF ACTION (TPD FORM 12.30) for the employee. The committee shall then meet with the affected employee to discuss the plan and the expectations of the program. The chair of the committee will notify the applicable bargaining unit.
PLAN OF ACTION
The PLAN OF ACTION should be flexible to permit modification. Significant progress, or adverse behavior by the employee, may require that the PLAN OF ACTION be modified.
The PLAN OF ACTION shall include:
A synopsis of the identified behaviors of the employee that are adversely affecting his work performance.
Specific actions required of the employee, the employee’s immediate supervisor, and/or his bureau/district commander.

Notice to the employee that his participation in the PLAN OF ACTION is mandatory, and will not mitigate any disciplinary action resulting from the employee's on-duty or off-duty actions (e.g., future complaints, internal investigations).
Recommendations stemming from the PLAN OF ACTION may include, but are not limited to the following:
Supervisory counseling
Retraining of the employee in the specific area of concern
Referral for remedial training
Re-assignment (within contractual rights)
Mandatory use of a body camera
Fitness for duty
Referral to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Prior to its implementation, the PLAN OF ACTION shall be forwarded to the chief of police, for approval.
Copies of the approved PLAN OF ACTION shall be sent to the appropriate division/bureau/district commander and to the involved employee.
An additional copy of the PLAN OF ACTION shall be placed in the employee's personnel file.
The division/bureau/district commander or his designee shall review and discuss the PLAN OF ACTION with the employee and his immediate supervisor.
The chief of police may direct employees to attend EAP counseling, or other sources of counseling, at his/her discretion.
PLAN OF ACTION SPECIAL PROVISIONS
All PLAN OF ACTION reports shall be in effect for a period of six months from the date of approval by the chief of police.

The supervisor responsible for implementing the employee’s PLAN OF ACTION (shift supervisor or range supervisor) shall closely monitor the employee's progress. If a referral was made based on a supervisor assessment, the referring supervisor shall not be the supervisor monitoring the employee during this period. Note that this does not apply to the Range supervisor.

The supervisor shall complete an EARLY INTERVENTION SYSTEM STATUS REPORT (TPD FORM 12.60) which shall be signed and reviewed by the affected employee. The status report shall then be submitted monthly by the immediate supervisor to the bureau/district commander, with a copy forwarded to the involved employee’s division commander.

At the end of the six month period, the immediate supervisor will complete a final progress report along with a recommendation, and forward it through the bureau/district commander to the division commander, who shall forward it to the chief of police for review.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: The recommendation may include:
A declaration of successful completion of the PLAN OF ACTION
A request for an extension of the PLAN OF ACTION
A referral for additional assistance to the involved employee
Any other action deemed necessary

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: If the recommendation is a declaration of successful completion of the PLAN OF ACTION and is concurred with by both the division/bureau/district commander and the chief of police, no further action is necessary.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: If the recommendation is not a declaration of successful completion of the PLAN OF ACTION, an assessment meeting will be held with the EIS Review Committee.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Once the Plan of Action is complete, regardless of the outcome, employees shall be offered an exit interview with committee members.
RECORD RETENTION
The EMPLOYEE ANALYSIS REPORT and the original PLAN OF ACTION shall be filed in the Office of the Chief of Police for a period of one year, after the completion of the PLAN OF ACTION.
ANNUAL SYSTEM EVALUATION
The accreditation manager shall conduct an annual documented evaluation of EIS, including findings and recommendations. The report shall be submitted to the chief of police.
Policy

The Toledo Police Department is committed to providing the opportunity for all sworn and civilian personnel of the Toledo Police Department to receive emotional and tangible support at a time when personal or professional difficulties may interfere with work, family, or daily life. Stress associated with the law enforcement profession may impact the health, well-being and job performance of all involved individuals. In order to help department personnel deal with such stressors, the department will maintain a Wellness Unit dedicated solely to the well-being of its personnel. The Wellness Unit will provide department personnel with professional, objective and non-judgmental resources. Through the Wellness Unit, both a Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) Team and a Peer Support Team will be coordinated and administered. Through privileged confidentiality, these teams will be available to assist employees and their families with individual and family support for both critical incidents and daily stressors.
Definition

CISM TEAM- A group of officers trained to provide CISM services and emotional support services to fellow officers during and after a critical incident. CISM Team members are certified by the International Critical Incident Stress Foundation and are a part of the Ohio CISM network.

CRITICAL INCIDENT- Any event experienced on or off duty that is outside the realm of normal experience and could be expected to produce significant stress reactions. These stressful events may generate intense reactions and briefly interfere with a person’s coping mechanisms.

A formal Critical Incident Stress Debriefing (CISD) is a group discussion of a traumatic experience. These confidential meetings typically occur within a reasonable time of the incident. Although a CISD is usually held within three days, the specific timing depends on a number of factors. CISM Team members must judge the timing of the CISD meeting on a case-by-case basis. The CISD follows a standardized group process model approved by the International Critical Incident Stress Foundation (ICISF).
CRITICAL INCIDENT STRESS DEFUSING- A brief small group process conducted by CISM Team members within hours of a traumatic experience.
A comprehensive, systematic, and multicomponent approach to managing traumatic stress within an organization.

A short-term problem resolution, assessment and referral program service provided to employees and family members by the City of Toledo. Services are available for personal problems such as: depression, marital-family and relationship issues, alcohol or substance abuse, stress, finances, childcare or eldercare consultations, critical incident defusing and/or debriefing.
FAMILY SUPPORT SERVICES- A set of interventions which may be utilized by CISM Team officers to provide a range of crisis support services to families of officers.
FOLLOW-UP SERVICES- Contact with officers following initial services provided by a CISM Team member.
PEER SUPPORT TEAM- A group of officers dedicated to one-on-one support of department personnel about any topic that is of concern to the individual.

POLICE CHAPLAIN- A clergy person with a passionate interest in and the specialized training for pastoral care in the dangerous world of law enforcement. The chaplain is led in his or her own faith to be available and ready to serve those in need but is non-denominational in service.
PRE-INCIDENT EDUCATION- CISM information provided to newly hired personnel during in-service education programs.

REFERRALS- Recommendations made by the Wellness Unit to department personnel to seek further assistance through other resources such as the City’s Employee Assistance Provider (Lighthouse Telehealth – Harbor), chaplains, or other mental health professionals.
A dedicated department unit tasked solely with both the mental and physical wellness of department personnel.
Procedures
WELLNESS UNIT

The Wellness Unit will be responsible for the coordination and implementation of the programs and services that are focused on the well-being of the Toledo Police officers, both from a physical and mental standpoint. Some of the programs that the unit will be responsible for coordinating include:
Lighthouse EAP
CISM and Peer Support Teams
Military Reintegration
Specialized, outside therapy options
Physical Fitness information
Health Screenings
Police Chaplains
Dietary Issues
Sleep Issues
CISM TEAM

The CISM Team will provide crisis support services for department personnel who are involved in a critical incident in order to mitigate the impact of traumatic stress on their lives. The CISM Team aims to accelerate normal recovery processes of individuals who are having normal reactions to abnormal events. The CISM Team also attempts to identify personnel who might benefit from additional services beyond the scope of the CISM Team. All CISM Team members will be certified by the International Critical Incident Stress Foundation (ICISF) in both “Group Crisis Intervention” and “Assisting Individuals in Crisis”. Incidents that may qualify as critical incidents include, but are not limited to:
Line of Duty Death
Officer involved shootings or actions that result in serious injury or death of another whether intentional or accidental
Serious injury to officers in the performance of their duties
Suicide of an officer or civilian employee
Serious multiple casualty incidents or accidents
Incidents involving serious injury or death of children
Prolonged hostage or barricaded subject situations
Personally threating situation to an officer
Prolonged incident that ends in loss of life
Any other incident that produces unusually high levels of stress or has an unusually powerful impact on an officer or civilian employee

CISM TEAM DEFUSING – A defusing is defined as a small, brief post-incident intervention conducted by specially trained CISM Team members or chaplain immediately following a stressful incident and is designed to lessen the impact of the event and accelerate recovery. These will be conducted by CISM Team Members. Attendance at a defusing can be mandated by the department. Defusings should be held within 8-12 hours of the incident and typically last approximately 20-45 minutes. CISM Team members will make a determination if a CISM Team Debriefing is warranted following the defusing.

CISM TEAM DEBRIEFING - A debriefing is a group discussion of a traumatic experience. Debriefings will be made available for all personnel involved in a critical incident. Critical incident debriefings shall be held within 72 hours after the incident occurrence and attended by the on-call CISM Team member, a Lighthouse EAP counselor, CISM Team members, chaplain, and those officers that were present at the incident. Officers directly involved in critical incidents will be mandated to attend scheduled debriefings when utilized. The purpose of mandatory attendance is to ensure those directly involved in the incident receive support opportunities and to remove the possibility of negative impressions or stigmas associated with attending debriefings or support sessions. All persons involved in the incident have a valuable contribution to make to the recovery process. Attendance at a debriefing can be mandated by the department. When debriefings are necessary, they will be provided in accordance with the procedures established by the International Critical Incident Stress Foundation (ICISF).
CRITICAL INCIDENT NOTIFCATION PROCEDURE
Upon being notified of the occurrence of a critical incident, the section commander will inform their division or bureau commander of the need for a CISM Team member and chaplain.

Notification shall be made to the on-call CISM Team member as well as the on-call chaplain. The CISM team monthly on-call member and chaplain shall respond to the appropriate location to assist officers with either one-on-one interventions or a postincident CISM Team Defusing.
The CISM on-call member may utilize other CISM Team members for assistance, depending on the nature and size of the incident.

The on-call CISM Team member shall further assess the situation to determine the need for a formal CISM Team Debriefing and communicate their findings to the chief of police, chief’s designee, or division/bureau commander. A formal CISM Team Debriefing may or may not be required.

Once a CISM Team Debriefing is deemed necessary, the Wellness Unit Supervisor and EAP Provider shall be notified and will be responsible for determining the date, time and location of the CISM Team Debriefing. The Wellness Unit Supervisor shall then notify the on-call CISM Team member, chaplain and division/bureau/section Commanders of the date, time and location of the formal CISM Team Debriefing. Division/Bureau/Section Commanders shall notify the officers involved in the incident of their mandatory attendance.
The on-call CISM Team member shall coordinate with Lighthouse Tele-Health LLC to administer the CISM Team Debriefing.
CISM TEAM RESPOSIBILITIES FOR OFFICERS INVOLVED IN A DEADLY/LETHAL FORCE INCIDENT

The primary purpose of the CISM Team is to provide emotional comfort and support to the involved officer. Officers acting in this capacity shall not serve as counselors or attempt to provide counseling that may be beyond their expertise. CISM Team members shall refer affected officers to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) when necessary.
A member of the CISM Team shall report to the scene of any shooting incident, as requested by the supervisor in charge, or by members of the Shooting Investigation Team.
When requested to report to a scene, the team member shall report to the supervisor in charge of the scene.
The officer will provide moral and emotional support, only, and shall not become involved in the related investigation.
He will discuss with the officer, any post shooting feelings that may or may not arise.
He may provide other assistance, as necessary, after clearance from the supervisor in charge of the scene.
NOTE: The involved officer may refuse assistance from a CISM Team member.
DEATH/SERIOUS PHYSICAL INJURY, REMOVAL FROM FIELD ASSIGNMENT

When any department employee’s actions or use of force in an official capacity results in death or serious physical injury, the department employee shall be temporarily removed from field assignments, pending an administrative review by the chief of police. This review shall be conducted as soon as possible. This precautionary action serves to:
Shield department employees who have not exceeded the scope of their authority from possible confrontations with the community.
Protect the public's interest, if a department employee has exceeded the scope of his authority.
Ensure that the department employee is mentally prepared to return to a field assignment.
POST CRITICAL INCIDENT PROCEDURES
Personnel closely involved with critical incidents or significantly affected by a critical incident may at the chief's discretion be mandated to attend counseling in addition to CISM Team actions.
Any officer directly involved in a critical incident may receive critical incident leave time at the discretion of the Chief of Police (as outlined in the respective labor agreements).

An officer who utilizes critical incident leave time will be mandated to attend at least one counseling session within 30 days of the leave time. These sessions will be coordinated by the Wellness Unit Supervisor.
Critical Incident leave time may be granted by Division Commanders, Bureau/District Commanders and the Wellness Unit Supervisor after approval from the Chief of Police.
PEER SUPPORT TEAM

The Peer Support Team is open to all officers, regardless of rank, seniority or assignment. The Wellness Unit Supervisor will maintain an application process and solicit members as needed. The Wellness Unit Supervisor will make the final decision as to who will be selected to be on the Peer Support Team.

Serving on the Peer Support Team is purely a voluntary assignment and officers may resign from the Peer Support Team at any time. Officers may be removed from the Peer Support Team by the Wellness Unit Supervisor if their duties, assignments, a violation of the confidentiality agreement, or any other situation creates an inability to function as a member of the Peer Support Team.

Peer Support Team Members will be trained in conjunction with the CISM Team and will be expected to attend semiannual training sessions. Peer Support Team Members may also receive additional training from other agencies and organizations when available. International Critical Incident Stress Foundation (ICISF), certified training in both “Group Crisis Intervention” and “Assisting Individuals in Crisis”, is required for any member of the Peer Support Team.
Department personnel may contact Peer Support Team members for support on any issue that is of concern to the member.

Any employee of the department may approach any Peer Support Team Member at any time. Individual support conducted during off-duty time is encouraged but such meetings are purely voluntary on the part of the support person and the individual requesting the meeting.
A Peer Support Team Member may approach department personnel to offer assistance.
The Wellness Unit Supervisor or his designee will make arrangements for appropriate peer support activities.
OFFICER INVOLVED SHOOTING (OIS) SUPPORT TEAM

Members of the Officer Involved Shooting Support Team are also members of the Peer Support Team and subject to all training and guideline requirements of the Peer Support Team. OIS Support Team members have an additional requirement in that they have properly utilized a firearm during a response-to-resistance incident. OIS Support Team members are responsible for leading one-on-one follow-ups with officers that have recently utilized their firearm during a response-to-resistance incident. Follow-ups will include not only discussing the effects of the incident itself, but also peripheral issues that may be of concern to the officer (family issues, community issues, procedural issues, etc.).
CONFIDENTIALITY – CISM/PEER SUPPORT TEAM MEMBERS

All CISM and Peer Support Team members have an obligation and duty to maintain strict confidentiality. Any statement or discussion with a CISM or Peer Support Team member, while fulfilling his or her role on the CISM or Peer Support Team, will remain confidential except as specified below. CISM or Peer Support Team Members are prohibited from making notes or recordings of conversations while providing support.
The following communications are not considered confidential and the CISM or Peer Support Team must report these circumstances to the chief of police.
The communication indicates clear and present danger to the individual who receives crisis response services or to other persons.
The communication pertains or is related to any criminal act.
Admission of child abuse or neglect.

The CISM and Peer Support Teams’ participation in the Ohio CISM network allows the teams to be protected under the Ohio Revised Code - 2317.02(K) Privileged Communications. This code states: “The following persons shall not testify in certain respects: Except as provided under division (K)(2) of this section, a critical incident stress management team member concerning a communication received from an individual who receives crisis response services from the team member, or the team member's advice to the individual, during a debriefing session.”

Communication between the CISM or Peer Support Team members and an individual is privileged. It is the policy of the Toledo Police Department not to question CISM or Peer Support Team members concerning support services. CISM or Peer Support Team members may take recommendations to the Wellness Unit Supervisor for referral to additional assistance services if they feel additional support may be needed by individual officers or employees. The Wellness Unit Supervisor will evaluate the recommendation. Confidential information will not be disclosed during this process.
The department will not seek any information from a CISM or Peer Support Team member about any service they provide other than verifying those in attendance at mandatory sessions.
CISM or Peer Support Team members who violate confidentiality will immediately be dismissed from the CISM or Peer Support Team and may be subject to additional disciplinary action.
CISM and Peer Support Team members are not legal counsel and should not attempt to provide legal advice.
EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PROVIDER (EAP)
The City of Toledo Employee Assistance Provider (EAP) will be utilized as a resource as needed in supporting employees affected by critical incidents.

All employees of the Toledo Police Department are eligible for the program through the contracted provider. Program eligibility includes the spouse, domestic partner, children and household members of the employee.
Participation in the program will not jeopardize or impair job security, promotional opportunity or reputation.

Employees who have issues that they feel may affect their work performance or their personal lives will be encouraged to voluntarily seek information concerning employee assistance programs on a confidential basis by contacting the Wellness Unit Supervisor.
An employee who chooses to take advantage of the services offered by the city under the EAP may contact the contracted provider and make arrangements for an initial consultation.
The current contracted provider is Lighthouse Tele-Health LLC at 6629 W. Central Avenue Toledo, Oh 43617. The phone number is 419-475-5338 (Local) or 1-800-422- 5338 (toll free).
When an employee has an emergency situation that requires immediate assistance, the employee may contact the contracted provider to arrange for counseling, which is available twenty-four hours a day.
SUPERVISOR REFERRAL TO EAP - All employees exhibiting behavioral or adverse job performance that indicates they may have the need for EAP services may be referred to the Wellness Unit Supervisor.
The referring supervisor shall be sensitive to the employee’s needs while the employee is using the program and cooperate with the Wellness Unit Supervisor, if requested.

When an employee has experienced a serious or critical incident, the employee's supervisor should recommend EAP services to the employee. When a supervisor feels that a serious or critical incident has had such a significant impact on the employee that requires time away from the current assignment, the supervisor shall make such request through his chain of command to the chief of police. The chief shall review the case and determine if the action is warranted and the length of the temporary assignment.

Participants in the EAP shall be expected to meet existing job performance standards and established work rules within the framework of existing labormanagement agreements. Any exception to this requirement shall be by mutual agreement between labor and management.

RECORDS AND CONFIDENTIALITY - All EAP records shall be kept strictly confidential and shall be considered private medical records within the limits governed by federal and state regulations. These medical records shall not be noted in any public document or in the employee's personnel file.
TOLEDO POLICE CHAPLAINS

The Toledo Police Chaplains work in conjunction with the Wellness Unit to meet the spiritual needs of the affected employees. Chaplains are coordinated by the Wellness Unit Supervisor in conjunction with the Personnel Commander. Chaplains are appointed by the chief of police and serve at the chief’s discretion.
All services offered by police chaplains are free of charge.

Police chaplains provide pastoral care for members of the department requesting emotional and spiritual guidance and will be available to assist members both on and off duty. Members are encouraged to call upon the chaplains for their services as necessary.

Supervisors should call out chaplains in situations where their presence may enhance the operations of the police units involved or be of service to the community on behalf of the Toledo Police Department. Examples of when to call out the chaplains may include: unexpected deaths, infant deaths, major accidents and homicide scenes with inconsolable family members.

Chaplains are permitted access to department facilities, events, and call-out locations when serving in an approved chaplaincy capacity. Commanders may restrict this access at certain internal affairs, intelligence or other sensitive operations where such presence may endanger operations, police personnel or the chaplain.

Chaplains shall display an ID badge at any emergency call-out field condition that identifies him or her as a Toledo Police Chaplain. Attire should be the clothing of their order or department issued polo shirts/jackets with the word “Chaplain” or conservative professional clothing to avoid unfavorable comment on the department.

Matters of a personal nature will remain private unless otherwise required by law. Police chaplains have an obligation and duty to maintain strict confidentiality within the limits of law, safety, mandatory reporting requirements, and department policy.
The following communications are not considered confidential and must be reported through the appropriate chain of command or required reporting channel:
The communication indicates a clear and present danger to the individual receiving services or to other persons.
The communication pertains or is related to any criminal act.
Police chaplains who violate confidentiality may be removed from the Police Chaplain Program and may be subject to additional review or action as determined by the department.
Services provided by the chaplains:
Respond and offer spiritual counsel to those affected when an officer has been killed in the line of duty or seriously wounded/injured.

Assist officials in making notifications to families of officers receiving serious injuries or upon death, or if requested by the officer on their CONFIDENTIAL NOTIFICATION OF SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH (TPD FORM 1.2).
Assist officers in making serious injury or death notifications in particularly difficult situations (e.g. the scene of a fatal traffic accident).
Attend and participate in funerals of active and retired members of the department.
Provide spiritual counseling to officers when requested.
Call on sick and injured police personnel at home or in the hospital.
Attend department graduations, promotions and award ceremonies, memorial services and other social events to offer invocations and benedictions.
When requested by the department, act as a liaison to other religious leaders in the community.
Provide pastoral care in crisis situations.
Chaplains shall maintain a visible and supportive presence with department personnel through attendance at roll calls and participation in a ride along with an assigned unit.
Assist in the instruction of or attend in-service training dealing with, but not limited to, topics such as stress management, ethics, family life and preretirement.
Credentials, Training and Availability

Ecclesiastically certified person in good standing and endorsed for law enforcement chaplaincy by a recognized religious body, with five (5) years’ experience in ministry. Acceptability in the program is contingent upon their continued good standing within the religious organization the Chaplain represents.
Willing to be carefully screened by a chaplaincy committee, comprised of the Personnel Section Commander and the Wellness Unit Supervisor.

Willing to become involved in training programs that enhance one's efficiency in meeting and dealing with people in crisis and should be familiar with community medical, psychiatric and other helping resources in the local area.
Be readily available to assist Toledo Police personnel, including call-out situations, without endangering their ministry work.
Must be an active member of the International Conference of Police Chaplains (ICPC) and in good standing.

After one (1) year of appointment to the position of Police Chaplain, the chaplain shall be scheduled to complete the Basic Chaplaincy Course Bundle through the International Conference of Police Chaplains and shall complete the course within the training completion period established by ICPC.
FITNESS INCENTIVE TIERED (FIT) PROGRAM

Police work can be dangerous and physically demanding. Research indicates that good physical fitness positively affects every aspect of life. A physically fit employee is less inclined to illness and injury, and enjoys improved mental alertness and emotional well-being. Officers who are physically fit are better equipped for the increased demands of today's law enforcement profession and can positively affect personal and public safety.

Officers who choose to participate in this voluntary program will be eligible to receive compensatory time added to their time bank depending on the tier of exercises they are able to successfully complete. These tiers will be based on OPTOC physical fitness standards.
ACADEMY MENTORING PROGRAM

Mentoring programs have been effective in developing more successful police officers who understand the organization’s culture, history, and mission, as well as increasing their job satisfaction, loyalty, appreciation, and feeling of institutional support.

Mentoring is a mutually beneficial relationship in which a well-respected, veteran officer (Mentor) provides insight, guidance, and support to a new recruit (Mentee) through their academy and FTO assignments, and possibly beyond. The Mentor may assist with personal or professional concerns that may impact job performance or overall well-being. The Mentor serves as a supportive resource with no role in formal training or evaluation.
Mentoring Goals:
To promote professional growth and to assist with the transition into a law enforcement career in the Toledo Police Department.
To increase the probability of successfully completing the probationary period and integration into the department.
To provide guidance for personal and professional development.
To support the overall well-being of the officer and their family. Eligibility:
Mentor must be a Toledo Police Officer (any rank) that has been selected and agreed to the voluntary terms of the program.
Mentee must be a Toledo Police cadet assigned to the Toledo Police Academy.
The Mentorship Program Coordinator will be the Wellness Unit Supervisor.

Selection and pairing of all Mentors will be conducted by a Mentor Selection Committee consisting of the commander of the Support and Administrative Services Division (or their designee(s)), the commander of the Toledo Police Academy (or their designee(s)), and the Wellness Unit Supervisor.
PRE-SERVICE EDUCATION

All officers will receive pre-service training regarding critical incident effects. Training should emphasize the nature of critical incidents and how stress associated with these types of incidents may affect emergency service personnel. Training should also provide the employee with suggestions regarding how to positively manage stress associated with critical incidents. Training will be coordinated by the Wellness Unit.
TRAINING
Training will be provided to all officers on an annual basis on aspects of physical health (i.e. exercise and nutrition, health screenings, sleep, etc.).
Training will be provided to all officers on an annual basis on aspects of mental health (i.e. reactions to trauma/stress and coping skills/treatment options, etc.).
GENERAL HEALTH AND PHYSICAL FITNESS
Personnel are expected to maintain a level of general health and physical fitness that will enable them to perform the duties as detailed in their job description.
ANNUAL REVIEW
A review of this policy will occur annually, including an assessment of the effectiveness of the department’s wellness programs, with adjustments as needed based on feedback and/or other outcomes.
Policy

The purpose of this policy is to provide department personnel with the information necessary to properly fulfill the reporting and testimonial requirements mandated under Brady v. Maryland 373 U.S. 83 (1963) and Giglio v. U.S. 405 U.S. 150 (1972).

The U.S. Supreme Court decisions and subsequent rulings involving Brady/Giglio mandate that law enforcement agencies identify and provide the prosecution with any exculpatory evidence and/or Brady/Giglio material that would have a reasonable probability of altering the results in a trial or could reasonably mitigate the sentencing of a defendant. This includes, but is not limited to, any material relevant to the credibility of government witnesses and law enforcement officers. Failure to abide by this policy may jeopardize a law enforcement officer’s ability to continue serving as such.
Definitions
Violations of an individual's 14th Amendment right to due process of law involving the failure to disclose exculpatory evidence.
The affirmative constitutional duty of the police to notify the prosecutor of any exculpatory evidence and Brady/Giglio material.

Evidence that is favorable to the accused is material to the guilt, innocence, or punishment of the accused; and that may impact the credibility of a government witness, including a police officer. Impeachment material is included in the Brady/Giglio disclosure requirements.

Evidence is material if there is a reasonable probability that disclosing it will change the outcome of a criminal proceeding. A reasonable probability is a probability sufficient to undermine confidence in the outcome of the trial or sentencing of a criminal case.
Procedures
GENERAL PROVISIONS OF DISCLOSURE -AFFIRMATIVE DUTY TO REPORT

When subpoenaed as a witness in a court case, prosecutors will discuss issues pertinent to Brady/Giglio disclosure with Toledo Police personnel during pretrial meetings. All Toledo Police personnel shall fully and truthfully answer all questions asked by the prosecutor.

Any previously unknown or unrecognized exculpatory evidence, for which a defendant is subject to, or is experiencing, a significant and on-going deprivation of liberty in relation to current or post-conviction investigations, shall be documented on a CRIME REPORT (TPD FORM 38.1) or SUPPLEMENTAL CRIME REPORT (TPD FORM 38.3)
explaining the details or nature of the evidence. The officer shall advise his or her direct supervisor and the commander of the Court Liaison Unit as soon as practical.
Collect and book any evidence per Department policy.
A copy of the report shall be forwarded to both the officer’s direct supervisor and the commander of the Court Liaison Unit.
Without undue delay, the officer’s direct supervisor will be responsible for ensuring follow-up with the commander of the Court Liaison Unit.
The commander of the Court Liaison Unit will notify the appropriate prosecutor as soon as practical.

If information is believed to be privileged or confidential (e.g., confidential informant or protected personnel files); the information will be forwarded to the prosecutor to determine the appropriate manner in which to proceed.

Evidence or facts are considered material if there is a reasonable probability that they would affect the outcome of a criminal proceeding or trial, this includes evidence that could be used to impeach an officer’s credibility on cross examination. Determining whether evidence or facts are material often requires legal or even judicial review. If an officer is unsure whether evidence or facts are material they shall document the circumstances in a CRIME REPORT (TPD FORM 38.1) or SUPPLEMENTAL CRIME REPORT (TPD FORM 38.3). Additionally, they shall address the issue with their direct supervisor.

Supervisors who are uncertain about whether evidence or facts are material shall address the issue in written form to an appropriate prosecutor. A copy of the document shall be retained by the supervisor.
EXAMPLES OF BRADY/GIGLIO MATERIAL THAT MAY BE SUBJECT TO DISCLOSURE INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, THE FOLLOWING:
Any witness statement, however recorded, which suggests that someone other than the defendant committed a crime.
Any evidence relevant to potential bias of a witness, including promises or deals made to the witness by the police.
Information that tends to diminish the degree of the defendant’s culpability or the defendant’s offense level under state or federal sentencing guidelines.

Information concerning any situation in which an officer was disciplined internally by any law enforcement related agency for lying, falsifying documents, preparing misleading police reports, planting evidence, providing false statements under oath and theft.
Any pending criminal charges and/or past convictions against an officer involved in an investigation. This includes both misdemeanors and felonies.
TESTIMONIAL IMPEACHMENT

Department personnel who are knowingly and intentionally untruthful, or are otherwise dishonest in the course of their employment, are subject to impeachment of testimony at trial. Such personnel are also subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

Pre-conviction and post-conviction investigations where claims of omitted exculpatory evidence are the result of the initial investigation by the department should not be conducted by investigative personnel involved in the initial investigation.
TRAINING
All Toledo Police Department personnel shall receive annual training in Brady/Giglio disclosure requirements.
Policy

The Toledo Police Department provides guidelines to officers so they are better prepared to render quality services to individuals of the LGBTQ+ community. The policy of The Toledo Police Department is to interact with the LGBTQ+ in a manner that is respectful, professional and courteous.
Definitions
Adopted Name - Non-birth name that a transgender individual uses in self-reference (this may or may not be the individual’s legal name).
Asexual – A person who has no sexual feelings or desires, or who is not sexually attracted to anyone.

Intersex – A set of medical conditions that features a congenital anomaly of the reproductive and sexual system. A person with an intersex condition is born with sex chromosomes, external genitalia, or an internal reproductive system that is not considered “standard” for either male or female. Referred to in the past as “hermaphrodites”, intersex is the preferred term.
LGBTQ+ - A term used to refer collectively to those who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning, intersex and asexual.
LGBTQ+ LIAISON OFFICER - The LGBTQ+ liaison officer is a department member selected by the chief of police to promote cooperation between department members and the LGBTQ+ community.
Queer - An umbrella term for sexual and gender individuals who are not exclusively heterosexual.
Questioning - Applies to people who are uncertain as to their sexual orientation or gender, as well as sexual and gender identity.

Transgender - A general term applied to a variety of individuals, behaviors, and groups involving tendencies that diverge from normative gender role (woman or man), commonly but not always assigned at birth, as well as gender roles traditionally held by society.
Procedures
ROLE OF LGBTQ+ LIAISON OFFICER
The LGBTQ+ liaison officer’s role includes, but is not limited to, the following:
Provides internal support to employees on LGBTQ+ matters.
Promotes cooperation between the department and the community, while taking a leading role in building a link between the police and LGBTQ+ community.
Informs the deputy chief of operations of LGBTQ+ significant events and incidents occurring in the community.
INTERACTIONS WITH TRANSGENDER INDIVIDUALS

Transgender individuals shall be addressed by their adopted name and with pronouns consistent with their gender identity (he/him/his; she/her/hers; they/them/their). Officers should respectfully ask transgender individuals how they preferred to be addressed.

Whenever reasonably possible, searches of transgender individuals shall be conducted by an officer of the gender preferred by the individual absent exigent circumstance. If exigency necessitates an immediate search, an officer of either gender may conduct the search.
The booking or transporting officer(s) shall inform jail staff of arrestee’s gender identity status.

When completing reports, the individual’s name and gender that is on the most current government identification (e.g., driver’s license, passport, etc.) shall be used to complete the suspect, victim and other necessary information fields. If available to the officer(s), the individual’s adopted name shall be listed in the alias field and their preferred gender identity status shall be listed in the narrative of the report.
An arrestee’s transgender status shall not be disclosed to any non-law enforcement personnel, except when required for some other lawful purpose.

Officers shall not remove any appearance-related items (wigs, prosthetic breasts, etc.) unless the items would be removed for a non-transgender individual or unless the items are evidence or present a safety hazard to the officers or others.
Officers that have questions regarding this policy should contact a supervisor for further guidance.
MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR TRANSGENDERED INDIVIDUALS

Persons that have had, or who are in the process of transsexual operations or taking hormone treatments could experience harmful physical reactions and may require medical attention. If a transgender individual experiences any need for medical attention, officers shall address the need with the same urgency and respect as any other medical situation.
Policy

In advancing the department’s goal of maintaining public trust and organizational confidence, the department commits to taking reasonable precautions to avert undue influence resulting from family and personal relationships between department employees. While the department recognizes the rights of employees to have familial and/or personal relationships with co-workers, public trust, workplace safety, departmental operations and morale require that employees avoid the appearance or actual conflict of interest. Therefore, employees shall not use their position or their relationship status for the purposes of coercing or seeking special treatment from another.
Definitions
FAMILY RELATIONSHIP –Relatedness or connection by blood, marriage, or adoption/foster care. Includes: significant other, domestic partner, multiple generations, and in-laws.
is a relationship involving employees who are dating, engaged in a romantic/sexual relationship or cohabitating.
A superior officer or professional employee who supervises, acts in the capacity of a Field Training Officer, directs and/or evaluates the activities of personnel assigned to them.
An employee who is answerable to another employee based on their rank, job classification or job assignment.

An employee who is subject to a formal evaluation process as part of a formal training program. This includes academy cadets, probationary officers in the Field Training Program, and employees assigned to new assignments/specialized units.
Procedures
HIRING, PROMOTION AND SPECIALIZED POSITIONS/ASSIGNMENTS

Personnel in familial relationships or involved in a personal relationship with candidates shall not participate in any part of the hiring, promotional, or assignment to specialized positions process.

If participation cannot be avoided (e.g., absence of available alternate), the final selection decision is subject to approval by the Chief of Police or his designee, or the Director of Public Safety.
SUPERVISOR/EMPLOYEE, TRAINER/TRAINEE RELATIONSHIPS

Employees, in a familial or personal relationship, shall not accept or knowingly be placed in a supervisor/subordinate assignment, trainer/trainee assignment, or in positions/assignments when the relationship could interfere with the job assignment, working conditions, morale, professionalism, and/or the goals and objectives of the department, as determined by the Chief of Police or his designee.
REPORTING

Supervisors and subordinates, assigned to the same unit or section, who develop a personal or familial relationship during the course of employment shall report the relationship to the commander of the Personnel Section.

If the relationship could create a conflict of interest, affect the job assignment, working conditions, morale, professionalism, and/or the goals and objectives of the department, one of the involved employees may be transferred to another position after consultation with the respective bargaining unit(s), and as determined by the Chief of Police or his designee.
At no time shall an employee, serving in the Training Section or as a Field Training Officer, develop a personal relationship with a trainee.
Allegations of fraternization and/or nepotism shall be forwarded to the Internal Affairs Section, documented and investigated in accordance with Directive 103.3, Administrative Discipline.

Allegations shall be based on the actual or reasonably perceived adverse impact(s) created by the alleged fraternization and/or act of nepotism, not the existence of any particular relationship in and of itself.
Allegations of fraternization and/or nepotism may be reported:
Sworn officers - Your commanding officer or Internal Affairs.
Civilian employees – The Personnel Section.
EXCEPTIONS

Only the Chief of Police or his designee may make exceptions to the directives in this policy such that personnel may be assigned to best fulfill and support the mission of the department, promote safety and welfare, avoid the creation or continuation of conflicts of interest, and enhance the quality and efficiency of service.
Policy
The administrative reporting system is established to provide a continuous and accurate flow of information between management and operational units.
Procedures
DAILY REPORTS
UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (UI)
Purpose – to report any unusual incident of exceptional concern to the Department that requires major police action or any incident of such a nature that it is potentially newsworthy.
A sworn supervisor of the appropriate rank shall respond to the scene and prepare an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0).
Distribution shall be made by sending the original report and a copy of any related reports via departmental email to the UI contact list and the affected employee’s chain of command.
ADULT INVESTIGATION CRIME CONTROL LOG
Purpose – to inform personnel of daily felonies, deceased persons, and the locations at which they occurred.
Investigative Services desk personnel shall log incoming calls from patrol officers.
REMOVED
REMOVED
DAILY TOTALS
Purpose – to record a summary of officers’ daily activities.
The following totals shall be provided to the watch commander or the watch commander’s designee by every patrolman at the end of each tour of duty:
Moving citations
Field Interviews (FI)
On-view misdemeanor/felony arrests and warrants
All reports
Parking citations
Traffic stops
Suspect stops
Walk-rides
MONTHLY REPORT
PURPOSE
