Whenever an officer seizes a container of an obviously flammable liquid (e.g., gasoline, kerosene, etc.) or any other liquid which cannot be identified, the container shall be protected for prints, when applicable, tagged and placed in the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage cabinet in the Safety Building garage.

Officers shall include in the CRIME REPORT/INCIDENT REPORT that the liquid is stored in the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage cabinet. A SUPERVISOR’S REPORT (TPD FORM 20.7) shall be sent to the Property Management Unit indicating that property has been placed in the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage Cabinet.

The Toledo Fire and Rescue Department Arson Unit shall be responsible for having fluids that are connected to an arson investigation analyzed and the container checked for prints. After the fluid has been analyzed, it shall be the responsibility of the Arson Unit to dispose of the remaining contents. The empty container shall be discarded, transferred to the Property Room or, if there is no prosecution, returned to the owner. This decision shall be made by the Arson Unit personnel assigned to the case.
Fluids not related to an arson investigation that need to be analyzed shall be placed in the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage cabinet. A REQUEST FOR ANALYSIS (TPD FORM 61.5) shall be completed.

If the property is not evidence in a criminal case, a completed PROPERTY ROOM RELEASE (TPD FORM 23.10) should be attached at the time the property is placed in the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage cabinet.
FIREARMS IN CUSTODY

Any officer who comes into the possession of a firearm shall first ensure it has been rendered safe. If it cannot be rendered safe, officers shall follow the procedures outlined in directive 304.1/8.4.4 Property Management; Loaded Firearms.
When an officer takes custody of a firearm, he shall complete both the A.T.F. FIREARMS TRACE REQUEST (TPD FORM 19.1) and a REQUEST FOR ANALYSIS (TPD FORM 61.5).

Contact on-duty CSIU personnel to process the firearm. If no CSIU personnel are working or available, book the firearm into the Central Station Night Property Room’s designated “CSIU” lockers ensuring that booking procedures do not compromise fingerprint or DNA analysis. (See directive 407.11/2 HANDLING OF DNA EVIDENCE).

Prior to booking the firearm into the Night Property Room’s designated “CSIU” locker or loaded firearms locker, the officer shall obtain all of the information required from the firearm. When a firearm’s serial number is not present or has been removed, officers shall record as much identifying information as possible (make, model, caliber, unique features). The forms shall be filled out as completely as possible, clearly describing the circumstances under which the firearm was obtained.

Officers shall mark the appropriate ‘test fire’ check box on the REQUEST FOR ANALYSIS. This is in addition to any other examinations requested for a particular investigation. Property Management Unit personnel will not process the firearm unless the required forms are completed and booked with the firearm. In instances where the forms are not completed or booked with the firearm, the officer’s supervisor will be notified and the involved officer will be directed to complete and submit the proper forms.
The officer shall place the A.T.F. FIREARMS TRACE REQUEST form, the REQUEST FOR ANALYSIS form and a draft copy of the General Offense report in the locker with the bagged firearm.
The Forensic Laboratory shall be responsible for having firearms appropriately tested.
When handling and booking the firearm, treat the weapon as if protecting for prints/DNA:

As with all evidence processed for DNA analysis/biological evidence, officers must avoid talking, sneezing, scratching, and coughing over the shell casings. Officers must avoid touching their face, nose and mouth when collecting and packaging the casings.
Wear nitrile gloves at all times when handling firearms. Change gloves if handling other property, before touching the firearm again.
Avoid touching (as much as possible) the areas of the firearm where DNA may exist
For semiautomatic firearms, officers shall remove the magazine from the weapon and remove the round from the chamber. For revolvers, remove all rounds from the cylinder.
DO NOT remove the bullets from the magazine
Place only one firearm and its associated magazine (if applicable) and bullets in the same brown paper bag. DO NOT USE PLASTIC BAGS OR STAPLES.
For rifles, wrap the firearm in brown paper to protect for DNA. Place associated magazine (if applicable) and bullets in a brown paper bag. The rifle and the bag can be placed into the same locker.
All other evidence not directly associated with the firearm (e.g., holsters, other bullets, drugs, etc.) shall be booked separately per normal booking procedures.

Officers shall attach to the paper bag with tape (NO STAPLES): Two completed property tags – one for the firearm/magazine and one for the bullets. Omit the number of bullets if still in the magazine, just fill out the caliber of the bullets, if known.
Biohazard stickers should be affixed to the firearm if the firearm was exposed to any hazardous material.
LOADED FIREARMS
Any officer who comes into the possession of a loaded firearm that cannot be rendered safe through familiar unloading techniques shall not attempt to unload or tamper with the firearm.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: If it cannot be determined if a firearm is loaded, it shall be assumed the firearm is loaded and the following procedures apply:
Officers shall transport the firearm in such a manner as to reasonably ensure the firearm will not discharge.
As soon as possible, the firearm shall be taken to the Scott Park District Station.
If the range is open, a range staff member will attempt to render the firearm safe and return it to the transporting officers.
The range supervisor shall determine who is best qualified to render the weapon safe.

If the range is closed, the firearm shall be placed in the Loaded Firearms Locker located at the Scott Park range area. Officers shall complete a SUPERVISOR’S REPORT stating that a loaded weapon is in the Loaded Firearms Locker and the report shall be placed in the range mailbox.
The involved officer shall ensure all other property booking procedures are followed, exercising extreme caution when marking and tagging the loaded firearm.
When the range opens, a range staff member will attempt to render the weapon safe and place it in the Firearms Locker in the Night Property Room for removal by Property Management Unit personnel.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: The Loaded Firearms Locker shall not be used for any other purpose.
CURRENCY
Any officer who takes custody of currency shall complete a CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM (TPD FORM 23.16). Instructions for banding currency and completing the form are printed on the form.
A second officer (witness officer) shall count all currency and coins. Both the primary officer and the witness officer shall initial each band of currency and sign the CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM.

Paper currency shall be neatly packaged with all bills uniformly oriented without any folded, curled or stapled bills. Officers shall fold and seal one (1) copy of the CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM and place it with the currency in a heat-sealed bag, ensuring that the "Currency Amount Total $____" portion of the form is visible from the outside of the bag. One (1) copy of the CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM shall be attached to the outside of the heat-sealed bag.
In the event that more than one heat-sealed bag is needed to secure the money, a CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM shall be completed for the amount of money in each bag.
The original CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM shall be submitted to the Records Section along with the CRIME REPORT/INCIDENT REPORT.
Once the currency has been securely heat-sealed, recounting the money becomes unnecessary.
Officers sealing the bags shall be responsible for the amounts stated on the inventory form.
All currency shall be booked into the Property Room or, during periods when the Property Room is closed, into a Night Property Room, Secure Mailbox.
If, for any reason, a heat-sealed bag is opened, the following procedures shall apply:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: At least two officers shall be present.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: The money shall be immediately counted and recounted to verify the amount.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: The officers shall complete a new CURRENCY INVENTORY FORM and reseal both the old and new forms in a new bag when booking the money back into the Property Room.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Complete a SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT (TPD FORM 38.3) stating the circumstances under which the bag was opened.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: If a discrepancy is discovered in the amount of money contained in the bag, the officers shall immediately notify their supervisor. The supervisor shall complete a DEPARTMENT INVESTIGATION FORM (TPD FORM 5.6) on the incident.
COIN MONEY

Officers coming into possession of coin money shall follow the procedure in Directive 304.1/8.5 – CURRENCY. In the event that a large number of coins are involved where counting and heat-sealing are not practical, officers shall request direction from their immediate supervisor and note their actions in the CRIME REPORT/INCIDENT REPORT.
FINE JEWELRY AND PRECIOUS METALS
Officers booking jewelry, watches and precious metals shall utilize plastic heat-sealed bags so that the contents of the bag are visible from the outside.

Several items that are similar in both description and value can be placed in one heat-sealed bag (e.g., several rings, several bracelets, etc.). Miscellaneous items of lesser value shall not be mixed in with more valuable items.
The contents of each bag shall be listed on the property tag, or an inventory shall be attached to the tag. This information shall also be included in the CRIME REPORT/INCIDENT REPORT.
RAPE KITS
Officers booking rape kits shall tag and book them separately from all other evidence.

Whenever an officer picks up a rape kit, he shall immediately deliver it to the Property Room. If the Property Room is closed, the kit shall be placed in the Safety Building Night Property Room. In addition, officers shall complete the following:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Sign and date the outside of the container.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Ensure the individual who hands the officer the container has properly sealed, signed and dated it.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Ensure hospital personnel have completely filled out all the necessary information on the outside of the container.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: If the transporting officer is not the original reporting officer, include the following information in a Crime Report, or in a SUPPLEMENTAL CRIME REPORT:
The date and time the kit was picked up.
The hospital from which it was picked up.
The time the kit was delivered to the Safety Building.
Rape kits shall not be placed in bags. A completed evidence tag shall be affixed to each individual rape kit. All other evidence from the same case shall be packaged and tagged separately.
DIGITAL EVIDENCE
Officers shall book all devices and media containing digital evidence into the Property Room.
When the Property Room is closed, the devices and media shall be booked into the Safety Building Night Property Room in the area designated for digital evidence.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: MEMORY CARD ENVELOPES (containing memory cards and PHOTO PLACARDS) shall be booked into the locker designated for MEMORY CARD ENVELOPES.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: All devices and other media containing digital evidence shall be booked into the Safety Building Night Property Room in the area designated for digital evidence.

EXCEPTION: Recordings made with the In-Car Camera Recording Systems, Body Worn Camera Systems, Unmanned Aircraft Systems, Drone as First Responder, and License Plate Readers shall be handled according to the respective department manual directive.
EVIDENCE SHELL CASINGS

Officers shall book all shell casings collected at a scene/incident into the designated mailboxes located at the Central and Scott Park Stations. As with all evidence processed for DNA analysis/biological evidence, officers must avoid talking, sneezing, scratching, and coughing over the shell casings. Officers must avoid touching their face, nose and mouth when collecting and packaging the casings.
Officers shall fill out the Property Log located at the mailbox.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Wear nitrile gloves when handling shell casings.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Shell casings shall be collected and packaged by caliber, if known, and by groupings (where located). Change gloves between each group of casings.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Place shell casings in Evidence Collection Envelopes (TPD Form 55.1a), or a small brown paper bag, and seal the envelope/bag using tape. Plastic bags shall not be used.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Packaged shell casings shall have an evidence tag attached using tape, not staples.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Officers shall deposit properly packaged shell casings into the mailbox.

blocks.label: (f)
blocks.text: Officers shall also include a copy of the General Offense Report and Request for Analysis (TPD FORM 61.5) in the file folder located above the mailbox. Do not staple the report to the evidence collection envelope.
STORAGE/SECURITY
The Property Management Unit is responsible for intake of evidence and proper storage and accountability of all items submitted.

Only authorized sworn personnel shall have access to the Property Management Unit, the property evidence lockers in the Night Property Rooms and other storage facilities (e.g., Large Item Storage Area, Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage cabinet, Loaded Firearms Locker).

The Night Property Room at each district station shall be utilized to book all property and evidence that has come into police custody after normal Property Room hours, except where provided in Directive 304.1/6 – PROPERTY MANAGEMENT UNIT ROOM EXCEPTIONS.

Access to both the Safety Building Night Property Room and the Large Item Storage Area, located in the Police and Fire Alarm Building, is gained via use of the officer’s keycard. Keys for other Night Property Rooms and the Firearms Lockers contained in the Night Property Rooms are located at the district stations. The keys will be maintained at the desk of each respective station. Keys for the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Storage Cabinet and the cage inside the Large Item Storage Area will be maintained at the desk of the Safety Building. The key for the Loaded Firearms Locker will be stored at the desk of the Scott Park District Station.

Officers placing property in any of the Night Property Rooms, the Large Item Storage Area, the Flammable Liquids/Fireworks Cabinet, and Loaded Firearms Locker shall record the required information on the appropriate PROPERTY LOG (TPD FORM 23.19A, B, C, D, E and F) provided in these areas.

It shall be the responsibility of the Property Management Unit to provide a PROPERTY KEY LOG (TPD FORM 23.11A, B and C) at the desk of each district station for the use of the Night Property Rooms and other storage facilities.
It shall be the responsibility of each desk officer to maintain the PROPERTY KEY LOG.

Desk officers shall ensure the officers utilizing the Night Property Room or other storage facilities requiring the use of a key complete the entry on the PROPERTY KEY LOG and that the keys are promptly returned.
The desk officer shall note the time that the keys were returned in the space provided on the PROPERTY KEY LOG.
The Property Management Unit commander shall maintain the completed copies of the PROPERTY KEY LOGS and PROPERTY LOGS.

Evidence, found property, and safekeeping property stored in any Night Property Room shall be placed in lockers. Currency and drugs shall be placed in the Secure Mailbox. Only items that are too large to fit inside a locker may be stored on a shelf within a Night Property Room.

Blood or urine OVI evidence shall be placed in the Safety Building Night Property Room refrigerator. The sealed container shall be placed in one of the lock-boxes contained within the refrigerator. The lock-box key shall then be dropped into the secure container designated for that purpose.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: In addition, a completed Lucas County Coroner Forensic Toxicology Property Control Form shall be routed in this manner: original to Records Section, one copy with the evidence, and one copy in the OVI package, if applicable.

Items may only be removed from lockers by Property Management Unit personnel or by the district station shift commander (for purposes of consolidating evidence into a single locker). The shift commander shall make a notation on the PROPERTY LOG to indicate which lockers were affected by the consolidation.

When property in sealed containers is released to officers, detectives, or Forensic Lab personnel for court, examination or viewing, Property Management Unit personnel shall verify that a specific container was released to a specific officer. Property Management Unit personnel will not open and verify individual contents. It is the responsibility of the officer receiving the container to verify the contents and re-seal the container, if opened, before it is returned to the Property Room.
The officer receiving the property shall inventory packages signed out.
Discrepancies in any inventory shall be reported immediately.
DISPOSITION OF PROPERTY

It is the responsibility of every member of the department who takes custody of property to authorize disposal of that property in a prompt and efficient manner within the confines of the law and department regulations.
State law provides for the return of property only to the individual who furnishes evidence of ownership.
All other claims for found or abandoned property require an order from either Municipal or Common Pleas Court.

Every member of the department shall review the status of all property for which they have responsibility on an annual basis, or upon request from the Property Management Unit, to determine if it is necessary to retain that property as evidence.

Unless an investigator or specific investigative unit has been assigned to a case, or unless otherwise stated in this manual, the officer who originally took the property shall be responsible for its disposition.

It is the responsibility of that officer or assigned investigator to determine if an investigation is complete, all criminal court proceedings are complete, and all statutory regulations regarding preservation of evidence are followed.
The determination to release or otherwise dispose of an item may be made by the supervisor of the officer or assigned detective if he determines it is in the best interest of the department to do so.
Department personnel shall, as is practical, initiate a preliminary investigation to identify the owner and return found property.
Found property stored in the Property Room shall be disposed of in the following manner:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Held for a minimum of 30 days. Property Management Unit personnel will attempt to identify and contact the owner of the property.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Property shall be held an additional ten days if an owner has responded to a written notice.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Property shall be released only to a properly identified owner or other authorized person.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: If no owner is located within 30 days, the Property Management Unit commander shall complete a release and process the items according to law and current procedures.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: The officer who later determines that found property has evidentiary value shall contact Property Management Unit personnel to have the property’s status changed to evidence.

A Safekeeping tag indicates that an individual has a possessory interest in the property and that they have been notified by the receiving officer of where and when the property may be obtained from the Property Room. Normally, safekeeping property will be held for 30 days after which the Property Management Unit commander may begin disposal procedures in accordance with laws regarding abandoned property.
Firearms held as evidence in felony cases may only be released by the case investigator of record or an authorized supervisor from the Investigative Services Division.
Firearms held as evidence in misdemeanor cases, or for safekeeping, may only be released by the officer that originally seized the firearm or a supervisor in that officer's bureau or division.
Firearms submitted as found property shall be destroyed after 180 days unless notice is made in writing to the Property Management Unit to change the status of a specific firearm to evidence.

All property submitted as evidence, found property or safekeeping associated with a deceased person may only be released by the Coroner's Office. One exception exists pursuant to ORC 313.14/C if requested by the family and a deceased person’s firearm is not needed as evidence in a criminal prosecution, the department shall return the weapon to an individual that may legally possess it.
Officers or investigators shall use the Property Management Computer System, when available, on department computers to designate items for disposal.

When an item is to be released to an individual, officers or investigators approving the release must either provide a completed PROPERTY RELEASE to the Property Management Unit, with the name of the individual authorized to receive the property, or provide the appropriate release information electronically by using the Property Management Computer System.
NOTE: Officers shall not provide the completed PROPERTY RELEASE to the individual authorized to receive the property.

It is the responsibility of the investigating officer to notify the owner that a release for their property has been issued and the owner can pick up their property at the Property Room within 30 days.

If the owner has not picked up their property within 30 days after the property release is authorized, Property Management Unit personnel will consider the property as being held for safekeeping, and begin disposal procedures.
Property cannot be released to “Owner,” “Parents,” etc.; an individual’s name is required.
PROPERTY ROOM ALARM - SAFETY BUILDING
When the alarm system of the Property Room is activated, the following procedures shall be followed:

The Safety Building desk officer shall immediately notify Communications Bureau personnel, which shall dispatch units and a supervisor to the Safety Building. If there are any in-service officers available at the desk area, the desk officer shall immediately direct them to the Property Room.
Communications Bureau personnel shall also notify the Property Management Unit commander, or his designee, who shall immediately report to the Safety Building.
The following areas shall be checked by the responding units prior to the arrival of the Property Management Unit commander:
All exterior basement windows.
Basement-level door at the southeast corner of the garage.
Property Room hallway counter.
All hallway doors in the basement.
Once the doors and windows are found to be secure, officers shall maintain visual coverage of the entire perimeter until the Property Management Unit commander arrives, or until properly relieved.
The Property Management Unit commander shall coordinate the interior search, make the proper notifications, and complete an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0).
LARGE ITEM STORAGE AREA ALARM - POLICE AND FIRE ALARM BUILDING
When the alarm system of the Large Item Storage Area is activated, the following procedure shall be followed:
The first responding units shall thoroughly check the exterior of the building for any sign of entry or damage.
When appropriate to do so, responding officers shall enter the building via the Beech Street overhead door and check the entire garage area for any sign of entry or damage.
If there is no sign of intrusion or damage, the overhead door shall be secured and the appropriate disposition code provided to the dispatcher.

If damage has occurred or entry has been gained, Communications personnel shall immediately notify the Property Management Unit commander, or his designee, who shall immediately report to the Alarm Building.
The Property Management Unit commander shall coordinate the interior search, make the proper notifications, and complete an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT.
POLICE DEPARTMENT FACILITY SECURITY / KEYCARDS

All department employees have responsibility for the security of department facilities. Secure areas shall remain locked with access limited to only those with the proper security authorization, unless accompanied by a department employee. Department employees shall report any defective security equipment (e.g., malfunctioning locks, components of the electronic access control system) immediately to their supervisor. The supervisor shall ensure the department facilities remain secure and the proper notifications are made to rectify the situation.
Keycards will be issued to all permanent department employees and work in conjunction with the Electronic Access Control System to limit physical access to department facilities.

The Property Management Unit commander is responsible for the issuance, maintenance, and tracking of all keycards. In the event an employee’s keycard is lost or stolen, the employee shall immediately follow the procedures in Directive 303.2/6.3 – OFFICIAL EQUIPMENT; LOST, DAMAGED OR STOLEN and notify Property Management Unit personnel so the card can be disabled.
PROPERTY FOR ANALYSIS RECEIVED FROM OUTSIDE AGENCIES

Other police departments and agencies often request assistance from the Toledo Police Department in the analysis of property for evidentiary value. The Toledo Police Department will assist other agencies with these requests, when possible, and will ensure the chain of custody is maintained for all property coming into its possession. Upon completion of analysis, all property received shall be returned to the original agency.

The Computer Crimes Office shall be responsible for the custody of all evidence and/or other property coming into the possession of the Computer Crimes Office and shall be responsible for the safekeeping, accurate recording, accounting for and proper disposition of all such property.

The Crime Scene Investigations Unit shall be responsible for the custody of all evidence and/or other property coming into the possession of the Crime Scene Investigations Unit and shall be responsible for the safekeeping, accurate recording, accounting for and proper disposition of all such property.
PRESCRIPTION DRUG DROP-OFF

In an effort to combat prescription drug abuse, which sometimes leads to more serious addictions, the Toledo Police Department will anonymously receive, from citizens, prescription drugs which are in need of disposal.

Secured collection boxes to receive the prescription drugs have been placed at district stations. Citizens are able to deposit unwanted prescription drugs, anonymously, during regular business hours at district stations.
The Community Services Section has been provided portable secured collection boxes to have available at block watch meetings and other special events.

When complete, the Community Services Section officers shall secure the portable boxes for safekeeping in a night property room locker and record the information on the night property room log. The Community Services Section officers will not be required to complete a report; the Property Management Unit will complete the report once the portable boxes are emptied. The boxes will remain locked and accessible only to the Property Management Unit.
The Property Management Unit shall be responsible for the collection of the portable boxes and emptying district station collection boxes.
The prescription drugs will be collected on an ongoing basis.
The prescription drugs shall be weighed and an INCIDENT REPORT will be generated documenting the weight of the drugs.
The Property Management Unit shall dispose of the unwanted prescription drugs according to their established procedures.
Policy

Toledo Police Department maintains and constantly strives to improve its intra-department communications network to provide for rapid and efficient police response and to facilitate management control.
Definitions
A password that a user may assign within an application that prohibits other users from opening the secured application.

A computer and any related devices, whether connected or unconnected, including, but not limited to, data input, output, and storage devices, data communications links, computer programs, and data that makes the system capable of performing specified special purpose data processing tasks.

DEPARTMENT’S COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEM – The department’s communication system consists of the 800 MHz countywide radio system, Computer Aided Dispatching (CAD) system, Mobile Data Computers (MDCs), computers, telephones, fax machines, mail service and emerging technologies.

Electronic records or messages created, sent, forwarded, replied to, transmitted, stored, held, copied, downloaded, displayed, viewed, read, or printed by one or several electronic messaging systems or services.
Computer components that include processor, keyboard, monitor, printer, mouse, cables, connectors, adapters, telephones, and any other device attached to any component.
an in-vehicle mobile computer used for two-way electronic messaging, data retrieval and report writing.
A password that a user utilizes to gain access to a network.
A sequence of characters required for access to a computer system.
A password assigned to the hardware of a PC that prevents other users from starting the system.
Web sites that focus on building and reflecting social networks, or relationships between people who share similar interests or activities.
The Technical Services Section commander is responsible for the overall operation and maintenance of the department's computer system.
a device used for voice or data communications. This includes conventional telephones, cellular phones, smart phones and other emerging technologies.
Procedures
THE DEPARTMENT’S COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEM RESTRICTIONS
Toledo Police Department’s communications system is subject to the following:

The departmental communications system is restricted to the official business of the department and shall not be used for the purpose of disseminating commercial advertising, or for the purpose of promoting any commercial business interests unless authorized by the Chief of Police.

Only authorized employees shall make alterations, additions, removals and/or repairs to any portion of the department’s communications system. They shall not permit any unauthorized personal use of the system.

The 800 MHz countywide radio system is not a secure means of communicating. Any person with monitoring capabilities may overhear these conversations. Communications records all telephone and radio transmissions.

Communications made through the department’s communication system are not protected and are subject to discovery in criminal or civil matters or may be used in internal investigations. Therefore, communications should be considered public records, and employees should realize they have no expectation of privacy.
All communications are subject to department audit.
DEPARTMENT COMPUTERS

The Toledo Police Department utilizes a variety of computer systems in providing services to the community. Employees shall be trained in the use of applicable computer systems and shall exercise the utmost level of integrity with all computers and networks.
PURCHASING
When a need arises for the purchase of computer hardware or software, a REQUEST FOR EQUIPMENT, SUPPLIES, OR SERVICES (TPD FORM 6.7), must be completed.
After the appropriate commander has approved the request, the form shall be sent to the Technical Services Section.

The Technical Services Section commander shall review the form, attach a specification sheet, and record the date the form was received. The specifications sheet and the REQUEST FOR EQUIPMENT, SUPPLIES, OR SERVICES will then be delivered to the Secretary of Police, who will provide a requisition number, send a copy to the Technical Services Section for their records, and forward the originals to the city’s Department of Information and Communications Technology.
The Technical Services Section will track all computer-related requests to ensure they are resolved in a timely manner by the city's Department of Information and Communications Technology.
All questions regarding computer-related equipment by department personnel shall be directed to the Technical Services Section commander.

Department personnel should not contact the city's Department of Information and Communications Technology with requests or inquiries about computer-related orders, unless they are assigned to the Technical Services Section.

Department personnel shall not accept any newly ordered computer hardware or software from anyone but the Technical Services Section unless prior approval has been obtained. This does not include replacement equipment (equipment on loan) being brought in as repair of existing equipment.
RESTRICTIONS
Use of any personal computer (PC) or workstation for any purpose that violates any federal, state, or local laws is prohibited.

Personal use of department network computer workstations is discouraged. However, there may be legitimate uses for the network involving work that is reasonably relevant to the organizational mission and is therefore authorized.

Personal use of Northwest Ohio Regional Information System (NORIS), National Criminal Information Center (NCIC), Law Enforcement Automated Data System (LEADS), Ohio Law Enforcement Gateway (OHLEG), LexisNexis, intelligence, surveillance system or local file databases is strictly prohibited.
Unauthorized use of another employee's password is prohibited.
COMPUTER SOFTWARE

Computer software generally is a licensed product. The city purchases the right to use a computer program on a specified number of computers. The department respects all computer software copyrights- and adheres to the terms of software licenses.
The Technical Services Section shall maintain a list of authorized department software.
Department personnel shall not load or download any software on a department-owned computer without authorization from the Technical Services Section commander.
Department personnel shall not:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Duplicate any licensed software obtained for the department’s use. This section does not affect making backup copies of department files and software.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Install personally owned/licensed software on any city-owned equipment.
ELECTRONIC MESSAGING
Electronic messaging capability is intended solely for departmental business purposes.
Any electronic message that is sent through the network may be retrieved even though it may have been deleted from the assigned employee's computer.
All electronic messages shall be professional and courteous.
INTERNET SERVICES
Department members who access Internet services shall do so in compliance with the following:

Department personnel shall use the Internet and other communications in an appropriate and responsible manner. Employees shall only use the Internet for purposes that support the department’s mission. Employees shall not use the Internet for non-work-related purposes.

When communicating, employees shall use appropriate language. Profane, obscene, offensive or inflammatory language shall not be used. Employees shall notify the commander of the Technical Services Section of any threatening or unwelcome communications received.
Accessing pornographic or offensive materials is prohibited except for specific police investigatory purposes and shall require the prior written permission of a deputy chief.

Personnel shall adhere to copyright guidelines in the use of software, information, the attribution of authorship, and in the transmission or copying of text or files on the Internet or from other sources.
EMAIL

Email is a form of communication used by the department. Important information from the department is disseminated through email communication. Email is available to all department members through computers located at the stations, Mobile Data Computers (MDC’s) and through any device with web browsing capabilities.
All department personnel shall check their email, at least once daily, during regularly scheduled work days.
Department personnel shall delete unwanted emails to ensure the email mailbox does not become full.
Department personnel shall be cautious about opening emails from unknown senders to reduce the possibility of infecting the computer and/or network with a virus.
REPAIRS
The Technical Services Section is responsible for all maintenance, support, and repair of department computers.
Requests for service should be placed via the electronic link “Easy Button” located on the Toledo Police Intranet.

In an effort to assist Technical Services Section personnel in resolving computer problems, the person reporting a malfunction shall make every effort to describe the nature of the problem. Personnel reporting computer problems shall telephone or e-mail Technical Services Section personnel with the following information:
Date and time of occurrence.
The type of computer and function that was being utilized when the problem occurred.
Whether the problem can be duplicated on the same or another computer.
The nature of the problem (e.g., computer out of memory, network services not available, or the content of any message that appeared in a dialog box reporting an error).
AUDIT

The Technical Services Section shall ensure that network security measures/practices are in place to protect the integrity of the system. These may include passwords, access codes, or biometric devices used to access department resources.

The Technical Services Section shall ensure that an audit of the department’s security practices is conducted annually to include password complexity, lockout thresholds, lockout reset, password history, other access codes or mechanisms, and access violations.
MOBILE DATA COMPUTER (MDC)
MOBILE/FIELD USAGE

The driver of any vehicle equipped with an MDC shall not operate the MDC while the vehicle is in motion. One (1) man units shall stop the vehicle before attempting to access information. Lucas County Emergency Services is responsible for all maintenance, support and repair of MDCs.
DISPATCH
Officers will have available to them, through the MDC, all 9-1-1 information regarding their calls for service. However, for an indefinite period, all calls will continue to be voice dispatched.
Officers shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Verbally acknowledge the call as well as announce their arrival on scene.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Verbally advise the dispatcher when a change of location is necessary.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Verbally advise the dispatcher when placing themselves out of service on a self-initiated incident, such as a traffic stop.
The dispatcher will continue to enter all CAD data regarding traffic stops and other on-view incidents.
GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES
It shall be the assigned officer's responsibility to safeguard the MDC using every reasonable precaution available (i.e., locking the vehicle when unattended).

Officers shall log on to the mobile network computer system at the beginning of their shift. The dispatcher will be responsible for logging the officer off at the end of the shift. Officers shall NOT log themselves out of the MDC without first informing the dispatcher.

At the beginning of the shift, it shall be the responsibility of the driver of the vehicle to ensure that the MDC is functioning properly. If the MDC is found to be malfunctioning, a request for repair shall be initiated immediately. Repairs will be made during normal business hours, unless otherwise directed.
STORAGE/SECURITY

The Technical Services Section is responsible for the physical security of all assigned MDCs and for obtaining any required maintenance. Use of a department computer by anyone other than an authorized user is prohibited.
It shall be the assigned officer's responsibility to ensure the security of the MDC against unauthorized use.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: An officer shall not give out his password to any person, nor shall a password be left in any discernible written form in or near the MDC.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Officers may be required to disclose their password to a supervisor or support personnel for departmental purposes.
LAW ENFORCEMENT INFORMATION

Officers shall use the MDC to make all NORIS/LEADS/NCIC inquiries unless circumstances exist that make using the MDC impractical (e.g., running a shoplifter for warrants inside a shopping mall). Officers shall advise the dispatcher if they are with a subject and awaiting confirmation of a warrant.
By law, responses from NORIS/LEADS/NCIC inquiries are protected information.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Officers shall ensure that unauthorized persons do not view responses from these systems.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Officers shall not provide protected information to any unauthorized person.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Officers are not permitted to use these information systems for their own personal use, but only for official criminal justice purposes.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Officers shall not initiate any inquiry outside those purposes necessary to complete a departmental objective.
Non-public sources of information made available to law enforcement personnel shall not be accessed or utilized for non-law enforcement purposes.
TRAINING
It will be the responsibility of bureau/section commanders to ensure that all officers under their command maintain NORIS certification.
It will be the responsibility of the Technical Services Section commander to design and administer computer-training programs specific to the software loaded on the MDCs.
VIDEO PRODUCTION
Department personnel requesting a video production shall submit a VIDEO OFFICE WORK ORDER (TPD FORM 31.13) to the Video Office outlining the project and the date the video is needed.
The request should be submitted as early as possible to avoid conflicts with other scheduled projects.
The Video Office will schedule a planning meeting with the person requesting the project. The planning meeting will consist of:
Outlining the video project.
Determining the date and location of the video shoot.
Determining what additional equipment and/or personnel will be required.
Instruction regarding script development or review of existing script.
Completion of any release form that may be necessary.
Discussion of applicable copyright laws.

Scheduling of follow-up meetings for review of the project and finalization of script. Script content shall be carefully examined to insure accuracy and consistency with department policy, laws, and ordinances.

Once the video location and date of production have been set, and the content of the script has been approved, the Video Office will coordinate the set-up of the video equipment as well as direct the video crew, subjects, and actors.
After the video shoot has been completed, the Video Office will complete whatever post-production services are necessary. These services include:
Editing
Transferring the image (e.g., videotape, Compact Disc (CD), Digital Video Disc (DVD), other media)
Recording the narration
Video duplication
Labeling, packaging and distributing of the final video program
After the completion of all post-production services, the Video Office will schedule a final review of the project with the requesting person.
Prior to release, all projects must receive approval from the requesting employee’s bureau or division commander.
REQUEST FOR OUTGOING COMPUTER MESSAGE TRANSFERS

All requests for outgoing transfer messages (TWX) from the department to outside agencies shall be made in writing and must be approved by the requesting employee’s supervisor prior to being presented to a Records Section supervisor. The approving Records Section supervisor shall cause the message to be sent.
NOTE: This applies to computer transfer messages only, and in no way affects requests from police officers for routine stolen, wanted or registration checks with LEADS, NCIC, or BMV.
USE OF DEPARTMENT TELEPHONES
TELEPHONE COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE PUBLIC

The telephone is the primary method by which department services are requested. All incoming telephone calls must be answered as promptly as possible to determine if a need for police service exists and, if so, to provide the required service.
TELEPHONE COURTESY
A department employee, when answering or initiating telephones calls, shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Courteously greet the caller.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Identify themselves by title and name, the unit they represent in the department and ask to be of assistance.

Employees should make every reasonable attempt to either supply requested information or assistance, or to promptly refer the party to the proper department or other public or private agency for assistance. When making referrals, employees shall use all information available at their disposal.

When a department employee intends to transfer a call to another extension within the phone system, the caller shall be made aware of the employee’s intention to transfer the call and shall be given the telephone number and the name of the unit or section.
TELEPHONE CALLS; IMMEDIATE SERVICE REQUIRED
When a department employee receives a phone call that requires immediate police mobile response, the employee shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Obtain the location of the incident.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Obtain all other pertinent information regarding the incident.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Relay all information to Communications personnel.

The caller shall also be advised that Communications personnel will be notified of the incident. If the call is of a non-emergency nature, the caller shall be directed to contact Communications at 419-245-3340.
LONG DISTANCE TELEPHONE CALLS
Long distance telephone calls shall be placed on city phones for official business only.
USE OF PERSONAL TELEPHONES
The use of personal telephones by department personnel is authorized and subject to the following:
Any employee, while on-duty or acting in an official capacity, shall not wear any hands free telephone devices, unless authorized by a supervisor.
Officers should consider the tactical situations they may confront and place telephones on vibrate or silent while on-duty.

Employees shall not use telephones in place of conventional methods of police related communications (e.g., cellular phone calls or text messaging from one unit to another about criminal activity). The department’s communication system should be used for these purposes.

Employees shall not place outgoing or answer incoming telephone calls while engaged in any department business which requires personal or face-to-face contact with any citizen, unless the telephone call is directly related to police business.
Communications of a personal nature shall be kept at a minimum while on-duty and should be conducted out of public view.

Cellular phone calls, text messages, emails and other communications, made with personal telephones to conduct department business, may be subject to discovery in criminal or civil matters or may be used in internal investigations. Therefore, these communications should be considered public records and employees should have no expectation of privacy.
EMPLOYEE CONDUCT

Images, video, audio files, or any other information obtained from the police department, during or outside the course of duty, shall not be posted, displayed, shared, or otherwise made available directly or on a blog, website, file transfer protocol server (FTP), mass storage device, or any other method of dissemination without permission of the Chief of Police, except as necessary in the performance of official duties. Employees must obtain prior approval from the Chief of Police to develop a Web page or to create a bulletin board (blog) that relates to the Toledo Police Department.

While on or off-duty, officers shall not take graphic, illicit, or compromising photographs, videos, or audio recordings of law enforcement activities (i.e., crime scenes, arrests, etc.) for personal use without the approval of the Chief of Police.
SOCIAL NETWORKING WEB SITES
Employees who use these types of web sites should ensure that they in no way represent themselves as Toledo Police officers.
No sensitive, classified, sexually explicit, or racially insensitive postings shall be made.
No posting that divulges sensitive information, discloses the identities of undercover officers or brings embarrassment or discredit to the Toledo Police Department shall be made.
No photographs of police vehicles, logos, uniforms, or facilities shall be posted or shown on these web sites.
ACCESSING SOCIAL NETWORKS ON CITY OWNED EQUIPMENT

Department employees shall not access social networking websites (e.g., Facebook, Twitter, MySpace) from City owned computers, unless access is directly related to employee’s duties. Permission from a supervisor is required prior to any employee accessing these types of web sites.
Policy

It is the policy of the Toledo Police Department to ensure the protection of Criminal Justice Information (CJI) and non-public media until such time as the information is either released to the public via authorized dissemination (e.g., Freedom of Information Act requests, within a court system, or when presented in crime report data), or is purged or destroyed in accordance with applicable record retention rules.

The Media Protection Policy was developed using the FBI Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Security Policy. The Toledo Police Department shall comply with the most current version of the FBI Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Security Policy and any state-specific CJIS Systems Agency (CSA) requirements. All personnel, contractors, and supporting entities with access to CJI shall adhere to CJIS administrative, technical, and physical safeguards requirements.
Definitions
Refers to tangible materials used to store or transmit data and content. This includes printed documents and imagery that contain CJI.

Any means by which information is communicated or expressed, including text, audio, video, or graphics, encoded in machine-readable formats and created, viewed, distributed, or modified on electronic devices. This includes memory devices in laptops and computers (hard drives) and any removable, transportable memory media, such as magnetic tape or disk, backup media, optical disk, flash drives, external hard drives, memory cards, or live monitoring.

A physically secure location is a facility, an area, a room, or a group of rooms within a facility with physical and personnel security controls sufficient to protect CJI, associated information systems, and non-public media. The perimeter of the physically secure location shall be prominently posted and separated from non-secure locations by physical controls. Security perimeters shall be defined, controlled, and secured. Restricted non-public areas in the Toledo Police Department shall be identified with a sign at the entrance.

A visitor is defined as a person who visits any Toledo Police Department facility on a temporary basis, who is not employed by the Toledo Police Department and has no unescorted access to physically secure locations within a Toledo Police Department facility where CJI, non-public media, and associated information systems are located.

Physical media owned by any entity other than the Toledo Police Department, or devices contracted to assist with the functions of the Toledo Police Department. This includes personal devices such as cellular phones, tablets, laptops, and other devices with similar capabilities.

Data that is not available to the general public and used for criminal investigations, identification, and intelligence. CJI includes Criminal History Record Information (CHRI), biometric data, identity history data, property data, case/incident history, and any information derived from FBI CJIS systems.

Physical or electronic media containing Toledo Police Department information that is not authorized for public release. Non-public media includes audio or video recordings, live monitoring, electronic files, and other department information for which access is restricted to authorized personnel.
Individuals with current training, credentials, and authorization from the Chief of Police to access media, a secure location, or some other restricted entity.

The designated individual responsible for ensuring the agency complies with FBI Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Security Policy requirements. LASOs manage access to sensitive criminal data, ensuring only authorized personnel use agency systems, and act as the primary liaison with state security authorities.
Dictates that users, systems, and applications are granted only the minimum access rights necessary to perform their specific tasks in order to minimize security risks.
A framework that implements security by assigning permissions based on job roles rather than individual users, ensuring efficient, standardized, and secure access management.

Authorized personnel who accompany a visitor at all times while the visitor is within a physically secure location to ensure the protection and integrity of the physically secure location and any CJI and non-public media therein.
Procedures
MEDIA STORAGE AND ACCESS

Controls shall be in place to protect electronic and physical media containing criminal justice information (CJI) and non-public media while at rest, stored, or actively being accessed. Only authorized personnel shall access CJI, non-public media, or secure locations. Non-public media and CJI shall only be used for law enforcement purposes. To protect CJI and non-public media, Toledo Police Department personnel shall:
Securely store electronic and physical media within a physically secure or controlled area. A secured area includes, but is not limited to, a locked drawer, cabinet, or room.
Properly protect any individually issued keys, proximity cards, computer account passwords, and other access credentials.
Restrict access to electronic and physical media to authorized individuals.
Ensure that only authorized users remove printed forms or electronic media containing CJI or non-public media.

Physically protect CJI or non-public media until the media reaches end of life. End-oflife media containing CJI or non-public media shall be destroyed or sanitized using approved equipment, techniques, and procedures in accordance with CJIS Security Policy media sanitization standards (e.g., NIST SP 800-88 or successor guidance). Sanitization methods shall be appropriate to the type of media and documented.

Personnel shall not use personally owned information systems or devices to access, process, store, or transmit CJI or non-public media unless authorized by the Chief of Police or designee, and only when all safeguards in this directive are in place. Any authorized personally owned device accessing CJI or non-public media shall:
Utilize CJIS-compliant encryption for CJI or non-public media at rest and in transit.
Store CJI or non-public media locally unless specifically authorized.
Require multi-factor authentication.
Be configured with department-approved security controls.
Be subject to remote wipe capability where feasible.
Be documented and approved by the LASO. The LASO shall maintain documentation of approved devices. Documentation shall include device identification, approval date, and applicable security controls.
Personnel shall not utilize publicly accessible computers to access, process, store, or transmit CJI or non-public media.

Store all hardcopy CJI or non-public media printouts maintained by the Toledo Police Department in a secure area accessible to only those employees whose job functions require them to handle such documents.
Safeguard all CJI and non-public media within the Toledo Police Department against possible misuse.
Take appropriate action when in possession of CJI and non-public media while not in a secure area:
CJI and non-public media shall not leave the employee’s immediate control. CJI and non-public media printouts shall not be left unsupervised while physical controls are not in place.

Precautions must be taken to obscure CJI and non-public media from public view, such as by means of an opaque file folder or envelope for hard copy printouts. While using electronic devices such as laptops, a session lock or privacy screen shall be used. CJI and non-public media shall not be left in plain public view.

When CJI or non-public media is electronically transmitted or stored outside the boundary of the physically secure location, the data shall be encrypted using FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules, or a successor standard, in accordance with CJIS Security Policy.

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Storage devices include external hard drives from computers, printers, and copiers used with CJI or non-public media. Storage devices also include thumb drives, flash drives, back-up tapes, mobile devices, laptops, etc.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Encryption keys shall be properly managed, stored separately from encrypted data where applicable, and access shall be restricted to authorized personnel.

Lock or log off computers when not in the immediate vicinity of the work area to protect CJI and non-public media. The agency shall enforce automatic session lock after a period of inactivity consistent with CJIS requirements. Access permissions shall be granted on a need-to-know basis. Personnel without a work-related need to access the data shall not have access to the information.
Access to CJI and non-public media systems shall require unique user identification and authentication. Shared accounts are prohibited.
Establish appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to ensure the security and confidentiality of CJI and non-public media.

Systems accessing, processing, or storing CJI and non-public media shall generate and retain audit logs sufficient to reconstruct events related to CJI and non-public media access, modification, dissemination, and deletion.
Audit logs shall be reviewed periodically in accordance with CJIS policy and retained consistent with CJIS retention requirements.
Access permissions shall be reviewed at least annually and upon role change or termination.
Access to live monitoring or recordings from privately owned cameras may be granted to department personnel through express consent or via legal processes.
Personnel assigned to the Training Section, or personnel assisting the Training Section, may utilize non-public media if needed and relevant to the scope of the training.
MEDIA TRANSPORT

Controls shall be in place to protect electronic and physical media containing CJI or non-public media while in transport (physically moved from one location to another) to prevent inadvertent or inappropriate disclosure and use. Dissemination to another agency is authorized under the following circumstances:
The other agency is an Authorized Recipient of such information and is being assisted by the accessing agency, or
The other agency is performing personnel and appointment functions for criminal justice employment applicants. The Toledo Police Department personnel shall:
Protect and control electronic and physical media during transport outside of controlled areas.

Restrict the pickup, receipt, transfer, and delivery of such media to authorized personnel. Toledo Police Department personnel will control, protect, and secure electronic and physical media during transport from public disclosure by:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: When CJI or non-public media is transported electronically outside a physically secure location, encryption meeting CJIS standards shall be used.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Use of privacy statements in electronic and paper documents.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Limiting the collection, disclosure, sharing, and use of CJI and nonpublic media to law enforcement purposes only.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Following the least privilege and role-based rules for allowing access. Limit access to CJI and non-public media to only those people or roles that require access.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Securing hand-carried confidential electronic and paper documents. When mailed or shipped, the agency must document procedures and only release to authorized individuals. Packages containing CJI or nonpublic media material that are mailed shall NOT be marked “Confidential.” Packages containing CJI or non-public media material shall be sent by methods that provide for complete shipment tracking, history, and signature confirmation of delivery.
Hand-carried electronic media shall remain under the physical control of authorized personnel at all times.
Chain-of-custody documentation shall be maintained for transported media containing CJI or non-public media.

Personnel shall not take CJI or non-public media home or take it while traveling unless authorized by the Toledo Police Department. When disposing of confidential documents, use a shredder or a document destruction service.
LOSS OF INFORMATION OR ACCESS; PERSONNEL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

If CJI or non-public media is improperly disclosed, lost, or reported as not received, or another security concern is discovered including facility access violations, loss of CJI or non-public media, loss of laptops, cell phones, thumb drives, CDs/DVDs and printouts containing CJI, or if CJI or non-public media has been improperly accessed, the following procedures shall be followed:

Personnel shall immediately notify their supervisor upon discovery of the incident. Report loss of issued keys, proximity cards, etc. to the on-duty supervisor, or the employee’s direct supervisor if the assigned bureau/section/unit has restricted hours.
A report must be completed and submitted. The submitted report shall contain a detailed account of the incident, events leading to the incident, and steps taken in response to the incident.
Report any security incidents involving CJI to the Toledo Police Department’s LASO immediately and in accordance with CJIS Security Policy incident reporting requirements.
LOSS OF INFORMATION OR ACCESS; SUPERVISOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Upon being informed that an individual under the supervisor’s responsibility has been involved in a situation where CJI or non-public media has been improperly accessed, disclosed, lost, or reported as not received, or another security concern is discovered, including facility access violations, loss of CJI or non-public media, loss of laptops, cell phones, thumb drives, CDs/DVDs and printouts containing CJI, the following procedures shall be followed:

Make arrangements to have authorized credentials resecured, such as a proximity card deactivated, door locks possibly re-keyed, passwords reset as necessary, or take steps to prohibit improper access to CJI or non-public media.

Ensure a satisfactory report is filed and that communication is made regarding the situation to the LASO. The LASO shall notify the Information Security Officer (ISO), CJIS Systems Agency, and/or FBI CJIS Division in accordance with CJIS Security Policy incident response timelines.
If appropriate, a Departmental Investigative Form (DIF) shall be completed.
VISITORS; PERSONNEL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The responsibility for the visitor procedure rests with the employee allowing access or continued access to the facility. Personnel physically allowing the visitor into the secured area accept responsibility for that individual, and either pass the responsibility to another Toledo Police Department employee, or remain with the visitor until the visitor exits the secure area. Toledo Police Department personnel shall ensure visitors comply with the following:

All visitors must complete the visitor access log before entering a physically secure location by listing their name, their agency, purpose for the visit, date of visit, time of arrival, and name and section of the person visited. Time of departure must be noted upon departure.
The visitor will be screened by Toledo Police Department personnel for weapons. No weapons are allowed in the agency except when carried by personnel authorized by the Chief of Police or designee.

All visitors in secure areas must be accompanied by a Toledo Police Department visitor escort at all times, including delivery or service personnel. Visitor escort personnel shall ensure visitors do not access CJI systems, non-public media, or view CJI unless authorized and properly screened in accordance with CJIS policy. The use of cameras or other electronic means used to monitor a physically secure location does not constitute an escort.

The visitor will be screened for electronic devices. Personal electronic devices may not be used in any secure area within the agency facility except when authorized by the Chief of Police or designee. Personnel shall ensure visitors are not permitted to enter a secure area with electronic devices, including cameras and mobile devices, unless approved by the Toledo Police Department Local Area Security Officer (LASO). Photographs are not allowed unless the command officer responsible for the area grants permission.
The visitor must show Toledo Police Department personnel a valid form of photo identification.
Visitors must adhere to Toledo Police Department policy for authorized unescorted access.

Noncriminal Justice Agency (NCJA) personnel (e.g., city information technology worker) who require frequent unescorted access to restricted areas will be required to establish a Management Control Agreement between the Toledo Police Department and the NCJA. Each NCJA employee with CJI or non-public media access will have a state and national fingerprint-based record check prior to being granted access to the restricted area.

Private contractors/vendors who require frequent unescorted access to restricted areas will be required to establish a Security Addendum between the Toledo Police Department and each private contractor or vendor. Private contractor or vendor personnel will have a state and national fingerprint-based record check prior to being granted access to the restricted area.
Personnel shall ensure visitors are not permitted to view screen information.

Individuals not having any legitimate business in a restricted area shall be escorted to a public area of the facility. Individuals in physically secure areas without an escort shall be stopped. If resistance or behavior of a threatening or suspicious nature is encountered, sworn personnel shall be notified.
Visitors shall not be allowed to sponsor another visitor.

Escort personnel will confirm the visitor is not leaving the building with any agencyowned equipment or sensitive data prior to the visitor’s departure. All Toledo Police Department personnel and supporting entities are responsible for reporting any unauthorized physical and electronic access, by either visitors or department personnel, to the Toledo Police Department through the chain of command.

All requests by groups for tours of the Toledo Police Department facility will be referred to the proper agency point of contact for scheduling. Visitor rules apply for each visitor within the group. The group leader will provide a list of names to the proper agency point of contact.
Escort personnel are responsible for properly evacuating visitors in cases of emergency.
AUTHORIZED PHYSICAL ACCESS

Only authorized personnel will have access to physically secure non-public locations. The Toledo Police Department will maintain a list of authorized personnel. The agency will implement access controls and monitoring of physically secure areas to protect all transmission and display media of CJI and non-public media. Authorized personnel will take necessary steps to prevent and protect the agency from physical and electronic breaches.

Department personnel shall use only the appropriate door for entry to and exit from the Toledo Police Department buildings and secure areas within those buildings, and shall use marked, alarmed emergency exits only in emergency situations.

Department personnel shall ensure the perimeter security door securely locks after entry or departure. No perimeter door shall be propped open. Unauthorized individuals shall not be permitted to enter after the perimeter door has been opened for an authorized purpose.
All personnel with CJI and non-public media access shall meet the minimum personnel screening requirements prior to being granted access.

To verify identification, a state of residency check and national fingerprintbased record check shall be conducted prior to assignment for all personnel who have unescorted access to CJI and non-public media and those who have direct responsibility to configure and maintain computer systems and networks with direct access to CJI and non-public media. Personnel shall be re-screened in accordance with state and CJIS requirements.

Support personnel, private contractors/vendors, and custodial workers with access to physically secure locations or controlled areas during CJI and nonpublic media processing shall be subject to a state and national fingerprintbased record check unless these individuals are escorted by authorized personnel at all times.
Any subsequent arrest or disqualifying event shall be reported in accordance with CJIS policy.

Employees shall keep appropriate Toledo Police Department personnel informed when CJI or non-public media access is no longer needed. In the event of termination of employment, the individual must surrender all property and access credentials managed by the local agency, state, and/or federal agencies.
All authorized personnel shall complete security awareness training.

All authorized Toledo Police Department personnel, Noncriminal Justice Agencies (NCJA) personnel such as city IT employees, and private contractor or vendor personnel will receive security awareness training prior to initial assignment and annually as required by the CJIS Systems Agency.
Security awareness training will cover areas specified in the CJIS Security Policy, at a minimum.
Policy

There are circumstances in which detainees are not immediately transported to a permanent detention facility. There are also situations when interviews may turn into interrogations, thereby suspects become detainees. In these instances, the department utilizes Temporary Detention Rooms and Temporary Detention Areas to safely secure detainees before transport to a permanent detention facility.
Definitions
Any individual coming into contact with agency personnel (e.g., citizen, traffic violator not in custody, mental patient not in custody).
Any individual whose actions cause a citizen or agency personnel to believe that they are involved or have been involved in criminal activity.

Any individual in the custody of agency personnel, and whose freedom of movement is at the will of agency personnel (e.g., arrestee, person in custody, mental patient in custody because he is absent without leave [AWOL] from a medical facility), including status offenders.
A single handcuff securely attached to a bench or seat which is attached to the chain or hinge of a detainee’s handcuffs, securing the detainee to the bench/seat.
A secure area designed and designated by a sign to confine detainees for short periods of time (e.g., secure area with walls and/or partitions specifically used to confine detainees).
A room designed and designated by a sign to confine detainees for short periods of time (e.g., secure rooms specifically used to confine detainees).
A room designed and designated by a sign for officers to conduct interviews and interrogations.
A room designed and designated by a sign for officers to conduct polygraph examinations.

A juvenile who has committed a crime that would not be a crime if committed by an adult (e.g., runaway, curfew, underage drinking, tobacco use, truant, unruly). A status offender in the custody of agency personnel, and whose freedom of movement is at the will of agency personnel is a detainee.

EXCEPTION: If the juvenile is arrested for a status offense and criminal offense, which is not a status offense (e.g., resisting arrest, assault, disorderly conduct), the juvenile is not considered a status offender.
Procedures
RESPONSIBILITY FOR DETAINEES
OFFICER'S RESPONSIBILITY

Whenever an officer has responsibility for a detainee, the officer shall exercise the utmost precaution to keep the detainee from escaping, injuring himself or others, and/or destroying any items of evidentiary value.

Transporting officers shall be responsible for the safety and welfare of the detainee at all times. Transporting officers shall maintain continual supervision and control of the detainee unless specifically excused by a sworn supervisor or investigator handling the case.
The relieving authority shall verbally notify the officer that he has been temporarily excused and shall advise him when to return.
Once properly relieved, the responsibility for the detainee transfers to the relieving officer/investigator.
When custody of a detainee is transferred to another officer, the officer accepting responsibility for the detainee shall properly search the detainee for weapons or other contraband.
TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOMS/TEMPORARY DETENTION AREAS
PHYSICAL CONDITIONS OF TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOMS AND TEMPORARY

DETENTION AREAS Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas shall be designated with a sign stating the room/area is a Temporary Detention Room/Area. Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas shall be free of objects that can be thrown, misused, or used as a weapon.
Benches shall be securely fastened to the floor.
Handcuff detainment devices shall be constructed and installed to securely hold a handcuffed detainee.

Doors to Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas shall remain closed and locked whenever a detainee is in the room/area, unless an officer is present in the Temporary Detention Room/Area (e.g., doors may remain open and unlocked when an officer is placing a detainee in or removing a detainee from the room/area).
GENERAL GUIDELINES FOR USE OF TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOMS/TEMPORARY

DETENTION AREAS Any officer may utilize a Temporary Detention Room/Area to temporarily secure a detainee. Officers shall use Temporary Detention Rooms, if available. Temporary Detention Areas shall only be used if all Temporary Detention Rooms are occupied or otherwise unavailable for use. Officers utilizing the Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas shall adhere to the following guidelines.
EXCEPTION: Juvenile Status offenders shall NOT be brought to a police facility.

Officers shall record the use of a Temporary Detention Room/Area by making the appropriate entries on the TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOM/AREA LOG (TPD FORM 15.29) maintained in a logbook at each Temporary Detention Room/Area.
Each time a detainee is placed in or removed from a Temporary Detention Room/Area, for any reason, the time in and out shall be recorded on the TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOM/AREA LOG.
Any meals provided to a detainee shall be recorded on the TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOM/AREA LOG.
The Operations Division commander, or his designee, shall maintain the completed TEMPORARY DETENTION ROOM/AREA LOGS.
Officers shall inspect the Temporary Detention Room/Area for weapons, contraband, or unsafe conditions prior to placing a detainee in the room/area and immediately after removing the detainee.

Prior to placing a detainee into a Temporary Detention Room/Area, officers shall remove all property from the detainee. The property shall be placed in one (1) of the property lockers provided near each Temporary Detention Room/Area. Officers shall secure the locker and maintain possession of the property locker key until the property transfers with the detainee.

Weapons, contraband or evidence shall be handled in accordance with existing procedures. All other property shall transfer with the detainee when they are transported to another facility or released from custody.

While in a Temporary Detention Room/Area, all detainees shall be handcuffed to a handcuff detainment device to ensure detainee safety, prevent escape, and to prevent damage to Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas.

The proper handcuffing technique to secure a detainee to a handcuff detention device is both hands handcuffed together behind the back with the operable portion of the handcuff detention device attached around the chain or hinge portion of the detainee’s handcuffs.
If another detention device is used instead of a handcuff detention device, officers shall ensure that both of the detainee’s hands remain handcuffed behind the back.
Males, females and juveniles shall be separated into different detention rooms/areas.
Juveniles shall be kept sight and sound separated from all adult offenders.
Officers shall keep their detainee under continual supervision using CCTV monitors and conducting visual checks, at least every 30 minutes, or as conditions warrant.
Officers shall remain alert for possible indications of medical problems, suicide attempts, escape attempts or other potentially harmful events that may occur.
In areas where a Temporary Detention Room/Area is not available, detainees shall be properly handcuffed and shall remain under continual supervision and control.
Generally, detainees shall only be held in Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas for as long as necessary and shall be transported to a permanent detention facility as soon as practical.
SECURITY MEASURES

Officers shall secure all firearms before entering a Temporary Detention Room/Area with a detainee, or before entering a Temporary Detention Room/Area that contains a detainee. Officers shall secure their firearms in one
of the gun lockers installed near the Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas. Officers should also consider securing other potentially harmful weapons prior to entering a Temporary Detention Room/Area.
Some Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas are equipped with duress alarms. Officers may utilize a duress alarm or the emergency button on a portable radio to summon assistance.

Only authorized personnel (e.g., police personnel) shall be permitted in Temporary Detention Rooms/Areas or to have access to detainees. Other individuals, such as attorneys and family members, will have access to a detainee after the detainee is booked into a permanent detention facility.

Officers shall allow reasonable water and restroom breaks for their detainees. Officers shall keep in mind the circumstances, the length of the temporary detention, and any security risk involved in removing handcuffs to allow a detainee to use restroom facilities. If there is any doubt on the part of the officer, a sworn supervisor or investigator shall decide what action to take.

blocks.label: (a)
