OPERATIONS DIVISION SUPERVISOR’S RESPONSIBILITIES
The operations division supervisor shall ensure the on-duty Investigations Bureau supervisor has been notified.
INVESTIGATIONS BUREAU SUPERVISOR’S RESPONSIBILITIES

When the on-duty Investigations Bureau supervisor receives information that a missing person may be endangered and the criteria for an Endangered Missing Adult Alert have been met, he shall immediately:
Notify the on-duty Records Section supervisor and provide range for the alert.
Ensure that surrounding law enforcement agencies are notified and prepare a poster to be distributed to agencies and media in areas where the endangered adult might be recovered.
If the adult is recovered, notify the on-duty Records Section supervisor to cancel the alert.
POLICE RECORDS CLERK RESPONSIBILITIES
When a police records clerk receives information that a missing person may be endangered he shall immediately:
Enter the missing person into NORIS/LEADS/NCIC using the Endangered Missing Adult Alert formatted entry.
Provide information to Records Section Supervisor when complete.
RECORDS SECTION SUPERVISOR’S RESPONSIBILITIES
When the on-duty Records Section supervisor receives information that a missing person may be endangered and the criteria for an Endangered Missing Adult Alert have been met, he shall immediately:
Send an administrative message containing circumstances of Endangered Missing Adult Alert to agencies in the range of the alert.
Provide the Ohio Attorney General’s office information and circumstances regarding the endangered missing including range of alert.
If the adult is recovered, cancel the LEADS Endangered Missing Adult Alert and provide recovery information to the Ohio Attorney General’s office.
Policy

When in accordance with certain procedures, Ohio law provides that a parent who deserts a child less than thirty days old does not commit any criminal offense in the state of Ohio and may not be subjected to criminal prosecution for deserting the child. This is codified under Ohio Revised Code Sections 2151.3515 through 2151.3530. The primary concern of this order is the safety and well-being of the surrendered child.
Procedures

ACCEPTANCE OF NEWBORN – While acting in an official capacity, officers shall take possession of any infant child who appears to be 30 days old or younger when presented with same by a person who either expresses intent to surrender the child, or fails to indicate intent to return for the child.
Officers shall immediately examine the child for indication of abuse or neglect.

Unless there is indication of abuse or neglect, no officer shall in any way attempt to identify or detain the person who has voluntarily surrendered the infant into his custody, nor shall he attempt to persuade the person not to desert the child. If there is apparent indication of abuse or neglect, this section does not apply and the officer shall take appropriate enforcement action.

Absent evidence of abuse or neglect, the officer shall ask for medical information about the child and the child’s parents from the person presenting the child. This information shall be entered on a SAFE HAVEN FOR NEWBORNS - MEDICAL HISTORY (TPD FORM 18.1) form.

Provision of this information by the person surrendering the child is completely voluntary and may be declined in total, provided in part, or the form may be taken by the person for submission at a later date.

The officer shall also provide information materials describing services available for parents and newborns. The acceptance or rejection of this material is completely at the discretion of the person surrendering the child.
TREATMENT OF NEWBORN AND REPORTING
Having received a surrendered infant, the officer shall immediately notify the dispatcher and request an EMS unit capable of transporting the infant to a medical facility for examination.
The officer shall also proceed to the medical facility, ensuring the Investigations Bureau and the Lucas County Department of Children’s Services are notified.

The officer shall remain at the medical facility until relieved by either a representative of the Investigations Bureau or Children’s Services, and shall provide same with a copy of the completed INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 38.12) detailing all the circumstances associated with the incident.

The responding investigator shall verify with hospital personnel whether there is indication of abuse or neglect of the child. If there are indications of abuse or neglect, the investigator shall initiate the criminal investigation. Absent indication of abuse or neglect, the investigator shall complete a supplemental report regarding the results of the hospital examination and shall insure that Children’s Services receives copies of all reports.
Officers shall use all available information to complete a SAFE HAVEN FOR NEWBORNS - MEDICAL HISTORY form, and the family services information card furnished by the Children’s Advocacy Center.

A 24-hour “hotline” has been established and operated by the Children’s Advocacy Center for the purpose of counseling and disseminating information to interested persons regarding the provisions of this law.
Policy

Since the department is decentralized through district stations, sub-stations and neighborhood offices, there are many accesses for the public to seek out an officer for assistance. Many of these walk-in complaints are to make out a report or report a crime. The following procedures shall be adhered to for handling citizens who indicate in some form or another they are being stalked, harassed or menaced in any way and that the suspect may be in the immediate area.
Procedures
WALK-IN COMPLAINT

When a citizen comes into a department facility to report a crime of stalking, menacing, domestic violence or similar crime, the reporting clerk/officer shall determine as quickly as possible if the suspect is in the immediate area.
If so, the clerk/officer shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Notify Communications of the situation and all pertinent information, including suspect description and vehicle description, if applicable.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Contact Records for a warrant check on the suspect and for possible vehicle description.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Ask the victim to stay until a unit arrives at the facility or apprehends the suspect.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Communications will enter a mask (priority two) and dispatch a unit to the area to look for the suspect or ask units if one is available to assist in the area.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: The dispatched unit shall search the area for the suspect.
If found, the unit shall inquire through Communications to the initiating clerk/officer to determine if the suspect has any warrants or if there is further information they need to know.

If the suspect is not found, or if found and not booked, the dispatched unit shall report to the originating clerk's/officer's location to determine if the victim needs an escort home or further assistance.

In no instance shall the original reporting clerk/officer leave his area to check for the suspect or escort the victim to any location if he is a clerk, on light duty status, or is not wearing the prescribed soft body armor. If the officer does leave his assigned area, he shall notify Communications of that fact.
Policy

Consistent with the department's policy of using only the level of force that is objectively reasonable to control or otherwise subdue violent or potentially violent individuals, the use of the TASER by trained personnel is authorized. The primary purpose for employing the TASER is to save human lives. Use of the TASER is authorized when it reasonably appears that an attempt to use other less-lethal options would endanger the safety of the subject, the officer, or any bystander in the area. It is not intended to be used as a general substitute for other less-lethal options that could be effectively utilized.
Definitions
CEW – Conducted Electrical Weapon
The TASER 7 is a two-shot CEW that is designed to provide the operator the capability to immediately follow-up ineffective shots with an additional cartridge deployment without reloading.

The TASER 7 cartridges are available in two different types for duty use; the 3.5 degree cartridge (stand-off cartridge - optimal range of 11-23 feet) or the 12 degree cartridge (QC cartridge -optimal range of 4-8 feet).
TASER 7 battery is rechargeable and serves as the device’s power source and a storage device that stores and transfers firing data to Evidence.com when docked.
Procedures
USE OF THE TASER
Use of the TASER shall be consistent with its placement in the Response to Resistance Continuum as detailed in Directive 103.2/1 – GUIDELINES FOR RESPONSE TO RESISTANCE.

The TASER may be used to control a dangerous or violent subject when deadly physical force does not appear to be justified and/or necessary; or attempts to subdue the subject by other conventional tactics have been, or will likely be, ineffective in the situation at hand; or there is reasonable expectation that it will be unsafe for officers to approach within contact range of the subject.

When dealing with exhausted individuals or persons exhibiting symptoms of distress or agitated/excited delirium, once officers engage in apprehension procedures, it is important to minimize the duration of the physical struggle. These subjects are at significant risk of arrest-related death. Immediate medical attention may reduce this risk.
Examples of situations in which the TASER may be used include, but are not limited to:
Dealing with mentally ill subjects who are perceived to be violent.
Armed subjects.
Warrant service where the subject is perceived to be violent.
Violent persons under the influence of drugs and/or alcohol.
Persons expressing the intent and having the means to commit suicide.
The primary risk of serious injury or death during CEW deployment occurs when the subject falls. Except in situations where the use of deadly force would be justified, the TASER shall not be used:
On any subject who may have been contaminated with combustible liquids.

When it is reasonable to believe that incapacitation of the subject may result in serious injury or death due to his physical location, such as on a ladder, roof, elevated platform, or in water more than several inches deep (potential for drowning).
On individuals who are in control of a motor vehicle.
On any detainee who is handcuffed, unless exigent, aggravated circumstances exist. The circumstances include, but are not limited to:
The subject being uncontrollable due to size and/or physical ability.
The subject poses an immediate threat of bodily harm to the officer, himself, or others present.
Subject has mobility and has escaped physical custody and is placing themselves or others in extreme peril.
On any juvenile who is known to the officer to be, or appears to be under the age of 13.
On any elderly person who is known to the officer to be, or appears to be over age 70.
On any woman who is known to the officer to be, or appears to be pregnant.
Other limitations of TASER use:

Officers shall not use the TASER in proximity to flammable gases, blasting materials, or any other highly combustible material (e.g., gasoline, natural gas, propane, meth labs) that may be ignited by use of the device.

A suspect or detainee shall only be exposed to the TASER for the minimum number of times required to gain control; however, no subject shall be exposed to the TASER more than three times unless exigent circumstances present a substantial risk of physical injury to the officer or to a suspect who has exhibited overly assaultive behavior. The officer shall articulate the exigent circumstance in the appropriate reports.

No suspect or detainee shall be exposed to the TASER by more than one officer at the same time. If simultaneous deployment occurs, the officers shall immediately communicate with each other and one of the TASERs shall be turned off.

Any detainee or suspect who has been exposed to the TASER shall be evaluated by hospital staff. EMS shall be summoned to the scene in accordance with subsections SWORN SUPERVISOR REPSONSIBILITIES WHEN TASER UTILIZED or in any other circumstances of serious injury.
The TASER shall not be pointed at any individual unless the officer involved reasonably believes it will be necessary to use the device.
The TASER shall not be treated as a toy, nor shall it be employed or utilized in horseplay.
DEPLOYMENTS OF TASERS
TASERs shall be issued to, and used only by, officers who have demonstrated proficiency in the use of the TASER.

The Training Section shall have certified instructors conduct annual refresher training to all officers who are certified to use the TASER. Any officer who fails to meet the proficiency standards shall receive remedial training.
TASERs shall be carried in approved holsters on the support side.
TASERs may be individually issued to officers as part of their official equipment or issued on a temporary basis from a pool of spare TASERs.

The preferred target areas are below the neck area for back shots and the lower center mass (below chest or heart area) for front shots. By lowering the point of aim to the lower torso on the front of the body by about four inches, the potential for Neuro-Muscular Incapacitation of the core muscles is often increased by splitting the belt line (one probe above the belt line the other below the belt line) of the body and targeting larger muscle groups.

Avoid intentionally targeting the CEW on sensitive areas of the body such as the head, throat, breast, chest or area of the heart, genitals, or known pre-existing injury areas without legal justification.
Preferred Target Area in Green
The TASER 7 may be used by officers to display a “warning arc” as a method of deployment. A RESPONSE TO RESISTANCE REPORT shall be completed.
Only properly functioning department-issued TASERs and smart cartridges shall be carried in the field.
TASERs issued from a pool shall only be issued to qualified officers specifically designated by the section commander or his designee.
The sworn supervisor issuing a TASER unit shall ensure that it includes two smart cartridges.
TASERs issued from a pool shall be appropriately logged on the TASER LOG – POOL ISSUED (TPD FORM 15.12).

All TASERs (individually issued and issued from a pool) shall be tested for readiness at the start of each shift. This readiness testing shall be conducted as part of the roll call procedure. The testing shall be conducted as follows:
TASER 7

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Remove the TASER 7 from the holster

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Ensure that the safety switch is in the down (SAFE) position

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: TASER 7 is to be put in the test mode.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: TASER 7 – Check the remaining battery life percentage on the CID Central Information Display). Replace the battery if the percentage is less than 20%. Place the TASER 7 battery in the charging dock if the battery shows low battery, or every 30 days, whichever comes first.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Depress one of the two arc buttons and perform the spark test for A FULL FIVE SECONDS. Check for visible spark between the electrodes and a rapid spark rate.

blocks.label: (f)
blocks.text: Check for any fault icons (in the upper right hand corner of CID) If there is a fault icon, forward the TASER to the TASER Coordinator in an interdepartment envelope with a SUPERVISORS REPORT (TPD FORM 20.7) detailing the issue. The TPPM or battery shall be left installed in the TASER and tape applied over the safety before placing it in an inter-department envelope. Place the safety switch in the down (SAFE) position. a. Take each smart cartridge out of the TASER and inspect them for cracks, damage, or missing blast doors. If there is damage, forward the cartridge to the TASER coordinator and take out a new cartridge from the district’s spare pool. b. Correctly replace the smart cartridges in the TASER. c. When instructed by a sworn supervisor, the officer shall then point the TASER 7 in a safe direction (usually toward the floor) and place the safety in the up (FIRE) position. d. The officer shall check to see if both cartridges are correctly communicating with the TASER 7.

blocks.label: (g)
blocks.text: All other TASERS discharges shall continue to be documented as described in Directive 401.21/3 – OFFICER RESPONSIBILITIES WHEN TASER UTILIZED

blocks.label: (h)
blocks.text: Should the TASER 7 not perform satisfactorily or fails, due to a mechanical issue, forward the TASER to the TASER Coordinator in an inter-department envelope with a SUPERVISOR’S REPORT detailing the issue. The TPPM or battery shall be left installed in the TASER and tape applied over the safety before placing it in an inter-department envelope.

Officers shall only use department issued TASERs, smart cartridges, holsters and accessories. No other parts or accessories may be used. The only exception is the alternate TASER holster as outlined in Directive 303.2/7.9.4 –UNIFORMS AND EQUIPMENT – TASER HOLSTERS.
OFFICER RESPONSIBILITIES WHEN TASER UTILIZED
Request the response of a sworn supervisor.
The officer shall advise the sworn supervisor that a subject has been exposed to a CEW and relate the approximate time the action occurred.
Treat persons who have been subjected to the TASER, or the probes, as follows:
Officers shall wear latex gloves when removing the probes from the skin. Sanitizing gel or spray shall be administered to each puncture site along with a Band-Aid (if needed) as soon as practical.

If the barbed shaft is embedded so deep as to prevent the probe from hanging loosely, or if the probe struck the subject in the head, groin, or woman's breast, the probe shall NOT be removed. EMS shall be summoned to examine the person and make a determination as to treatment. The person shall also be evaluated by hospital staff.
All other medical considerations shall utilize the procedures outlined in Directive 103.2/6 - RENDERING MEDICAL AID AFTER USE OF FORCE.
The smart cartridge and probes used shall be tagged and placed into evidence as follows:
As the probes may be contaminated with blood, they shall be handled only while wearing latex gloves. See Directive 401.12 – COMMUNICABLE DISEASES AND CONTAMINATION for biohazard precautions.

The probes shall be placed back into the smart cartridge portals - pointed end first, and secured within the smart cartridge. The wires shall then be loosely collected, NOT wound around the cartridge, and the entire used cartridge, probes and wires shall be placed in a large sharps tube with end caps affixed Standard evidentiary booking procedures shall then apply.
The serial numbers of both the TASER 7 and the expended cartridge(s) shall be recorded in the crime report.
TASER discharges shall be documented as follows:

Discharges involving a person or animal, (whether intentional or accidental, warning arc, and whether hit or miss), require the completion of a RESPONSE TO RESISTANCE REPORT. Careful attention shall be paid to the description of any subject injury - both initial and secondary, and the circumstances surrounding the use of the TASER.
SWORN SUPERVISOR RESPONSIBILITIES WHEN TASER UTILIZED
Respond to the scene where the TASER has been utilized.
Summon EMS to administer emergency medical care, if needed and make sure the person is evaluated by hospital personnel.

Determine the need for photographs in the event of an unusual injury either from probe penetration or of a secondary injury. Processing of the photographs shall be according to the procedures outlined in Directive 407.1/5 – DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPH.

Ensure that officers who use the TASER complete a RESPONSE TO RESISTANCE. The report must indicate if the device was used as the warning arc, with the probes, as a drive stun (physical contact), or both; and how many times the subject was exposed.

Conduct a follow-up investigation of the incident, carefully documenting any secondary injuries to the subject by completing the factual narrative portion of the supervisor review in the reporting system.
The TASER 7 used in the incident shall be downloaded via the unit’s docked battery, with the information retrieved from Evidence.com, as follows:

The activation times recorded on the printout shall be examined and labeled appropriately. The test conducted at the beginning of the shift shall be labeled "Shift Test.” The actual field use of the unit - including the number of times it was fired shall be labeled "Field Use." The post-use test conducted by the sworn supervisor shall be labeled "Supervisor Test."
The sworn supervisor shall then sign and date the printout.
The printout shall be attached to the completed RESPONSE TO RESISTANCE REPORT AND forwarded as noted in Directive 103.2/5.3 – ROUTING.
Removed

summary: Revised October 2026. The TASER sits in the yellow band of the Response to Resistance Continuum (103.2) and is for dangerous or violent subjects when deadly force is not justified, conventional tactics have failed or will fail, or it is unsafe to close to contact range. The directive says plainly it is **not a general substitute** for other less-lethal options that would work.

The real risk is the fall. That is why the prohibited list is about position and vulnerability: elevated locations, water, moving vehicles, combustibles, handcuffed detainees, kids under 13, adults over 70, and pregnant women, all barred unless deadly force would be justified.
Every exposure brings a supervisor to the scene, a hospital evaluation, a Response to Resistance Report, and the cartridge booked as evidence.
must: Carry the TASER in an approved holster on your support side, and use only department-issued units, smart cartridges, holsters and accessories (2.1.2, 2.5)

Spark test it at roll call every shift: safety down, test mode, battery above 20 percent, a full five-second arc, check for fault icons, inspect both cartridges, then confirm both cartridges communicate with the unit when the supervisor says so (2.4)
Aim low center mass on front shots (about four inches lower, splitting the belt line) and below the neck on back shots (2.1.4)
Minimize the struggle with exhausted, distressed or excited delirium subjects; they are at significant risk of arrest-related death, and fast medical attention reduces it (1.1)
Request a sworn supervisor after any exposure and tell them a CEW was used and about what time (3.1)
Get every exposed person evaluated by hospital staff (1.4)
Wear latex gloves to remove probes, sanitize each puncture site, and apply a Band-Aid if needed (3.2.1)
Leave the probe in and call EMS if it is embedded too deep to hang loosely, or if it struck the head, groin or a woman's breast (3.2.2)

Book the cartridge: probes back in the cartridge portals point first, wires gathered loosely and not wound around the cartridge, everything in a large sharps tube with end caps, then standard evidence procedure (3.3.2)
Record the serial numbers of the TASER and the expended cartridges in the Crime Report (3.4)

Complete a Response to Resistance Report for any discharge involving a person or animal, intentional or accidental, hit or miss, including a warning arc, stating whether it was arc, probes, drive stun or both and how many exposures (3.5.1, 4.2)
Articulate the exigent circumstances in your reports any time you exceed three exposures or use the TASER on a handcuffed detainee (1.2.4, 1.3.2)
never: Use the TASER, unless deadly force would be justified, on someone who may be contaminated with combustible liquid, who could be seriously hurt by falling from a ladder, roof or platform or into water more than a few inches deep, who is in control of a motor vehicle, who appears under 13 or over 70, or who appears pregnant (1.2)

Use it on a handcuffed detainee, except in exigent, aggravated circumstances: uncontrollable due to size or ability, an immediate threat of bodily harm, or an escaped detainee putting people in extreme peril (1.2.4)
Fire it near flammable gases, blasting materials, gasoline, natural gas, propane or meth labs (1.3.1)
Expose a subject more than three times without exigent circumstances presenting a substantial risk of injury, and never use more than the minimum needed for control (1.3.2)
Deploy on the same person at the same time as another officer; if it happens, communicate immediately and one unit goes off (1.3.3)
Point it at anyone unless you reasonably believe you will need to use it, and never treat it as a toy or use it in horseplay (1.5, 1.5.1)
Intentionally target the head, throat, breast, chest or heart area, genitals, or a known pre-existing injury without legal justification (2.1.5)
notes: Authorized examples: violent mentally ill subjects, armed subjects, warrant service on a violent subject, violent intoxicated persons, and suicidal persons with intent and means (1.1.1)
The TASER 7 is two-shot with no reload between cartridges. Stand-off cartridge (3.5 degree) is optimal at 11 to 23 feet; close quarters cartridge (12 degree) at 4 to 8 feet (Definitions)
A warning arc is a deployment and gets a Response to Resistance Report (2.1.6)

The supervisor responds, summons EMS if needed, decides on photographs of unusual injuries, downloads the unit through Evidence.com, labels the activations Shift Test, Field Use and Supervisor Test, signs the printout and attaches it to the report (4)
Pool TASERs go only to qualified officers designated by the section commander, with two cartridges, logged on TPD 15.12 (2.3)
A faulty unit goes to the TASER Coordinator in an interdepartment envelope with a Supervisor's Report, battery left in and tape over the safety (2.4.1f, h)

blocks.text: Policy

It is essential that all law enforcement officers understand their role and responsibilities, as well as the inherent dangers involved, when responding to robberies of banks and financial institutions. Therefore, when responding to robbery alarms at these establishments, officers shall follow the procedures set forth in this policy in order to enhance the potential for an arrest and observe proper precautions for the safety of officers, employees and bystanders.
Procedures
RESPONDING UNITS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
Observe and note any suspicious vehicles leaving the area, or persons in close proximity of the bank.

The first unit on scene shall serve as the Primary Unit, establishing a position of cover/concealment that provides maximum observation of the front of the facility. The primary unit shall direct additional responding units until relieved by a supervisor.
The primary unit or supervisor shall direct additional units to establish a perimeter around the facility.

Once a perimeter has been established and no notification of a “false alarm” has been received, the primary unit or the supervisor shall have the dispatcher telephone the facility. When the call is made, the dispatcher shall determine the following and advise the units at the scene:
If the robbery is still “in progress”.
If the suspect(s) has left the facility.

Should responding units arrive while the robbery is still in progress, UNLESS OTHERWISE DIRECTED, OFFICERS SHALL WAIT FOR THE SUSPECT(S) TO EXIT THE FACILITY BEFORE ATTEMPTING AN APPREHENSION. This procedure reduces the likelihood of creating a hostage situation.

When a robbery has occurred, the crime scene shall be secured and protected for processing by SIU technicians. Responding officers and detectives shall be directed away from entry/exit points used by the suspect(s).
DOOR PLACARDS

Immediately following an actual robbery at a bank where the perpetrator has fled, it is bank policy to place a fluorescent orange diamond-shaped sign in a conspicuous place on the outermost door of the bank. It will read “OFFICE TEMPORARILY CLOSED.”
In the event of an unwarranted alarm, officers should be greeted upon their arrival outside the bank by a bank official carrying a plain fluorescent green placard and bank credentials.
Officers arriving at the scene of a hold-up alarm who find neither a green nor an orange placard must consider the following scenarios:
It is a good robbery and the perpetrator(s) is still inside.
It is a false alarm and bank employees are not aware of it.
Officers must not rely on the placard system 100% and maintain cover until the status of the incident has been verified.
Policy
Gang related activity has detrimental effects on society. It is the policy of the department to provide efficient, quality law enforcement services to the community to address gang related activity.
Procedures
GANG RELATED ACTIVITY

If a crime is gang related, department personnel are instructed to contact the Gang Task Force Section supervisor by radio or by phone. If the Gang Task Force Section supervisor cannot be immediately contacted, a SERGEANT’S REPORT (TPD FORM 20.7) shall be sent to the Gang Task Force Section supervisor.

Any department member receiving information linking a crime to gang activity shall include in the CRIME REPORT (TPD FORM 38.1) all information relevant to such activity, checking the “GANGS” box under “Notify Agency” in ReportWISE or circling box #6 "Gang Related," on the face of the CRIME REPORT.

Any member of this department acquiring knowledge of gang related activity that does not require a crime report shall complete a GANG INFORMATION REPORT SHEET (TPD FORM 70.4) and forward it to the Gang Task Force Section.

Department personnel shall limit their collection and processing of information regarding membership in a gang to that which identifies: a person's criminal activity; threat of criminal activity; gang related activity as defined in this section; or activity that otherwise presents a threat to the community and can be associated with a gang.

A direct admission of gang involvement by a subject shall cause his inclusion in the Gang Intelligence File. Lacking an admission, the Gang Task Force Section will analyze the information and consider whether it meets their criteria for inclusion in the database. Generally, a person identified as demonstrating two or more of the characteristics listed in this directive will be entered into the database or have their file updated.
Removed
Indicators of gang related activity can include the following:

CRIMINAL ACTIVITY involving a gang related modus operandi. Examples of such activity include: drive-by shootings, assaults, robberies, carjackings, gang fights, menacing, drug offenses, criminal damaging or vandalism, especially if gang graffiti is used.

ASSOCIATION with a known gang member as determined through personal observations or as verified by other law enforcement personnel, members of the court, school, probation, correctional, and/or parole officials.
TATTOOS of gang logos or symbols observed and verified by law enforcement, court, school, probation, correctional, and/or parole officials.

CLOTHING & JEWELRY known to be a sign of gang membership or worn in a manner so as to indicate affiliation with a gang. (e.g., one pant leg rolled up, belt buckle worn off center, gang colors, gang insignia, gang pins, medallions, belt buckles, etc.)
POSSESSION OF GANG RELATED MATERIAL such as writings or other paraphernalia.
Policy

The Canine Unit provides specially-trained canine teams charged with the responsibility to successfully fulfill the needs of the Toledo Police Department by assisting patrol, narcotic, SWAT officers and detectives in crime suppression through criminal apprehension and evidence recovery. The Canine Unit provides expertise to accomplish tasks such as building searches, area searches, evidence searches, subject tracking, criminal apprehension, and narcotics and/or explosives detection.
Definitions
A working-class or service dog which has been procured and specifically trained to execute a number of specific tasks which makes use of the canine’s speed, agility, and sense of smell.
CANINE OFFICER or HANDLER – A police officer who has been specifically trained in the care, handling, and training of a police service dog.
A police officer and his/her assigned canine.
A group of officers assigned / trained in the handling of canines.
A vehicle utilized and equipped to transport a police canine.
Procedures
Removed. Formerly definitions.
REQUEST FOR CANINE TEAM

Any department member requesting the use of a canine team shall contact Communications via the air and provide the nature of the request. A Canine Handler shall advise Communications when responding to an incident or request.
If a request for the services of a canine team is not fulfilled, the requesting department member shall be advised.
REQUEST FOR OFF DUTY CANINE TEAM

If there are no canine teams on duty, Communications shall contact the Canine Unit Supervisor and explain the nature of the request for a canine team. The Canine Unit Supervisor shall determine if canine team response is necessary.
If a request is unable to be fulfilled, the requesting department member shall be advised.
MUTUAL AID REQUESTS
When a request is received from an outside agency for canine team assistance, Communications shall broadcast for any available canine team.
The Canine Unit Supervisor or the respective shift’s Watch Commander shall be advised of the request and shall determine if the request will be accommodated.

The Canine Handler has the final decision regarding the deployment of the canine. If the handler determines that a canine should not be deployed, the canine handler shall notify the requesting agency and advise them of the reason for the refusal.
CANINE RESPONSE

Canine teams shall patrol in modified, specially-equipped vehicles designated for such duty and will be clearly marked "K-9 UNIT". The canine teams shall respond to calls for service throughout the city and when not engaged in canine activity shall assist their shift’s patrol officers.
The following are designated for canine team response (this is not an all-inclusive list):

To assist in locating any suspect involved in a felony and/or misdemeanor crime (excluding minor misdemeanors), where the suspect has fled on foot and a possible tracking/area search mission has developed.
Absent a chargeable offense described above, mere flight from pursuing officers shall not justify the deployment of a canine.
Locating lost persons and/or victims in natural disasters.
Search for evidence or contraband including narcotics or explosives.
Vehicle Searches
Building Searches
The canine handler shall notify Communications of his/her intent to respond to any specific call for service.
Officers shall not approach or touch the Canine without permission from the canine handler.
APPREHENSION

Canine handlers may utilize only that force reasonably necessary to effectively subdue and maintain custody and control of a suspect. Handlers must consider the totality of the circumstances known to them when considering the use of their canines. Canine handlers shall utilize reasonable means to affect suspect apprehension without the suspect incurring a canine bite. Any situation in which a deployed canine bites a person shall be considered a use of force. The ACTION-RESPONSE REPORT, TPD FORM 29.3, shall be completed by the canine handler for all canine-bite incidents.
Handlers shall not utilize the canine in bite situations for misdemeanants who do not pose an immediate threat to officers and/or citizens.
Canine teams shall be deployed and utilized only for tasks in which they have received departmental training.

Before deploying the canine to make a physical seizure, the handler shall consider the severity of the crime, whether the suspect poses an immediate threat to officers or citizens, and whether the suspect is actively resisting or attempting to evade arrest by hiding or fleeing. Prior to releasing the canine, and throughout the deployment of the canine, the handler will ensure that: a) Upon the immediate release of the canine, the canine handler will attempt to notify Communications that their canine is deployed on an apprehension. b) There are no citizens present who will be endangered by the release of the canine. c) A verbal warning will be given twice by the handler prior to releasing the canine, unless exigent circumstances exists that would endanger the handler and/or officers by doing so. This warning will give notice that the canine will be released if instructions are not followed to stop, surrender, and/or reveal themselves. d) The canine handler must maintain visual contact with the canine throughout the pursuit. In the event visual contact is about to be lost, the handler will immediately recall the canine. e) If the suspect surrenders prior to contact, the handler will immediately recall the canine. f) Handlers will appraise each situation and make a decision whether to deploy their canine based upon their training, current law, and department policy regarding Action-Response.
BUILDING SEARCHES

Canine teams will be trained in searching buildings for persons attempting to avoid apprehension. When it is determined that an intruder may be present, the outside perimeter should be secured. No officers shall enter the building until the canine team arrives. Only the canine team and one back-up officer shall enter the building. Deviation from this policy is permitted only with the approval of the canine handler.

The canine handler will verbally alert the person(s) inside the building. This warning will include notice of the presence of the police and its intent to release a police canine in the building if instructions are not followed for persons to surrender and/or reveal themselves. Warnings shall be made at least (2) two separate times to provide the person(s) an opportunity to surrender and/or reveal themselves. Adequate time shall be given for a response to the warnings. If the person inside the dwelling refuses to respond or surrender, the canine shall be released to search the building.

The decision to allow the canine to search on or off leash will be left to the discretion of the canine officer, and will be dependent upon existing conditions. The handler should be cognizant of the environment (i.e., environmental and geographical hazards, etc.) prior to taking the canine off-leash. The handler shall always consider officer safety, the severity of the crime under investigation, and the possibility that an innocent person(s) may come into contact with the canine while the canine is offleash.
AREA SEARCHES AND SUSPECT TRACKING
Searching a specific outdoor area may be useful in the apprehension of a suspect when their physical presence has been detected.
During area searches and tracking of suspects, patrol units should secure a perimeter and attempt to clear unauthorized persons from the area to be searched.

Verbal warning shall be given periodically during the search unless exigent circumstances exists that would endanger the handler and/or other officers. One officer may accompany the canine team as back-up and cover. Deviation from this policy is permitted only with the approval of the canine handler.

Patrol units shall not enter the established perimeter unless ordered to do so by an Operations Division supervisor. The backup officer will keep perimeter units updated with their location and provide direction of the tracking by radio communication. This will allow the perimeter units to move accordingly in an effort to keep the perimeter secure. All officers having contact with the deployed canine shall maintain their perimeter until the canine is under the control of the canine handler.
VEHICLE SEARCHES

The use of a canine team for narcotics detection in vehicles is a valuable tool in drug enforcement. The canine's ability to alert on a narcotic is directly related to the availability of the scent and the proficiency of the canine.

The canine handler shall be responsible for ensuring that narcotics detection is initiated and performed safely. No detection operations shall occur if the canine handler has deemed the area to be unsafe.

It shall be the responsibility of the requesting officer or back-up officer(s) to maintain observation of the vehicle’s operator and occupants. The canine handler must be attentive to the canine during narcotics detection.
All vehicle occupants shall be removed prior to the canine’s entering a vehicle’s interior.

When the canine enters a vehicle’s interior for narcotics detection, the officer that requested the canine shall take custody of any narcotics, contraband or paraphernalia found by the canine and immediately advise the canine handler of its location.

It shall be the responsibility of the requesting officer to determine if an arrest will be made and to ensure that any evidence/contraband is booked per department guidelines in the Property Management Unit.
Policy

In order to increase transparency and officer safety, the Toledo Police Department equips patrol and limited marked vehicles with In-Car Video Camera Systems (ICVCS) to capture both video and audio recordings of citizen interactions. The recordings serve to document officer/civilian contacts, arrests, and critical incidents, as well as to enhance the accuracy of reports and court testimony.
Definitions

DVR – A Digital Video Recorder (DVR) is a component of the ICVCS that stores video/audio recordings. USB – Universal Serial Bus (USB) is an industry standard that defines cables, connectors and communication protocols used for connection, communication, and power supply between computers and electronic devices.
A USB flash-drive issued to officers that contains officer specific log-in information required for the L3 ICVCS.
Procedures
GENERAL GUIDELINES
Officers operating a police vehicle equipped with an ICVCS shall record both the video and audio portions of the following:
All motor vehicle stops.
Foot and vehicle pursuits.
Investigative stops of pedestrians.
Any transport of detainees or civilians.
Major incidents where evidentiary video may be captured (i.e., potentially fatal or fatal accidents, structure fires, homicide or shooting scenes, etc.)
All officers, regardless of when they arrive on scene or if they were dispatched to the scene, shall ensure that incidents requiring activation are recorded on their vehicle’s ICVCS.

Officers may record other incidents they feel may be of importance (i.e., planned enforcement activities, erratic driving, suspicious activity, conditions at a crime or accident scene, audio of conversations of individuals seated in the police car, etc.).
Supervisors who believe that a recorded incident may have administrative or investigatory value shall notify their district commander as soon as practicable.
Video recordings generated by the department are subject to public records law. Public records requests shall be handled according to procedures in DIRECTIVE 302.1/2.1
RELEASE OF DEPARTMENT RECORDS.
No in-car video recording, disk, file, or copy thereof shall be shown or released to an outside entity without prior approval of the district commander.
Under no circumstances shall a DVR be removed from a vehicle, unless requested by the Chief’s Office or Technical Services Unit.
All officers shall be trained in the proper use of the ICVCS prior to operating the system.
START-OF-SHIFT VEHICLE INSPECTIONS
Prior to the beginning of a shift, officers assigned to a vehicle that is equipped with an ICVCS shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Inspect the ICVCS for physical damage, unplugged cables, or missing equipment. A supervisor shall be immediately notified of problems.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Start the police vehicle. (The ICVCS will power on.)

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: If applicable, utilize the USB key issued to the officer to log into the ICVCS by inserting it into the USB port of the DVR, on the radio/emergency lights console. Any USB key that is lost or damaged shall be immediately reported to a supervisor, who shall properly address the situation, per DIRECTIVE 303.2/6.3 – OFFICIAL EQUIPMENT; LOST, DAMAGED OR STOLEN. Position and adjust the camera to record each incident.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Ensure that the wireless microphone or BWC is turned on and properly synced with the system.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Conduct a test recording. The test recording shall be classified as Test/Other. Play the recording back to ensure that the camera is adjusted properly to record incidents and that the interior and wireless microphones are recording. If the ICVCS is not functioning properly, a supervisor shall be notified immediately and the issue noted on the VEHICLE INSPECTION SLIP (TPD FORM 15.2).
RECORDING INCIDENTS
While recording an incident, officers shall:

Ensure the ICVCS is recording until the incident is complete, even upon the demand of an involved party to stop recording. This includes the placement and removal of detainees from secured areas of police vehicles.
Inform those who ask, that the audio/video recording equipment is actively recording.
Removed.
Immediately contact a supervisor when experiencing recording problems, or when the DVR is full.
POST RECORDING; CLASSIFICATION
When an incident has concluded, the ICVCS should be deactivated. The video shall be classified by selecting one of the following classifications:
Classifications:
Test/Other – for camera tests, Code 3 runs, and non-evidentiary transports.
Traffic Stop – no arrest.
Arrest/Evidence.
Suspect Stop – for field interviews, etc.
Pursuits
Removed

Re-Classification: If an ICVCS video is incorrectly labeled, a supervisor shall be notified. Re-classification can be conducted by the officer’s supervisor, the officer, or the assigned investigator. If assistance is needed, a help ticket may be submitted to Technical Services, via the TPD INTRANET’s “Technical Service Help Ticket” icon.

If an officer feels that a recorded incident may have training value, a SUPERVISORS REPORT (TPD FORM 20.7) shall be forwarded to the Technical Services Unit stating the officer’s name, ID number, and the date and time of the incident. A brief description of the incident shall be included in the report. Technical Services shall forward the recorded incident to the Training Section.
END-OF-SHIFT
At the end of an officer’s shift, the officer shall log out of the ICVCS.
SUPERVISORS; RESPONSIBILITIES
DAMAGE TO ICVCS

Supervisors shall arrange for repair of the system by submitting a help ticket to Technical Services, via the TPD Intranet’s “Technical Service Help Ticket” icon. An UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0) shall also be completed by the referring supervisor and forwarded to the district commander and the Administrative Services Bureau Commander.
Any noticeable damage or tampering discovered shall be followed up by supervisors, and, if necessary, a department investigation shall be initiated.
REPAIR OF ICVCS
The day shift watch commander or designee shall coordinate the repair of ICVCS components with the Technical Services Unit.
Before a vehicle is sent out for repair, the Technical Services Unit shall be contacted to review the problem and ensure that repair is necessary.
PURSUITS
All available in-car video shall be reviewed and utilized as part of any pursuit investigation.

Supervisors shall document in the narrative of the VEHICLE PURSUIT FORM in the department’s management system whether an ICVCS was present in the vehicle and whether it was activated during the incident as required.
ACTION RESPONSE
All applicable recordings shall be reviewed and utilized as part of any action response investigation for report accuracy.
CRITICAL INCIDENTS
If an officer is involved in a critical incident, the supervisor shall classify it as Arrest/Evidence and document it in a supplemental report.
SUPERVISORY REVIEW - COMPLIANCE WITH POLICY AND PROCEDURES
Supervisors are permitted to review footage to ensure compliance with ICVCS policies and procedures. This includes, but is not limited to, the following:
When officers are the subject of a complaint or a pattern of allegations of misconduct.
When recordings are evidentiary or investigatory in nature.
For training purposes.
In response to public records requests.
When officers are in their probationary period or with a field training officer.

As a condition of an Early Intervention System (EIS) Plan of Action, the review shall be documented on the monthly EARLY INTERVENTION OBSERVATION REPORT (See Directive 103.11/7.2.1 – PLAN OF ACTION SPECIAL PROVISIONS) and on the VIDEO REVIEW LOG (TPD FORM 23.29).
EVIDENTIARY HANDLING
When a significant event is recorded on an ICVCS, officers shall classify the video, per DIRECTIVE 401.25/4 POST RECORDING; CLASSIFICATION.
When it is determined that a recorded incident may be of administrative or evidentiary value, officers shall classify the video as “Arrest/Evidence” and notify a supervisor.
The supervisor shall review the video segment to determine if the video is of administrative or evidentiary value.
Removed.
Removed.

DVD video transfers shall be requested via a TOLEDO POLICE VIDEO OFFICE WORK ORDER (TPD FORM 31.13) and shall include the incident’s date, time, and involved officers. The form shall then be forwarded to the Video Unit for processing.

Unauthorized copying of any video segment from a DVR is prohibited. The Video Office shall perform all video analysis and/or duplication services. Requests for all video analysis and/or duplication services shall be made using the TOLEDO POLICE VIDEO OFFICE WORK ORDER.
MAINTENANCE; SECURITY
Digital recordings shall be retained according to the Records Retention Schedule.

Officer access to in-car camera system video shall be obtained through the TPD Intranet. Officers are authorized to view recordings captured on their in-car camera and other officers’ in-car cameras only for official purposes, including preparing a report, courtroom preparation, official training, furtherance of an ongoing investigation, or when completing assigned tasks such as redaction of a public records request. A supervisor may grant access to another officer’s in-car camera recordings.

Supervisors shall access in-car camera recordings only for official purposes, including those previously listed, as well as supervisory incident review and required audits. Non-sworn employees assigned to duties which require access to footage shall view incar camera footage only for official purposes.
QUARTERLY AUDITS BY ACCREDITATION UNIT

Personnel from the Accreditation Unit shall randomly review a minimum of five recordings quarterly to ensure compliance with departmental policies and procedures. The reviews shall be recorded on the Video Review Log and stored in the Planning, Research and Inspections Section.
TRAINING
Officers shall receive initial training on the use of the in-car video camera system while in the academy.
Policy

In order to increase transparency and officer safety, the Toledo Police Department equips officers with body worn cameras (BWCs) to capture both video and audio recordings of citizen interactions. The recordings serve to document officer/civilian contacts, arrests, and critical incidents as well as enhance accuracy of reports and court testimony.
Procedures
GENERAL GUIDELINES
The BWC is considered personal equipment and is the responsibility of the officer to whom it is issued. Only officers who have completed approved training shall be issued a BWC.
The BWC will be part of the department annual equipment inventory that is conducted in April.
Officers issued a BWC shall wear the device at all times while on-duty and while working off-duty in a law enforcement capacity.

Officers not issued a camera shall sign a BWC out from the Central or Scott Park District Station before they begin working an off-duty project. If a BWC is not available for sign out, the on-duty watch commander shall be notified immediately. At the conclusion of the off-duty project, officers shall immediately return the BWC to the district station where the BWC was obtained. A supervisor shall be notified if video needs to be uploaded. The BWC shall not be re-issued until the video transfer is complete.
Officers issued a BWC shall record the following while on-duty and while working offduty in a law enforcement capacity:
All motor vehicle stops
Investigative stops of pedestrians
Dispatched calls for service involving interaction with citizens

On-view incidents requiring enforcement activity and/or major incidents where evidentiary video may be captured (i.e., potentially fatal or fatal accidents, structure fires, homicide or shooting scenes, etc.)
Suspect and witness statements/interviews
Foot and vehicle pursuits
These requirements apply to all officers that arrive on the scene of one of the above listed incidents regardless of when they arrive or if they were dispatched to the incident.
Officers may record other incidents they feel may be of importance (i.e., erratic driving, suspicious activity, conditions at a crime or accident scene, etc.).
Supervisors believing that a recorded incident may have administrative or investigatory value shall notify their district commander as soon as practical.

Officers shall wear only department issued BWCs. BWC equipment and all data, images, video, and metadata captured, recorded, or otherwise produced by the equipment is the sole property of the department.

Video recordings generated by the department are subject to public records law. Public records requests shall be handled according to procedures in DIRECTIVE 302.1/2.1 – RELEASE OF DEPARTMENT RECORDS.

Officers are authorized to view recordings captured on their BWC and other officers’ BWCs only for official purposes, including preparing a report, courtroom preparation, official training, furthering an ongoing investigation, or completing assigned tasks such as the redaction of public records requests. A supervisor may grant an officer access to another officer’s BWC recordings. Supervisors shall access BWC recordings only for official purposes, including those previously listed, as well as supervisory incident review and required audits. Non-sworn employees assigned to duties that require access to BWC footage shall view the footage only for official purposes.

Except with the prior approval of the chief of police or to satisfy a public records request, no BWC recording, disk, file, or copy thereof shall be shown or released to an outside individual or entity.
START-OF-SHIFT INSPECTION
Prior to the beginning of a shift, officers who have been issued a BWC shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Inspect the BWC system for physical damage and immediately notify a supervisor if damage is discovered.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Affix the BWC on the outer most garment of the uniform and position it vertically at, or slightly above the shirt pockets.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Prior to the beginning of the officer’s shift, the officer shall conduct a test recording. During the test, the officer shall state his name, id number, and the date. The officer shall note the following when starting a recording:

The BWC should vibrate once, say “Recording” and the red status LED light should start flashing, indicating that the recording successfully initiated. The status LED light will continue to flash red while recording is in progress and the BWC will beep every 120 seconds as a reminder that the BWC is recording.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: After recording the required statement, the officer shall stop the recording.

The BWC should vibrate, and the red status LED light should stop flashing, indicating that the recording has stopped. The BWC will then say “Stop Recording- Categorize.” The officer will then select one of the category presets and within five seconds needs to press the center button to confirm the category. The BWC will beep two times if the video was not categorized. The uncategorized classification will be saved as a test.
RECORDING INCIDENTS
While recording an incident, officers shall:
Ensure the BWC is recording until the incident is complete, except as noted in 3.3 of this section.
Inform those who ask that the audio/video recording equipment is actively recording.

When entering a private home or building where consent of the owner or person with authority to consent to the entrance is required and that person expressly declines to permit video and/or audio recording inside the home or building, the officer shall terminate the recording. Depending on the circumstances, the officer may request the citizen to step outside if they wish to continue the recording

This will NOT apply when consent to enter the private home or building is not required, or when it is no longer required once inside the home/building. This includes entrances related to a search warrant, arrest warrant, domestic violence calls, and emergency or exigent circumstances.

In the event that a recording is suspended, terminated, or interrupted prior to the conclusion of an incident, the officer shall record the reason on the BWC before deactivation and, if a report is generated for the incident, the reason shall also be documented in the narrative of the report.
Moved to Directive 401.26/1.3.1 GENERAL GUIDELINES.
Immediately contact a supervisor when experiencing recording problems, or when the body camera is full.

Requests for deletion of portions of a recording (i.e., an accidental personal recording) must be submitted on a REQUEST FOR VIDEO DELETION FORM (TPD FORM 23.28) and approved by the chief of police or his designee in accordance with state record retention laws. All requests and final decisions shall be kept on file.
RECORDING INCIDENTS; TRANSPORTS
When transporting detainees or citizens and the In-Car Camera System is unavailable for any reason, the BWC shall be activated.
Officers may activate their BWC in addition to the In-Car Camera if they so choose.

Once the officer has reached their destination with the detainee or citizen, the officer shall activate the BWC and record the citizen’s or detainee’s release from the vehicle or wagon and the escort of the citizen or detainee to the final point of destination, detention, or medical treatment.
RECORDING INCIDENTS; RESTRICTIONS
BWCs shall only be used in conjunction with official law enforcement duties. The BWC camera shall not generally be used to record:
Communications with other police personnel or duties outside of official law enforcement business, unless permission has been granted by the chief of police.
Encounters with undercover officers or confidential informants.
In any location where individuals have a reasonable expectation of privacy (i.e., restroom, locker room, etc.).
Removed
Once officers have entered Lucas County Corrections Center, after securing their weapons.

An investigator, regardless of rank, can request that BWCs be turned off so as not to jeopardize an investigation. The BWC shall be turned back on, if required, once the reason for the request has concluded. A detailed supplemental report must be completed by the investigator explaining why the request was made.
RECORDING INCIDENTS; EXCEPTIONS

Officer safety and the furtherance of police-community relationships are paramount. If there is a question of when to record, officers should record. However, officers are allowed some discretion with regard to recording encounters.
Situations in which activating the camera would be unsafe, impossible, or impractical. A description of the reason why the body camera was not activated shall be recorded on any generated report.
Informal, non-law enforcement related interactions with members of the community (i.e. a citizen asking for directions or just having a chat with a citizen).
If an informal interaction with a citizen begins to escalate, the officer shall activate the body camera if able to do so safely.
POST RECORDING
When an incident has concluded, the BWC should be deactivated.
If a report for an incident is generated and the BWC recorded the incident, the narrative portion of the report shall document BWC usage.
If a traffic stop is conducted and a citation issued, and the BWC recorded the incident, the usage of the BWC shall be documented in the affidavit portion inside the citation.
If a suspect stop is conducted and the BWC recorded the incident, the usage of the body camera shall be documented in the comments section of the FIELD INTERVIEW REPORT (TPD FORM 57.1).
Removed
END OF SHIFT
At the end of an officer’s shift, the officer shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Ensure that their BWC is charged, turned on and docked to ensure all video may be downloaded, and ready for the next workday.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Removed
CLASSIFICATION OF VIDEO

The video from the BWC shall be classified for the purpose of record retention and ease of locating. Officers shall categorize the BWC video recording at the end of an incident. BWC recordings, by default, are classified as uncategorized and will be saved as a test video. The BWC recording shall be classified by selecting from the following:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Traffic Stop

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Arrest/Evidence

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Removed

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Suspect

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Transport

blocks.label: (f)
blocks.text: Test
SUPERVISORS; RESPONSIBILITIES
DAMAGE TO BODY WORN VIDEO CAMERAS

The supervisor shall document all problems with the BWC via a Help Desk Ticket on the TPD Intranet. This report shall be completed immediately and contain the details of the problem, the name of the officer reporting the problem, and the date/time it was reported.

In the event that the BWC was damaged, an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0) shall also be completed by the referring supervisor. This report shall be completed immediately and contain the details of the damage, the names of the officers reporting the damage, and the date/time it was reported. The Unusual Incident report shall be forwarded to the Technical Services Unit commander, the district commander and the Support and Administrative Services Division commander.

Any BWC lost, while in the officer’s possession shall fall under Department Manual 303.2/6.3 OFFICIAL EQUIPMENT; LOST, DAMAGED, OR STOLEN. Officers shall be personally responsible for the care and security of their BWC. If an officer’s issued BWC suffers irreparable harm, is stolen, or is lost due to the officer’s negligence, the officer shall pay the replacement cost of the equipment. Additionally, if negligence is found, the officer could face disciplinary action.
PURSUITS
All BWC recordings shall be reviewed and utilized as part of any vehicle pursuit investigation.
Supervisors shall document in the narrative of the VEHICLE PURSUIT FORM in the management system if a BWC was activated during the incident as required.
Officers shall categorize pursuits as Arrest/Evidence. Supervisors will need to change the category from Arrest/Evidence to Pursuits when they review the video in the GETAC viewer.
RESPONSE TO RESISTANCE
All BWC recordings shall be reviewed and utilized as part of any action response investigation for report accuracy.
CRITICAL INCIDENTS

If an officer is involved in a critical incident, the supervisor shall take possession of the BWC as soon as practical, ensure it is uploaded to the server, classify it as Arrest/Evidence, and document it in a supplemental report.
ACCIDENT SCENES
All accident scenes shall initially be classified as “Traffic Stop”.
When it is determined that a recorded incident may be of evidentiary value, officers shall log into the Getac Viewer and classify the video as “Arrest/Evidence.”
DOCKING/UPLOADING
At the end of an officer’s shift, the officers shall ensure that their BWC is placed in the docking cradle for video uploading.

If an officer is involved in a critical incident (use of force, pursuit, officer involved shooting, etc.) a supervisor shall ensure that every involved officer’s BWC is placed in the docking cradle for video uploading prior to the end of their shift.
Combined with Directive 401.26/10.7 SUPERVISORY REVIEW – COMPLIANCE WITH POLICY AND PROCEDURES.
SUPERVISORY REVIEW - COMPLIANCE WITH POLICY AND PROCEDURES
Supervisors are permitted to review footage to ensure compliance with the BWC policy and procedures. This includes, but is not limited to the following:
When officers are the subject of a complaint or a pattern of allegations of misconduct.
Evidence/Investigatory in nature
Training issues
Public records requests
When officers are in their probationary period or with a field training officer

As a condition of an Early Intervention System (EIS) Plan of Action the review shall be documented on the monthly EARLY INTERVENTION SYSTEM STATUS REPORT (TPD FORM 12.60) (See Directive 103.11/7.2.1 PLAN OF ACTION AND SPECIAL PROVISIONS) and on the VIDEO REVIEW LOG (TPD FORM 23.29).
Removed
QUARTERLY AUDITS BY ACCREDITATION UNIT

A supervisor from the Accreditation Unit shall randomly review a minimum of five recordings quarterly to ensure compliance with departmental policies and procedures. The review shall be recorded on the VIDEO REVIEW LOG and stored in the Planning, Research and Inspection Section.
EVIDENTIARY HANDLING
When a significant event is recorded on a BWC, officers shall upload the BWC as soon as practicable.
When it is determined that a recorded incident may be of evidentiary value, officers shall log into the Getac Viewer and classify the video as “Arrest/Evidence.”
Removed
Removed

DVD video transfers shall be requested via a TOLEDO POLICE VIDEO OFFICE WORK ORDER (TPD FORM 31.13), and shall include the incident’s date, time, and involved officer(s). The form shall then be forwarded to the Video Unit for processing.

Unauthorized copying of any video segment from a BWC is prohibited. The Video Office shall perform all video analysis and/or duplication services. Requests for all video analysis and/or duplication services shall be made by utilizing the TOLEDO POLICE VIDEO OFFICE WORK ORDER.
MAINTENANCE; SECURITY
Digital recordings shall be retained according to the Records Retention Schedule.
Officer access to BWC recordings shall be obtained through the GETAC logon icon located on the TPD Intranet. Officers shall use their user name and password for access to the GETAC video system.

summary: Revised in October 2026, so read this version, not what you remember. The rule of thumb the directive gives you is: **if there is a question of when to record, record.** The camera goes on for every traffic stop, every pedestrian investigative stop, every dispatched call with a citizen contact, every on-view enforcement or major incident, every suspect or witness statement, and every foot or vehicle pursuit. That applies to every officer who arrives on scene, dispatched or not, whenever they arrive.

The one consent-based exception: if you need the occupant's consent to be inside a home or building and they expressly refuse to be recorded, you stop recording. That exception disappears when consent is not required: search or arrest warrant, domestic violence calls, emergency or exigent entry.
must: Wear your issued BWC at all times on duty and on off-duty law enforcement work; if you have no camera, sign one out at Central or Scott Park before an off-duty project and return it immediately after (1.2, 1.2.1)

Record all motor vehicle stops, pedestrian investigative stops, dispatched calls involving citizen interaction, on-view enforcement and major incidents, suspect and witness statements, and foot and vehicle pursuits, regardless of when you arrive or whether you were dispatched (1.3, 1.3.1)
Keep recording until the incident is complete (3.1)
Tell people who ask that you are recording audio and video (3.2)
If you stop, suspend or interrupt a recording before the incident ends, state the reason on camera before deactivating and put it in the report narrative (3.4)
Record when a recording was not activated and why on any report generated (6.1)
Activate the BWC during transports when the in-car camera is unavailable, and in every case record the release from the vehicle and the escort to the final destination (4.1, 4.2.1)
Start of shift: inspect for damage, mount on the outermost garment at or slightly above the shirt pockets, and do a test recording stating your name, ID number and date, then categorize it (2)

Categorize every recording at the end of the incident (Traffic Stop, Arrest/Evidence, Suspect, Transport, Test); uncategorized video is saved as a test. Pursuits are categorized Arrest/Evidence; accident scenes start as Traffic Stop and are reclassified Arrest/Evidence if they have evidentiary value (9, 10.2.3, 10.5)
Document BWC use in the report narrative, in the affidavit section of a citation, or in the comments of a Field Interview Report (7.1 to 7.3)
Contact a supervisor immediately for recording problems or a full camera (3.6)
End of shift: charged, powered on, and docked so video uploads (8, 10.6.1)
Upload significant events as soon as practicable and classify them Arrest/Evidence in the Getac Viewer (11, 11.1)
If an informal chat with a citizen starts to escalate, turn the camera on if you can safely do so (6.3)
never: Wear a camera that is not department issued; everything the camera captures belongs to the department (1.6)
Show or release any recording to an outside person or entity without the chief's prior approval or a public records request handled under 302.1 (1.9)

View recordings for anything other than official purposes: reports, court prep, training, ongoing investigation, assigned redaction work. Another officer's video requires a supervisor's permission (1.8)
Copy any video segment yourself; the Video Office does all duplication and analysis, requested on a Video Office Work Order (TPD 31.13) (11.5)

Record conversations with other officers or non-law-enforcement business without the chief's permission, encounters with undercover officers or confidential informants, places with a reasonable expectation of privacy such as restrooms and locker rooms, or inside LCCC after securing your weapon (5)
Delete anything on your own; accidental personal recordings go through a Request for Video Deletion Form (TPD 23.28) approved by the chief or designee (3.7)

Recordings are public records subject to the Records Retention Schedule and to the department's video fee policy (1.7, 12.1)

blocks.text: Policy
It is the policy of the Toledo Police Department to recover stolen property and prosecute offenders through the joint cooperation of the police department and pawnbrokers or secondhand dealers.
Definitions
For purposes of this order shall mean pawnbroker, secondhand dealer, antiques dealer, or consignment dealer.

A person, corporation, or firm engaged in the business of lending money on deposit or pledges of personal property, other than securities, printed evidence of indebtedness, titles, deeds, or bills of sale, at a total charge, rate of interest, or discount or other remuneration in excess of eight per cent per annum, and includes a person engaged in the business of purchasing personal property from another person with an agreement that the personal property will be made available to that other person for repurchase within an agreed-to time period and for an amount greater than the price originally paid to that other person for the purchase of the personal property.

Any person, society, firm, club, partnership, organization or corporation that sells or purchases for the purpose of resale, second-hand articles. "Second-hand dealer" includes the sale of goods on consignment and the sale of second- hand goods in combination with the sale of new merchandise.

Any person, firm or corporation engaged in the business of buying for resale, trade, or transfer of personal property having special value because of its age, including but not limited to, paintings, clothing, furniture, glass, ceramics, rugs, silverware, carvings, sculpture and other movable personal property.

Any person, firm or corporation receiving consignment goods for the purpose of selling consignment goods which include all categories of movable personal property as enumerated in the Antique and Secondhand Dealer definitions.
Procedures
DEALERS
When officers respond to dealer’s shop, it is often while investigating alleged stolen property having been located at the store. Often, this property is related to different types of investigations.
If the alleged victim is on scene, officers shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Speak with the alleged victim and attempt to determine the circumstances under which the property was originally stolen.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Verbally advise the employee(s) of the shop to hold the property in question for follow-up by the Investigations Bureau.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Document the victim’s statements in an original crime report, if one has not already been made, or in a supplemental report to the original.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Document the date, time, location, property, and the specific employee(s) who were advised.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Document all identifiable characteristics of the property (i.e. serial and model numbers). Take photos if practical.

blocks.label: (g)
blocks.text: Forward the report to the Investigations Bureau. Unless the property involves a Crimes Against Persons investigation, the Property Recovery Unit shall follow-up with the investigation.
If the alleged victim is not on scene, officers shall:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: Verbally advise the employee(s) of the shop to hold the property in question for follow-up by the Investigations Bureau.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: On a SERGEANT’S REPORT (TPD 20.7); document the date, time, location, property, and the specific employee(s) who were advised.

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Document all identifiable characteristics of the property (i.e. serial and model numbers).

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Document any information about the alleged victim that is known.

blocks.label: (e)
blocks.text: Forward the SERGEANT’S REPORT to the Investigations Bureau, Property Recovery Unit.
In no instance shall the officer seize the property and/or return it to the alleged victim/owner. Officers shall not threaten to or file criminal charges against the dealer, or any employees thereof.
Policy

As a part of our commitment to the preservation of life, our department has an obligation to provide first aid to the public in the absence of medical personnel. Narcan is the name given to the generic drug Naloxone. Naloxone is used for the complete or partial reversal of opiate-induced overdoses. Naloxone has been shown to be safer than aspirin, and unlike aspirin, there have been no reported deaths from the use of Naloxone. Naloxone can be administered by several methods (e.g., intramuscular, intranasal, intravenous). The Toledo Police Department will administer Naloxone by the intranasal method (i.e., Nasal Narcan). Existing law holds the officer, as well as the department, blameless from any harm determined to be the result of the use of Naloxone (Nasal Narcan), as long as a medical response team has been summoned. It is the policy of this department for trained officers to administer Naloxone (Nasal Narcan) to persons believed to be suffering from opioid overdoses, as soon as practicable, to minimize overdosing effects in accordance with law and department policy.
Definitions
Generic drug which is also know under the trade names of Narcan and Evzio. The half-life of Naloxone is relatively brief (as short as 30 minutes which is shorter than the half-life of opiates).
Intranasal method of administering Naloxone used by Toledo Police Department personnel.
Procedures
TRAINING
Only officers that have been trained shall be authorized to administer Naloxone (Nasal Narcan).
INDICATIONS AND USE
INDICATIONS
Nasal Narcan shall only be used on subjects believed to be suffering from an opioid overdose. Symptoms indicating that a subject is suffering from an opioid overdose, include, but are not limited to:
Blood-shot eyes
Pinpoint pupils, even in a darkened room/area
Depressed or slow respiratory rate
Difficulty breathing (labored breathing, shallow breaths)
Blue skin, lips, or fingernails
Decreased pulse rate
Low blood pressure
Loss of alertness (drowsiness)
Unresponsive
Seizures
Evidence of ingestion, inhalation, or injection (needles, spoons, tourniquets, needle tracks, etc.)
Past history of opioid use/abuse
USE When an officer suspects a person is suffering from an opioid overdose, officers shall:
Notify Communications that the patient is in a potential overdose state and request a Life Squad and a Toledo Fire and Rescue first responder.
Maintain universal precautions against the transfer of blood of other body fluid, perform a patient assessment, and determine unresponsiveness.
If use of the Nasal Narcan kit is warranted, follow all protocols outlined in the Nasal Narcan training.
Notify Communications immediately after administering Nasal Narcan to create a recorded time when the dose was administered.
To the best of the officer’s ability, monitor the patient for recurrent symptoms (altered mental status, respiratory depression, circulatory compromise)
To the best of the officer’s ability, report the observed signs and symptoms and all other relevant information about the patient to the responding Emergency Medical Services (EMS) personnel.
Officers shall give the entire used Nasal Narcan kit to the transporting Life Squad.
MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT
MAINTENANCE
The shelf life of Narcan is approximately 2 years and should be kept out of direct sunlight at temperatures between 59 and 86°F.
Nasal Narcan kits shall be issued by the equipment sergeant to trained officers at the beginning of the shift.
It shall be the responsibility of the officer to inspect the kit, prior to each shift
Any Nasal Narcan kit found to be expired or contain missing/damaged required equipment shall be returned to the equipment sergeant for replacement.
Due to the sensitivity of temperature fluctuations, at no time, shall any Nasal Narcan kit be stored inside the trunk of any vehicle.
Nasal Narcan kits shall be returned to the equipment sergeant at the end of an officer’s shift.
REPLACEMENT
The Property Management Unit shall maintain a stock of Nasal Narcan kits
The Day Shift Watch Commander shall be responsible to maintain a stock of Nasal Narcan kits available for trained officers.
If Nasal Narcan kits are needed, they shall be obtained from the Property Management Unit.
REPORTING REQUIREMENTS
A Crime Report (TPD Form 38.1) entitled “Overdose” shall be required in all cases when a Nasal Narcan kit is used.
A Records Section number shall be obtained and recorded on the report.
The State of Ohio shall be the victim.
The patient shall be listed as the suspect.
Officers shall document the indicators that the patient exhibited that led the officer to believe the patient was suffering from an opioid overdose.
Officers shall document which Life Squad arrived to the scene.
Officers shall document which hospital the patient was transported to.
Officers shall document if the Narcan Nasal kit was deployed and if it was successful (to the extent possible).
Officers while at the scene of an overdose (both fatal and nonfatal) shall attempt to contact the Vice Narcotics Section.
Officers shall contact the Persons Section for fatal overdoses or when contact with the Vice Narcotics Section cannot be made. Officers shall log fatal overdoses with the Persons Section.
All reports shall be forwarded to the Vice Narcotics Section prior to the completion of the officer’s tour of duty.
Purpose
