If, however, the circumstances are such that the hostage faces an immediate threat of loss of life, immediate intervention on the part of officers is warranted.
OFFICERS SHALL:
Assume the role of Incident Commander until relieved by proper authority.
Advise the dispatcher of the incident and provide all pertinent information.
Ensure a supervisor has been advised of the incident.
Ensure that the evacuation of injured persons is conducted based upon tactical considerations.
Advise responders of safe avenues of approach and where to report.

Attempt to obtain as much information as possible about the incident (e.g., the exact location and number of suspects, hostages, and victims, weapons, hazards to backup officers, crimes committed, etc.) and continually update the dispatcher.

Contain and isolate the incident scene through the establishment of an inner perimeter to cover all exits. The inner perimeter should provide a reasonable degree of safety while maintaining contact with the incident scene.
As time and resources permit, establish an outer perimeter and control pedestrian and vehicular traffic around the area.
Escort to safety and detain potential witnesses and/or bystanders.
Not release any information regarding the event or persons involved unless authorized by the Incident Commander.
COMMAND OFFICER/INCIDENT COMMANDER RESPONSIBILITIES
The sergeant responsible for the area shall immediately respond to the scene.
Upon arrival, a command officer will take overall command of the scene, evaluate the circumstances, and assume the duties of the Incident Commander. The Incident Commander shall:
Ensure a command post is established and notify the dispatcher of the location.
Ensure the evacuation of injured persons is conducted based upon tactical consideration.
Ensure other arriving officers are briefed.

Ensure through the dispatcher that SWAT personnel, the Critical Incident Negotiator Team Commander and three trained critical incident negotiators are summoned to the scene. Dispatch will look for on-duty personnel first. If not enough negotiators are available, dispatch will then send out an Everbridge alert message.
Specially trained personnel (e.g., SWAT, critical incident negotiators, bomb squad, canine, etc.) are assets available to the Incident Commander.
Arrange for relief of the first officer on the scene so they can be debriefed.
Ensure establishment of an inner and outer perimeter.
Request a Life Squad from the Toledo Fire and Rescue Department to stand by and ensure that a safe route for their arrival has been designated.
Whenever practical, evacuate occupants of the affected residences or facilities, as well as adjoining structures as deemed necessary.
Ensure that crowd control and control of vehicular traffic have been established.
If necessary, request that the dispatcher establish a tactical channel for the incident.
Ensure an officer is assigned the duty of maintaining a chronological log of actions and assignments.

Summon any other units or equipment such as canine, Northwest Ohio Bomb Squad, and/or public utilities, relief officers, etc. as necessary. Communications personnel shall determine the method of communicating with other agencies. Communications with other city services can be accomplished by dispatch notifying the requested representative and asking that they report to the command post. Ensure all affected command personnel are informed of major developments.

Designate an area for a media center and an officer to act as Public Information Officer (PIO). Since the suspect may have access to a radio or television, the media must be advised of the danger posed by ill-thought news coverage.
At the conclusion of the incident, ensure:
The crime scene is secured until properly relieved by investigators.
All personnel utilized are accounted for.
A damage assessment of Department equipment is conducted.
All equipment is returned to pre-response state of readiness.
SWAT COMMANDER RESPONSIBILITIES
The SWAT Commander, upon being summoned to the scene, shall be responsible for supervising the efforts of the tactical response team. The SWAT Commander shall:
Report to the Incident Commander and coordinate tactical team response.
Establish a tactical operations center, if necessary.
Assume responsibility for the inner perimeter if special weapons and tactics are required and manpower permits. Deploy an arrest team on the inner perimeter if necessary.
Ensure firearms discipline is maintained during all tactical operations.
Supervise the tactical response team’s preparation and tactical plans.
Formulate, review, and recommend tactical response alternatives to the Incident Commander.
Keep the Incident Commander informed of all developments and operations.
If tactical intervention is required:
Assume responsibility for the tactical intervention and all tactical response assets.
CRITICAL INCIDENT NEGOTIATIONS TEAM RESPONSIBILITIES
The critical incident negotiation team shall consist of the unit commander and three (3) negotiators.

If an officer already on scene has established communication and rapport with the suspect prior to the arrival of the trained critical incident negotiator, then the officer shall negotiate with the suspect, under the direction of the primary negotiator. The officer shall not be relieved unless the situation warrants it.
The primary critical incident negotiator shall ensure:

blocks.label: (a)
blocks.text: He identifies himself and asks if medical attention is needed.

blocks.label: (b)
blocks.text: Attempts to obtain all pertinent information about the hostage taker or barricaded suspect (e.g., description, motives, weapons, physical and mental state, crimes committed, drug or alcohol consumption), hostage (e.g., identity, physical condition), and the site (e.g., layout).

blocks.label: (c)
blocks.text: Attempts to negotiate with the suspect to resolve the incident in a peaceful manner.

blocks.label: (d)
blocks.text: Provides real-time intelligence and coordinates the negotiation strategy with the Incident Commander and the Tactical Operations Team Commander.
NON-NEGOTIABLE ITEMS
The decision as to what is negotiable is up to the Incident Commander; however, there are some demands that are non-negotiable. They include:
No hostage shall be removed from the scene.
No officer shall be exchanged for a hostage.
No weapons shall be supplied.
No release of a prisoner in custody in this or any other jurisdiction, nor agreement to transmit such a demand.
No deadlines shall be accepted.
No alcohol or drugs shall be supplied.
AFTER-ACTION REPORTS

The Incident Commander, Tactical Operations Team Commander, and Critical Incident Negotiation team shall submit an after-action report, through their appropriate chain of command, as soon as practical after the conclusion of the incident. See Directive 104.1/6 – AFTER-ACTION REPORT.
Policy

In all incidents involving explosives, the protection of human life will dictate the exact procedure to be followed in a given situation. Use of a specialized unit trained in the handling, disposal and investigation of such incidents is mandatory to help ensure the safety of all persons concern.
Procedures
INVESTIGATIONS INVOLVING HAZARDOUS DEVICES
When a dangerous explosive device or suspected explosive device is located by on-scene officers, their supervisor and the Toledo Police Department Northwest Ohio Bomb Squad (NOBS) shall be notified.

Officers at the scene shall NOT attempt to touch, move or disarm the device. It shall be kept in mind that some devices can be detonated by electronic transmission, e.g., radios, cell phones, pagers, computers, etc.; therefore, NO transmitters shall be activated within 300 feet of the device.

Other situations under which the NOBS should be contacted shall be left to the discretion of the on-scene commander; however, if there is any doubt, the NOBS should be called using the following guidelines:

The Incident Commander (IC) at the scene shall immediately notify the Communications supervisor, either by phone or radio to make notification that the presence of the NOBS is required. Communications supervisor shall:
Notify an on-duty member of the NOBS.
If no member of the NOBS is on duty, the on-call NOBS member shall be notified.
If the on-call member can not be contacted, the NOBS Commander shall be notified.
After the NOBS is notified; the appropriate watch commander shall be notified and shall report to the scene.
RESPONSIBILITY OF THE INCIDENT COMMANDER (IC)
The IC at the scene shall take whatever action is necessary for the protection of life in the area.
The IC shall be responsible for the overall police response and activity at the scene. He shall lend every cooperation to the NOBS officer and utilize whatever resources are required.
The IC shall ensure that a copy of the UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0) and related reports are forwarded to the Strategic Response Bureau commander and the NOBS commander.
RESPONSIBILITY OF THE NOBS
The NOBS members at the scene shall have the final responsibility for the handling and disposal of all explosive devices and materials.
When requested to do so NOBS officers shall also assist in post-blast investigations.
REQUESTS FOR ASSISTANCE FROM OUTSIDE AGENCIES

Whenever any member of the department receives a request from an outside agency for assistance with a dangerous explosive device or material, the member shall refer the request to the Investigations Bureau desk.

The desk personnel shall obtain the name of the requesting person, agency and a telephone number where the person can be contacted. This information shall be transmitted to a NOBS officer, who shall make a decision on rendering assistance based on the NOBS Procedure Manual.
Policy

The following section was developed to provide general guidelines to officers responding to hazardous material (HAZMAT) incidents. The purpose of the guidelines is to provide effective direction, control and coordination among safety department personnel responding to HAZMAT incidents.
Procedures
FIRST RESPONSE
The first arriving unit on the scene shall make an assessment to determine whether or not a HAZMAT incident exists.
When approaching a suspected HAZMAT incident, the first unit should:
Approach the scene from the upwind side.
Identify the material from a safe distance.
Convey essential information to Communications and other units responding.
The first officer on the scene shall be responsible for directing police operations until properly relieved.

As soon as practical, secure the site of the incident and await the arrival of properly trained and equipped personnel of the Toledo Fire & Rescue Department's HAZMAT Team. NOTE: Personnel shall not be assigned to areas for which they do no not have proper training, protective clothing or equipment to operate within reasonable safety.
HAZMAT INCIDENT COMMANDER

The ranking fire department command officer on the scene of a HAZMAT incident shall assume command of the scene and shall act as the Incident Commander. The Incident Commander shall direct all on-scene operations, as well as, coordinate the efforts of all responding agencies involved in on-site emergency operations. The Incident Commander shall exercise command and control through the various supervisors of each respective agency.
HAZMAT DUTIES
In addition to law enforcement activities, the following is a list of duties that department officers may be called upon to perform at the scene of a HAZMAT incident:
At the direction of the Incident Commander, establish a perimeter around the site of the incident.
Conduct an evacuation of an area at risk, as determined by the Incident Commander.
Maintain security within the area of operations.
Establish and maintain emergency traffic control operations.
Assist in the removal and identification of deceased persons.
Establish a liaison with Red Cross authorities and assist with emergency shelter operations.
Supplement Fire Department communication capabilities.
Conduct investigations and complete all reports required by circumstance, law and Toledo Police Department policy.
Policy

Mutual aid between police agencies in Ohio is controlled by the Ohio Revised Code (ORC). Section 737.04 of the ORC delineates guidelines and requirements for mutual aid agreements between police agencies.
Procedures
COOPERATION WITH OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES

The department will maintain a close working relationship with other law enforcement agencies and make available to them information concerning techniques and procedures developed or used by the department.
RESPONSE OUTSIDE CITY – LIFE-THREATENING SITUATIONS

When a life-threatening situation is occurring in one of the jurisdictions bordering the city of Toledo, and a Toledo Police Department unit is the nearest police assistance, they shall respond to render assistance, stabilize the situation, and/or hold the status quo until police assistance from the jurisdiction involved arrives.

Dispatch of a Toledo Police unit shall ONLY occur with the approval of the on-duty shift supervisor in Communications. In other than life-threatening situations, no Toledo Police unit shall enter another jurisdiction without the prior approval of the Communications shift supervisor or an Operations command officer. Approval shall be based upon the information available at the time.

Whenever any officer of the department is dispatched or given approval to respond to an incident in another jurisdiction, a command officer shall also be dispatched to supervise Toledo officers and to complete an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0) listing details of the incident and the department's role. Communications shall also notify the affected on-duty watch commander about the incident.
RESPONSE OUTSIDE CITY – NOTIFICATION TO OTHER JURISDICTION

In all situations where Toledo Police officers have been sent into another jurisdiction to render aid and the request for assistance did not originate with the authority involved, the Communication shift supervisor shall ensure the jurisdiction involved is notified of the following:
That Toledo Police officers have been dispatched into their jurisdiction
The location from which Toledo Police officers are responding
The reason for the dispatch
All available information about the incident occurring
Request jurisdictional units be sent to assume primary responsibility for the situation
REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE – OUTSIDE JURISDICTION
Whenever the Toledo Police Department receives a request for assistance from the following:
City of Bowling Green
City of Maumee
City of Northwood
City of Oregon
City of Perrysburg
Perrysburg Township
City of Rossford
City of Sylvania
Sylvania Township
Lake Township
Washington Township
Village of Ottawa Hills
City of Walbridge
Village of Whitehouse
City of Waterville
University of Toledo
Metro Park Rangers (Toledo Area)

Policy

The policy of the Toledo Police Department is to protect Life. The goal for police response, in Active Threat incidents, is to disrupt the on-going threat by: denying the Active Shooter(s)/Threat’s access to additional victims, rescuing injured personnel, and extracting potential victims. Immediate intervention, by responding officers, is critical. The implementation of contact, rescue, and containment teams is important to save lives, prevent serious injury, and stop the on-going threat. Active Threat incidents are sufficiently unique, such that their effective handling cannot be reduced to rigid procedures. This protocol shall be used as a guideline, to the extent possible and practical, in a crisis situation. Active Threat response tactics are not a substitute for conventional response tactics, to a violent barricaded individual, or hostage situation.
Definitions

An armed person or persons who has used deadly physical force, or has threatened such use on other persons, and continues to do so while having access to additional victims. The means by which the Active Threat is deploying his/her deadly force is not limited to firearms. The mere fact that innocent civilians are being subjected to deadly force requires the same level of response, as if they were being subjected to gunfire. QUAD - Quick Action Deployment addresses the requirement to respond, immediately, to an Active Threat Incident, with a focus on tactical team movement, while implementing a push to contact, or a search formation that officers can employ, with minimal training. SINGLE OFFICER RESPONSE – Concept that the first officer responding to an Active Threat Incident isolates, distracts, and ends the threat, when an active threat is engaged.
Procedures
INCIDENT PRIORITIES
a) Stop the active threat b) Rescue the victims c) Provide medical aid d) Preserve the crime scene
RESPONSIBILITIES
RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE FIRST OFFICER ON SCENE

The first officer on-scene should assess, to the extent possible and practical, whether or not his/her immediate entry would lessen the toll of casualties, or if by making a single officer entry, he/she would expose additional responding officers to further risk.
If circumstances allow, wait for additional officers to arrive on scene for Quick Action Deployment (QUAD).

Prior to making entry, officers shall notify the dispatcher that entry is being made, as well as the specific location of the entry. In the event of a Single Officer Response, the officer shall notify dispatch of their entry location, before entering, to assist in linking up with additional officers, as they arrive on scene.
Until the threat is located and disrupted, do not administer first aid, or assist with evacuation.
Note the location of victims, for later notification to dispatch.
Note the locations of suspicious devices, move past, and continue to threat. Leave all doors open, and do not utilize police radios, if a suspicious device is located.
Any guns encountered during the search should be rendered safe, secured by the officer, and their location should be noted, for evidentiary purposes.
Locate and engage, to disrupt the threat.
If a suspect is apprehended, always handcuff and leave a team member with the suspect, while other team members continue.
RESPONSIBILITIES OF ADDITIONAL OFFICERS ON SCENE
Additional officers shall not enter, without first advising dispatch, and the officers inside.
Officers arriving after a Single Officer Response is initiated, should be verbally announcing their presence, when approaching the Single Officer’s last known location, and listening for a response.

Search at low ready; this allows for a wider field of view, and may prevent a startled-response shooting. Know that additional officers will be aggressively working the building, in search of the threat.
Officers should keep radio traffic to a minimum, to allow the officers inside to communicate their location.

Officers should also be prepared to identify one another, from the Toledo Police Department, as well as, other jurisdictions, when linking up, during an Active Threat Incident (i.e., information about the department, patches, or business cards).
Plainclothes officers should consider placing their badge on their person, where it can be easily seen, and identified
COMMAND OFFICER/INCIDENT COMMANDER RESPONSIBILITIES
The sergeant responsible for the area shall immediately respond to the scene.

Upon arrival (unless involved in the initial entry), a Command Officer shall evaluate all circumstances, assume the duties of the Incident Commander, and the overall command of the scene. The Incident Commander shall:
Ensure that a command post is established, and notify the dispatcher of the location.
Determine if the facility has undergone any degree of evacuation, or if it is under lockdown.
If an evacuation (to any degree) has taken place, shall attempt to gather intelligence from those evacuated, and facilitate public sheltering, if necessary.
If a lockdown has occurred prior to officer arrival, shall determine whether to order law enforcement- supervised evacuation, or leave it in lockdown mode.
Determine and orchestrate the appropriate containment of the incident, and any additional building sweeps and/or clearing needed, after responding officers have completed their initial tasks.
Ensure that all injured persons have been evacuated, based upon tactical considerations.
Ensure that arriving officers are briefed.
Ensure the establishment of an inner and outer perimeter.
Request a Life Squad from the Toledo Fire and Rescue Department to stand by, and ensure that a safe route, for their arrival, has been designated.
Whenever practical, evacuate occupants of the affected residences or facilities, as well as adjoining structures, as deemed necessary.
Ensure that crowd control, and the control of vehicular traffic has been established.
Request that dispatch establish a tactical channel on one of the OPS Talkgroups for the incident.
Ensure that an officer is assigned the duty of maintaining a chronological log of actions and assignments.

Summon other units or equipment, such as SWAT, canine, Northwest Ohio Bomb Squad, Aviation Unit, and/or public utilities, relief officers, etc., as necessary. Communications shall determine communication with other agencies and city departments for additional services or considerations.
Ensure that all affected command is informed of any major developments.

Designate an area for a media center. Contact and advise the Public Information Officer (PIO). Since the suspect may have access to radio or television, the media must be advised of the danger posed by ill-thought news coverage.
Designate a Reunification Staging Area where family or loved ones can be reunited with victims involved in the Active Threat Incident.
After the incident, the Incident Commander shall ensure that:
The crime scene is secured, until properly relieved by investigators.
All police personnel have been accounted for.
A damage assessment of department equipment is conducted.
All equipment is returned to a pre-response state of readiness.
An after-action report is completed, and submitted to the Chief of Police, through the Deputy Chief of the Operations Division. See Directive 104.1/6
AFTER ACTION REPORT.
ANNUAL ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW
The Chief of Police or designee will conduct a documented annual review of the department’s practices concerning active threats.
The review shall include, but is not limited to, department policy and procedure, statistical data, and training needs.
Policy

It is the policy of the Toledo Police Department to work with citizens in keeping both communities and citizens safe from crime associated with mass attacks and terrorism. The goal is to foil potential attacks before they can be carried out. The “See Something, Say Something” initiative encourages citizens to recognize and report individuals demonstrating warning signs indicative of a terrorism event. Some behaviors that seem suspicious may be constitutionally protected but could indicate a future intent to conduct an attack. Therefore, it is imperative that department personnel take appropriate action when recognizing or becoming aware of potential threats and acts of terrorism.
Defintions

JTTF (JOINT TERRORISM TASK FORCE) LIAISON OFFICER- To better protect citizens, the department staffs a position on a multijurisdictional task force organized to proactively combat acts of terrorism and investigate terroristic acts.

The commanding officer of the unit serves as a link to the Intelligence Liaison Officer (ILO) Program as well as the Regional Intelligence Coordinator (RIC) for the Ohio Division of Homeland Security (OHS). The commander also engages in Critical Infrastructure/Key Resources (CIKR) protection activities.

The ILO Program is designed to enhance information and intelligence sharing between law enforcement agencies and public and private sector critical infrastructure entities. Through the Ohio Fusion Center Network, the ILO recognizes, reports, and/or disseminates intelligence regarding suspicious activity. Fusion centers are able to conduct in depth analysis of open source social media outlets to determine if an individual is planning an act of mass violence.
Procedures
OFFICER RESPONSIBILITIES
REPORTING

Any officer observing or otherwise becoming aware of information (e.g., citizen tips, suspicious person trespassing on property of critical infrastructure, etc.) of possible terrorism or mass attacks, through the course of their duties shall:
Initiate a report (crime, incident, field interview report) containing as many facts as possible regarding the potential threat.
Immediately notify the on-duty Investigations Bureau (ISB) supervisor of the potential threat while remaining on-scene for further instructions.
Notify their immediate supervisor so that an Unusual Incident Report (TPD Form 40.0) can be completed.
SUPERVISOR RESPONSIBILITIES
The supervisor, after being made aware of the potential threats , shall:
Complete an Unusual Incident Report after consulting with the ISB supervisor.
Assist in the investigation as determined by ISB.
INVESTIGATIVE SERVICES SUPERVISOR RESPONSIBILITIES
The on-duty investigative supervisor, after being made aware of the potential threats, shall:
Gather all of the known facts and start a preliminary investigation.
Notify the ISB commander.
If necessary, notify the appropriate law enforcement agency (federal, state, local) of the threat and coordinate or assist in the investigation as needed.
If determined that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) should handle the threat response, notify the JTTF (Joint Terrorism Task Force) Liaison officer as soon as possible.
If appropriate, notify the target (e.g., individual, school, private business, public entity, etc.) of the potential threat.
Notify the Communications/All Hazards Liaison Unit.
Determine if the gathered intelligence needs to be disseminated via the Fusion Center Network
JTTF (JOINT TERRORISM TASK FORCE) LIAISON OFFICER RESPONSIBILITIES
If called upon to handle the investigation, coordinate with department personnel and other applicable agencies.
Determine if the gathered intelligence needs to be disseminated via the Fusion Center Network.
Policy
It is essential that the Chief of Police be informed immediately of emergencies, critical incidents and other matters that may significantly affect department operations.
Definition

An unusual incident is any incident that is, or may be, of exceptional concern to the department, or that requires major police action, or incidents of such a nature that they are potentially newsworthy.
Procedures
NOTIFICATION TO THE CHIEF
DISTRICT STATION COMMANDER’S RESPONSIBILITY

Generally, the district station commander shall make notification to the Chief of Police unless delegated to a subordinate command officer. Notification shall be made when any of the following incidents occur:
Aircraft disasters.
Multiple arrests (four or more) at a single incident or the arrest of an elected official, public official, prominent person or city employee.
Bar incidents that involve guns or result in serious injury.
Barricaded/hostage incidents.
Only burglaries which are extraordinary.
Major disasters (flood, tornado, etc.)
Large drug and/or cash seizures.
Activation of Emergency Alert System (flood, tornado, etc.).
Implementation of Emergency Call-Back Plan.
Large-scale evacuations.
All fatal accidents.
Felonious assaults resulting in serious or critical injury.
Discharge of firearms, including accidental discharges, police personnel being fired upon, etc., however, excluding dog shootings.
Major fires and those resulting in death.
All homicides.
Injured officers; serious on-duty injury – immediate notification; serious offduty injury – notify as soon as possible.

Allegations of personnel misconduct involving: drugs, alcohol, unscheduled drug testing, criminal conduct, excessive force involving serious injury, video/audio taped evidence, slow police response, or extraordinary incidents.
Mutual aid requests from outside agencies.
Pursuits resulting in an injury accident or where there is an obvious and serious violation of the policy.
All rapes, unless involving a “known suspect” or date rape situation.
Riots.
Robberies in the downtown business district and those which are extraordinary in nature.
School incidents involving a gun, hit list, etc., that result in injuries or extraordinary in nature.
Suicides, if deceased was a ‘prominent’ person or under 18 yrs. of age.
Any unusual occurrence that may generate a lot of media attention (large civil disorders, gangs, racial disorders, etc.).
If there is a major occurrence other than those listed above, the district station commander shall determine whether immediate notification is appropriate.

If an incident requiring the notifications listed above directly involves a department employee not assigned to the Operations Division, it shall be the responsibility of the Operations Division commander to notify the employee’s division commander.
SUPERVISOR’S RESPONSIBILITY
A supervisor of the appropriate rank shall respond to the scene and prepare an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT (TPD FORM 40.0), when any of the above-listed situations or below-listed incidents occur:
Accidents involving police officers, on or off duty; large expressway accidents; and other accidents involving major or unusual circumstances.
Allegations of the use of excessive force not involving serious injury.
Since it is impossible to compile an all-inclusive list of exactly what types of incidents would qualify as being ‘unusual,’ supervisors shall not limit their reports to just those incidents listed.
If a question should arise as to whether an UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT should be filed, the supervisor shall seek the advice of a superior officer.
ROUTING OF UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORTS
The original report and a copy of any related reports (note the exception below) shall be reviewed and approved by a supervisor and forwarded through the chain of command to the division commander.
A photocopy of the UNUSUAL INCIDENT REPORT, along with a copy of any related reports, shall be forwarded to the Personnel Section and the Chief of Police without delay.
EXCEPTION: No copies of the USE OF FIREARMS REPORT (TPD FORM 7.1) are to be attached to the unusual incident report.
Policy

The preplanning of special events is critical to the efficient and effective handling of such incidents. The department shall respond to these events with sufficient resources and in accordance with the procedures contained in this Standard Operating Guideline.
Procedures
TYPES OF SPECIAL EVENTS
Special events include but are not limited to parades, fireworks displays, strikes, major demonstrations, entertainment events and major sporting events.
SPECIAL EVENT PLAN
When the Operations Division commander determines the scope of an event is of such magnitude that an event coordinator is required, he shall designate one.
The specified person assigned to coordinate an event shall ensure that a written plan is developed.
The plan shall be submitted for review and approval to the Operations Division commander at least five workdays prior to the event, if time permits.
Prior to the event, a copy of the approved plan shall be returned to the event coordinator and/or the person supervising the event.
The plan shall include, at a minimum, the following:
Written estimate of traffic, crowd control, and crime problems expected.
Contingency plan for traffic direction and control (ingress and egress of vehicles, alternate traffic routes, parking, emergency vehicle access, etc.).
Use of Special Enforcement personnel, if applicable.
Logistical requirements (number of officers needed, relief of officers, barricades, mobile command post, radios, vehicles, etc.).
Coordination with other department components or outside agencies involved in handling the incident (e.g., Traffic Section, news media, emergency medical services, etc.).
AFTER-ACTION REPORT

The event commander, after consultation with the affected district commander, shall submit an after-action report to the Operations Division commander, within ten workdays after the conclusion of the incident. See Directive 104.1/5 – AFTER ACTION REPORT.
